title: Tanner McKee: I'm ready to make the most of "huge opportunity"
summary: Tanner McKee fell to No. 3 on the depth chart ahead of Week 1 this season, but he worked his way back to the No. 2 job in time to be the next man up when the Eagles made a surprising announcement on Thursday.
full_text: ' Tanner McKee fell to No. 3 on the depth chart ahead of Week 1 this season, but he worked his way back to the No. 2 job in time to be the next man up when the Eagles made a surprising announcement on Thursday. Jalen Hurts will not play against the Panthers in Week 6 because of a blood clot in his calf and it is unclear when he will be cleared to return to action. That positions the 2023 sixth-round pick to make his first start outside of a pair of throwaway Week 18 games after the Eagles had already clinched their postseason spot. On Thursday, McKee said the backup mindset is to be ready at a moment's notice so it's a positive that he will get practice time with the first team heading into his chance to make a strong impression on the Eagles and the entire league this Sunday. "Every opportunity that you get to play is a huge opportunity , especially being a sixth-round pick," McKee said. "Every opportunity is a huge opportunity. I'm obviously very excited and ready to make the most of it." The Eagles have a lot of injury issues beyond the one that's knocked Hurts out of action, so it's not an ideal situation for a backup to come in and shine but it's the chance that McKee gets and we'll see what he can do with it on Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bo Nix: I don't know where the disconnect is offensively
summary: The point of playing football games is to win football games and the Broncos were able to do that against the Seahawks on Thursday night, but the result didn't shield their quarterback Bo Nix from some harsh criticism after the game.
full_text: The point of playing football games is to win football games and the Broncos were able to do that against the Seahawks on Thursday night, but the result didn't shield their quarterback Bo Nix from some harsh criticism after the game. During the Prime Video postgame show, former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick called Nix's performance in the 17-14 overtime victory " garbage ." The Broncos picked up 153 yards on a pair of early touchdown drives that staked them to a 14-0 lead, but they only picked up two first downs over the rest of the night while punting seven times and the futility allowed the Seahawks to send the game to overtime. Nix finished 17-of-27 for 107 yards and the team's longest pass play went for 16 yards, which he said after the game was not part of a design to be overly conservative and that he doesn't "understand why we can’t really push the ball vertically right now." Nix said he recognizes the need to do that for the offense to pull equal weight to the defense in Denver. “We’re definitely capable ," Nix said. "We’ve shown it and I don’t where the disconnect is right now to be honest with you. . . . I just think we're really, for some reason, struggling to find those explosive plays and that’s what makes an offense really spectacular — finding explosive plays. And right now we don’t have those.” The one positive that Nix could point to is that the Broncos did not turn the ball over while the Seahawks gave it away three times, including an overtime interception that set up Denver's winning points. Head coach Sean Payton didn't delve into the offense's struggles beyond saying "we’re going to see a lot that we want to clean up ," but it is clear that his decision to take over playcalling has not solved all that's wrong with Nix or the rest of the unit.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos won despite totaling just 32 yards on their last 10 possessions
summary: The Broncos' offense was stunningly bad for most of Thursday night's game.
full_text: The Broncos' offense was stunningly bad for most of Thursday night's game. They beat the Seahawks anyway. Over Denver's final 10 possessions — two in the second quarter, three in the third quarter, four in the fourth quarter and one in overtime — the Broncos' offense totaled 32 yards. Seven of those 10 possessions ended in punts, two ended with the ends of the first and second halves, and the one in overtime began in field goal range and ended with the game-winning field goal. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix could not move the offense at all: He threw the ball 27 times for 107 yards, got sacked twice for a loss of 13 yards, and had four rushes for two yards. Add all that up, and in 33 plays, Nix totaled 96 yards. That's 2.9 yards per play. Usually, you can't win in the NFL when your quarterback is playing like that. Fortunately for the Broncos, Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold also played a losing game . Darnold's overtime interception did something Nix couldn't: Put the Broncos in position to win.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sam Darnold: Unfair to our team that I keep turning the ball over, I have to be better
summary: "No way to sugarcoat it: That one sucked. Can't turn the ball over," Darnold said.
full_text: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold was blunt in his self-assessment after Thursday night's loss to the Broncos. "No way to sugarcoat it: That one sucked. Can't turn the ball over," Darnold said immediately upon taking the podium at his post-game press conference. Darnold threw two interceptions, one in the fourth quarter and one in overtime, of a game the Seahawks would ultimately lose 17-14. He acknowledged afterward that the defense and special teams played well enough to win, and he did not. "When you have a defense and special teams group that's playing the way they are for us, for me, I've just got to protect the football," Darnold said. "Dropping back and taking what they give me, I feel like I did a pretty good job of that in the first half, and then late in the second half, those two plays, you can't have it." Darnold knows that the loss was on him. "It's BS for me to keep turning the ball over," Darnold said. "It's not fair to our defense. It's not fair to our special teams. It's not fair to our entire team. I've got to be better."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ryan Fitzpatrick on Bo Nix's night: "That right there is garbage"
summary: Quarterback-turned-analyst repeatedly tees off on Denver QB.
full_text: The Broncos won on Thursday night, beating the defending Super Bowl champions in overtime. But the victory comes with a major asterisk; Denver's offense continues to be not good enough. As Ryan Fitzpatrick of Prime Video put it after the game, quarterback Bo Nix is not good enough. "Bo Nix is not playing competitively," Fitzpatrick said, growing increasingly animated as he went. "It's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing quarterback right now. . . . He has no trust from his coach, he calls a screen play on third and eight. . . . Now they're in the locker room right now, they're excited. They won. He's not playing competitive football right now. . . . I can only imagine how Sean Payton feels. I mean, Sean Payton, [offensive coordinatpr] Davis Webb, everybody that blocks for him. He's not competing right now. And that's something that he's hung his hat on for the last two years. I don't know if he's still injured. I don't know what's going on. But it's not good enough. It's effort." Later in the postgame show, Fitzpatrick was given another chance to elaborate on his critique of Nix. “Well, there’s no fire and there’s no passion," Fitzpatrick said. "And that doesn’t mean you’ve got to be yelling at guys on the sideline or inspiring in the huddle. You can do it with your play as well. And I just don’t see it. And I just think that he needs to be sat down and they need to tell him being a quarterback in the NFL is a very special thing. And right now he’s taking it for granted. He is. And there’s a lot of guys that have played this game that watch that game that think, ‘That right there is garbage. That effort is garbage. That is not a quarterback in the NFL. We deserve better.’” For the game, Nix completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards, no touchdowns, and no interceptions. His passer rating was 71.1. Denver's offense gained only 168 yards. Seattle gained 353. It remains to be seen whether Payton will have anything to say publicly about Nix's play. Payton may have some pointed things to say privately — and if the issues continue, who knows what will happen? Because Nix is in his third season, whatever comes next will be critical. Nix will be eligible for a second contract after the season. And the Broncos' eventual options could be to either pay him market value or move on. Bot every team wants to kick the can or pay a mid-level contract to a guy who lands in the "average" category. To win consistently and to chase championships, it's critical to have a guy who's playing like a franchise quarterback.
author: Mike Florio

title: New report links Greg Olsen to Monday Night Football in 2027
summary: The offseason game of broadcaster roulette will be intriguing, and expensive.
full_text: '' The offseason game of broadcaster roulette will be intriguing, and expensive. With the Monday Night Football spot at ESPN/ABC opening up if Troy Aikman leaves, there will be more than a few who want it. John Ourand of Puck drops a juicy nugget in the latest edition of The Varsity newsletter. Take it away, John: "My best sources are predicting that Greg Olsen will wind up in ESPN’s Monday Night Football booth next season." It's just a prediction, but Ourand wouldn't throw something like that around unless he had good reason to believe it. Hovering over any of the top spots will be Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, who has the chops and the cachet to pick his spot and name his price. Olsen, who has won multiple Emmys (including the most recent one, from his spot on the Fox "B" team) seems destined to land with a No. 1 team, somewhere. Whether that's ESPN, CBS, or Prime Video, it seems inevitable that Olsen, who was bumped to the bench because Fox wanted Tom Brady, will once again have a prime spot, somewhere.
author: Mike Florio

title: Seahawks need to consider whether Drew Lock gives them a better chance to win
summary: The conversation, however it's resolved, needs to be had.
full_text: The conversation, however it's resolved, needs to be had. Should the Seahawks turn to Drew Lock over Sam Darnold at quarterback? Darnold has seven interceptions in four full games (he handled five snaps of the Week 1 game against the Patriots). Drew Lock threw four touchdown passes and no picks in most of the Patriots game and all of the Week 2 game against the Cardinals. Darnold has started four games since returning from his glute injury. He's 1-3. Said Darnold on Tuesday, regarding the miscues: "I’m going to continue to be as decisive as I can be and go through my reads and trust what I see, trust my feet, all those things. Can’t have turnovers. You have to protect the football in this league. If you don’t, you’ll pay.” For a running back like James Cook of the Bills, a turnover problem could mean fewer reps and touches in the tailback rotation. For a quarterback, it's all or nothing; he either takes all the snaps, or he takes none of them. At some point, the Seahawks need to ask themselves whether Lock should be the one taking the snaps. Obviously, benching Darnold would likely mean the Seahawks would move on in 2027. His $35.5 million in compensation for next year, the last of his contract, isn't guaranteed. He earns a $10 million roster bonus on the fifth day of the league year in March. The Seahawks may ultimately decide to ride or die with Darnold for the rest of the season. But they at least need to have the conversation about making a switch, and the possibility of being benched at some point needs to be on the table in order to underscore Darnold's assessment. " You have to protect the football in this league. If you don’t, you’ll pay .”
author: Mike Florio

title: Thursday Night Football: Broncos beat Seahawks 17-14 in overtime
summary: Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal with 4:53 remaining in overtime after Ja'Quan McMillian's pick of Sam Darnold.
full_text: The Broncos had not lost a home game leading by 11 or more points in the fourth quarter since a 2004 loss to the Raiders. They still haven't. The Seahawks rallied from 11 down in the fourth quarter to force overtime, but Sam Darnold threw an interception on the first possession of the extra period. Ja'Quan McMillian's pick at the Seattle 43 put the Broncos in field-goal range, and Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal to win it 17-14. The Broncos moved to 4-2, while the Seahawks fell to 3-3. In the second half, the Broncos had 30 yards and two first downs, going 0-for-6 on third down. Bo Nix was 7-of-12 for 29 yards in the final 30 minutes. The Broncos gained only 8 yards on their game-winning, overtime field-goal drive, but it was enough. The Seahawks couldn't get out of their own way all night: They had 91 yards and three points in the first half; Rashid Shaheed lost a fumble; Jason Myers missed a 47-yard field goal off the right upright in the third quarter; and Darnold threw two picks in crunch time. The Seahawks were in field-goal range to tie the game late in the fourth quarter when Broncos cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine intercepted Darnold, undercutting Tory Horton at the Denver 31. The pick with 1:25 left didn't end the game as the Seahawks had all three timeouts. The Broncos burned only 15 seconds off the clock before Shaheed returned Jeremy Crawshaw's punt 31 yards to the Seattle 46. Eight plays and 38 yards later, the game was tied on Myers 34-yard field goal with 3 seconds left in regulation. The Seahawks had six drives inside the Denver 40 but had only a field goal, a touchdown and a 2-point conversion to show for it. Seattle outgained Denver 353 to 168, with Darnold going 27-of-51 for 278 yards with two picks. He was pressured on 24 of his dropbacks, and the Broncos sacked him five times. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 passes for 134 yards after having only two catches for 11 yards at halftime. Nix finished 17-of-27 for 107 yards, with RJ Harvey catching three passes for 31 yards. Harvey and J.K. Dobbins scored the Broncos' touchdowns on short runs.
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks draw to within 14-11 of Broncos
summary: The Seahawks have their first touchdown of the night, and Thursday Night Football has a game.
full_text: The Seahawks have their first touchdown of the night, and Thursday Night Football has a game. George Holani scored on a 1-yard run, and Rashid Shaheed caught a 2-point conversion on a pass that Sam Darnold threw up for grabs. It has the Seahawks within 14-11 of the Broncos. The Seahawks went 67 yards in 11 plays, converting a third-and-long and a fourth-and-medium. Sam Darnold threw a 7-yard pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba to the Denver 32 on fourth-and-4 and later converted a third-and-10 with an 18-yard scramble. Jason Myers missed a 47-yard field goal off the right upright in the third quarter or the game would be tied. Darnold is 20-of-38 for 195 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: NFL says it will be "selective" about playing on Wednesdays
summary: The NFL has begun scheduling some games on Wednesdays.
full_text: '' The NFL has begun scheduling some games on Wednesdays. For now, "some" will be the operative word. Via Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing , NFL executive V.P. and chief media officer Hans Schroeder said this week at a Front Office Sports event that Wednesday games are not likely to become the norm. “ We’re going to be selective ,” Schroeder said. “I don’t think what you’re going to see is playing Wednesday football throughout the year. But if there’s opportunities to do something creative like we did on Wednesday and Thanksgiving Eve or like Christmas became on those certain days, we’re going to look at it. We’re going to figure out whether we think it’s a smart thing to do. And then we’re going to look at the numbers and make sure that the numbers and the viewership validates what our instincts are.” While that explanation surely reflects the league's current thinking on the issue, the league's thinking about playing on Christmas once included no plan to play on Christmas when December 25 falls on a Tuesday or a Wednesday. Indeed, it was Schroeder who said that . And then someone crunched the numbers and the owners said, "Do it." That could happen with Wednesday night football. If Sunday Ticket is, as YouTube believes it will be, " deconstructed ," the league would have an added incentive to peel more games from the Sunday afternoon cluster and drop them into prime-time windows. Why not Wednesday night? Why not Tuesday night? The league learned during the pandemic that it's possible to pull it off, and with the league having no qualms about a Sunday-to-Thursday turnaround, it's possible to devise a schedule that has teams playing on the non-traditional days of the week. For Wednesdays, the easiest approach would be to configure the schedule to give the assignment to teams emerging from a bye, or to teams who play on the prior Thursday. Tuesday night games could be the final contests of a given week, with the teams then playing on Sunday or Monday. In the end, it will all be driven by the desire to make more and more money. And prime-time standalone games make more money than they do when dropped into a Sunday afternoon window with multiple other games.
author: Mike Florio

title: Police continue to withhold the Josh Jacobs video
summary: As Packers running back Josh Jacobs continues to spend the early weeks of the 2026 season on paid leave, the NFL reportedly still hasn't gotten access to the key piece of video generated by the incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to battery.
full_text: As Packers running back Josh Jacobs continues to spend the early weeks of the 2026 season on paid leave, the NFL reportedly still hasn't gotten access to the key piece of video generated by the incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to battery. Via Danielle Lerner of USA Today , police in Wisconsin are delaying the release of the video — both to the NFL and to the media. Last month, the judge presiding over the criminal case lifted a temporary court order sealing the evidence in the case, while concluding that the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department had the discretion "to apply a balancing test between the rights of the public, the defendant and the victim in deciding whether to release the records." In an October 13 letter to USA Today , Hobart-Lawrence police chief Michael Renkas explained that, although the department determined it could release some records with "appropriate redactions," it is required to wait because the lawyers in the underlying case intend to seek a new court order blocking the disclosure. "Accordingly, the Department is temporarily withholding all responsive records in accordance with the statutory waiting period and any applicable court orders," Renkas wrote. "This temporary hold does not constitute a denial of your request or a reversal of the Department's balancing-test determination." Some in league circles believe Jacobs could return from paid leave soon, with the games Jacobs has missed eventually being credited toward his suspension. However, it seems unlikely that the NFL will allow Jacobs to play until it sees the video. The NFL learned the hard way the lesson of closing a player's Personal Conduct Policy case without first seeing the relevant video. The release of the Ray Rice elevator video in September 2014, coupled with a report that the NFL had seen it before it was leaked to TMZ, sparked a major controversy that threatened the employment of the Commissioner. Surely, the league won't risk putting itself in that same position again. And so the bottom-line message is, or should be, that Jacobs doesn't play until the NFL sees the video.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets S Minkah Fitzpatrick will appeal fine for hit on Browns WR KC Concepcion
summary: Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick said he received a fine from the NFL for a hit that concussed Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion on Sunday.
full_text: '' Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick said he received a fine from the NFL for a hit that concussed Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion on Sunday. Fitzpatrick wouldn't reveal the fine amount but said he will appeal. " It was a football play , in my opinion," Fitzpatrick said Thursday, via Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News. "Obviously, we don't like to see anybody get hurt. I'm happy to see that he's back out practicing this week. But in my opinion, it was a football play, a bang-bang play as their coach put it." Fitzpatrick ripped off Concepcion's helmet, which also likely drew a fine from the league, in the first quarter before an unnecessary roughness penalty four plays later that knocked out Concepcion. Concepcion returned to practice Wednesday but remains in concussion protocol after another limited practice Thursday. “When you look at the league rules, they say you can’t hit a defenseless player,” Fitzpatrick said. “I really don’t know what that means. “I understand why I got the penalty. It wasn’t for targeting or hitting him in the head. It was for hitting a defenseless player. In my opinion, when a receiver has the ball, you have every right to hit him as long as you are not hitting him in the head.” Browns fans were not fans of Fitzpatrick before Sunday. They remember his tackle on then-Cleveland running back Nick Chubb in 2023 that tore ligaments and the meniscus in Chubb's left leg. “I’m over that issue,” Fitzpatrick said of the Chubb play.
author: Charean Williams

title: Troy Aikman: It seems like ESPN is going to go in a different direction
summary: Hall of Fame quarterback and ESPN/ABC Monday Night Football analyst Troy Aikman made some waves on Thursday morning by creating the clear impression that he's planning to leave after his current contract expires, after Super Bowl LXI.
full_text: '' Hall of Fame quarterback and ESPN/ABC Monday Night Football analyst Troy Aikman made some waves on Thursday morning by creating the clear impression that he's planning to leave after his current contract expires, after Super Bowl LXI. Aikman elaborated on his remarks to Jimmy Traina of Underscore Media. "It just seems to be where they’re going — that they’re gonna go in a different direction because there’s been no talks, no contract negotiations," Aikman told Traina. "We’re in a Super Bowl year. The Super Bowl is Feb. 14. My contract ends in March. It just doesn’t seem logical that if they were gonna keep me, something wouldn’t be in place before that.” The more recent quotes create a window for ESPN to still attempt to extend Aikman. He didn't say the door is closed from his perspective; he said he's sensing it's closed from the company's perspective. It officially won't close until his contract expires and he becomes a free agent. Traina also asked Aikman whether he believes it will be difficult to finish the year, in light of his impression that ESPN won't be trying to keep him. “The rest of the season will be fine," Aikman said. "Excited about it. Looking forward to it. It’s awesome that we got the Super Bowl. Not a problem at all." In his latest comments, Aikman didn't address the report of tension with his long-time broadcast partner, Joe Buck, or the contention that they recently argued about the fact that Buck has signed a five-year extension while Aikman has been, by all appearances, frozen out. Whether it's posturing from Aikman or not, all other potential suitors now know he's in play. Which will be a factor in the looming game of broadcaster musical chairs, with ESPN, CBS, and Prime Video all potentially looking to land one of the big names. Aikman is among the biggest in football broadcasting. He's been part of a No. 1 team for a long time, and he could instantly move to top of the wish list for other networks that will be looking for a new lead NFL analyst.
author: Mike Florio

title: Thursday Night Football: Broncos lead Seahawks 14-3 at halftime
summary: The Broncos have stymied the Seahawks, limiting them to 91 yards and forcing a fumble.
full_text: The Broncos have a banged up secondary. It hasn't mattered. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph's unit forced three punts, recovered a fumble and allowed only a field goal. The Broncos lead 14-3 at halftime. The Seahawks have 91 yards, including only 40 net passing yards, and are 2-for-6 on third down. Sam Darnold is 7-of-15 for 52 yards and has been sacked twice. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has only two catches for 11 yards. Sean Payton, who took over play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb a game ago, has called a more balanced game with 17 runs and 15 passes, and the Broncos have 130 yards. The Broncos had scored only 23 first-half points in their first five games combined. Bo Nix is 10-of-15 for 78 yards, with running back RJ Harvey catching three for 31. J.K. Dobbins has 11 carries for 35 yards. The Seahawks lost tight end Elijah Arroyo, who injured his shoulder while trying to recover Rashid Shaheed's fumble. He is doubtful to return. The Broncos have ruled out running back Tyler Badie with a left thumb injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Broncos run for a second TD, 14-3 lead
summary: The Broncos entered Thursday night ranked 30th in total offense, including 25th in rushing.
full_text: The Broncos entered Thursday night ranked 30th in total offense, including 25th in rushing. They are having no problem moving the ball against the league's No. 1 defense, though. The Broncos have 125 yards, including 51 rushing, after three drives against the Seahawks. RJ Harvey's 1-yard touchdown run with 5:15 remaining in the first half has the Broncos holding a 14-3 lead. Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon was called for a 20-yard defensive pass interference penalty on Courtland Sutton in the end zone to set up Harvey's score. J.K. Dobbins scored the team's first touchdown on a 4-yard run. Dobbins has 10 carries for 35 yards and Harvey three carries for 10 yards. Bo Nix is 9-of-13 for 74 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Broncos take 7-3 lead over Seahawks in second quarter
summary: The Broncos looked more like the Broncos of 2025 on their second drive Thursday night.
full_text: The Broncos looked more like the Broncos of 2025 on their second drive Thursday night. Denver went 74 yards in 16 plays and 8:39 for a go-ahead touchdown. J.K. Dobbins' 4-yard run to the end zone has the Broncos leading 7-3 with 12:52 remaining in the first quarter. Running back Tyler Badie converted a fourth-and-3 with a 6-yard run to the Seattle 42 to keep the drive going. But Badie then left for the training room and is questionable to return with a left thumb injury. The Broncos also converted a third-and-8 and a third-and-6, with Bo Nix completions of 9 yards to Evan Engram and 9 yards to Courtland Sutton. Nix is 7-of-10 for 59 yards, and running back RJ Harvey has three catches for 31 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers WR Mike Evans misses practice with Achilles soreness
summary: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans has played through injured ribs.
full_text: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans has played through injured ribs. He had another injury added to the report on Thursday. Evans was listed as a non-participant with an Achilles. "Just some Achilles soreness," coach Kyle Shanahan said. Defensive end Nick Bosa, who has missed the past three games with a calf injury, remained out of practice Thursday. The 49ers added defensive tackle Gracen Halton to the report with a quadriceps issue, and he did not practice. Running back Christian McCaffrey (rest), wide receiver Deebo Samuel (hamstring), safety Marques Sigle (ankle), defensive tackle James Thompson (ankle), linebacker Garret Wallow (hamstring) and left tackle Trent Williams (rest) also did not practice. Shanahan said injured reserve is a possibility for Samuel. Fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee), wide receiver Christian Kirk (calf), offensive tackle Colton McKivitz (illness), safety Siran Neal (neck), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder), defensive end Mykel Williams (knee) and offensive guard Carver Willis (toe) were limited. Kirk had his 21-day return-to-practice window opened Thursday as he returns from injured reserve.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jon Morris, a member of the Patriots Hall of Fame, died at 84
summary: Jon Morris, a member of the Patriots Hall of Fame, has died, the team announced Thursday.
full_text: '' Jon Morris, a member of the Patriots Hall of Fame, has died, the team announced Thursday. He was 84. The cause of death was undisclosed. The Boston Patriots selected Morris in the fourth round in the 1964 AFL draft, and the Packers took him in the second round of the NFL draft. The Holy Cross product signed with the Patriots and spent 11 of his 15 NFL seasons in New England. Morris was a six-time AFL all-star center from 1964-69 and a Pro Bowl selection in 1970 when the team joined the NFL as part of the AFL-NFL merger. Morris spent the 1974-77 seasons in Detroit before a final season with Chicago in 1978. “Jon Morris was one of the great players who helped build the foundation of our franchise,” Patriots owner Robert Kraft said in a statement. “For generations of Patriots fans, he represented the toughness, dedication and pride of those early teams.” Morris played alongside future Patriots Hall of Famers Gino Cappelletti, Babe Parilli and Jim Nance, and he went into the team's Hall of Fame in 2011. Morris was also included on the Patriots’ 50th anniversary team in 2009.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams add S Kam Curl to practice report with an ankle injury
summary: The Rams added safety Kam Curl to the practice report Thursday.
full_text: The Rams added safety Kam Curl to the practice report Thursday. He was limited due to an ankle injury. It indicates Curl injured his ankle during practice, but coach Sean McVay doesn't hold a news conference again until Friday. The Rams also added offensive lineman Keagen Trost to the injury report with a hamstring injury, but he was a full participant. Wide receiver Alex Bachman (wrist) returned to full participation after limited work Wednesday. The rest of the Rams' report remained the same: Tight end Davis Allen (foot) did not practice, and inside linebacker Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and cornerback Josh Wallace (shoulder) were limited again. Inside linebacker Omar Speights (knee) was a full participant for a second consecutive day.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jeremiyah Love missed practice again on Thursday
summary: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love's ankle injury continues to create uncertainty about the first-round pick's availability for Sunday's game against the Rams.
full_text: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love's ankle injury continues to create uncertainty about the first-round pick's availability for Sunday's game against the Rams. Love missed practice for the second straight day on Thursday. The injury has been lingering for a couple of weeks and head coach Mike LaFleur said on Wednesday that the team would "give it a little bit of rest and see how it is as the week goes on ." Friday will bring more word on whether the Cardinals will have the rookie for Week 6. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are the other backs on Arizona's 53-man roster. Safeties Wydett Williams (concussion) and Andrew Wingard (knee) also missed practice. Safety Kitan Crawford (ankle) and wide receiver Devin Duvernay (ribs) were both limited participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Caleb Williams confirms he tore his hamstring, doesn't know his status for Sunday
summary: Williams has had two full practices this week as he works his way back from the Week 2 injury.
full_text: Caleb Williams has had two full practices this week, but the Bears quarterback insists he doesn't know whether he will return for Sunday's game against the Falcons. “Before you start asking, I do not know if I’m playing yet,” Williams said Thursday, via Dan Wiederer of TheAthletic.com. Williams injured his hamstring in a Sept. 20 game, and he has missed the past three games. He said he has checkpoints to clear and a "stress test" to pass before he can play. In his first media availability since his injury, Williams explained what happened when he went down awkwardly on a red-zone scramble in the fourth quarter of the 9-3 loss to the Vikings. “I felt a pop,” Williams said. “That’s why I looked back. I looked back just like everybody else does when you feel a pop. [You] think somebody grabbed you, and nobody grabbed me.” Williams took issue with reports that he was diagnosed with a strain, which some labeled a Grade 2 strain. “It was a hamstring tear,” Williams said, “and a pretty serious one.” Williams would not reveal the grade tear he has. “We got a grade, but I wouldn’t say it’s deserved to be put out there after all the false [reports],” Williams said. “So next question.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. has full practice, expects to have no limitations Sunday
summary: Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. participated fully in Thursday's practice, and he expects to have no limitations for Sunday's game against the Packers.
full_text: ' Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. participated fully in Thursday's practice, and he expects to have no limitations for Sunday's game against the Packers. "That's what I’m shooting for . That's what they're shooting for as well," Porter told Patrik Walker of the team website. "So that's what we're gonna try to do." Porter was inactive at the start of the season with the Steelers after not getting the expected long-term contract extension. He played 25 snaps in his debut with the Cowboys in Week 4, but missed the Week 5 game last Thursday night after coming down with an illness on game day. title: Cowboys DC Christian Parker: Mike Pettine a "right-hand man" not a "save the day" hire
summary: The Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator and former Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant this week and defensive coordinator Christian Parker was asked at a Thursday press conference if Pettine is a "save the day" hire after a rough start.
full_text: ' The Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator and former Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant this week and defensive coordinator Christian Parker was asked at a Thursday press conference if Pettine is a "save the day" hire after a rough start. Parker said, via Clarence Hill of DLLS Sports, that "I don’t need to respond to that" and explained that he sees Pettine as a "right-hand man" in his first season running the defense. Parker's first NFL job was working under Pettine in Green Bay in 2019 and Parker outlined how he plans to utilize the veteran coach for the rest of this year. "Sounding board, advancing, watching film, he'll have an area of expertise just like all the position coaches do," Parker said, via the team's website. "I think when we come in Monday, he's already kind of gotten ahead on the next opponent, those kinds of things. Those roles usually are focused on advances, some area of expertise, and just kind of having a guy to bounce ideas off of." Parker said that he views the Cowboys' defensive problems as "very fixable" and Sunday night against the Packers would be an ideal time to show that the staff has started that process.

title: With his next TD catch, Davante Adams will pass Larry Fitzgerald on the all-time list
summary: Rams wide receiver Davante Adams has four touchdown catches this season.
full_text: Rams wide receiver Davante Adams has four touchdown catches this season. On his next touchdown, he'll have more than all but five players in NFL history. Adams and Larry Fitzgerald are currently tied with 121 career receiving touchdowns, the sixth-most in NFL history. With one more, Adams will have 122 and move ahead of Fitzgerald for sole possession of No. 6 all time. No one is going to catch the all-time leader, Jerry Rice, any time soon. Rice retired with 197 career receiving touchdowns. But everyone else ahead of Adams is someone Adams might be able to catch, with a few more good years: In second place is Randy Moss with 156 receiving touchdowns, followed by Terrell Owens with 153, Cris Carter with 130 and Marvin Harrison with 128. Adams has a shot at surpassing both Harrison and Carter this year, and moving into fourth place all-time. The 33-year-old Adams had 73 touchdown catches with the Packers, 23 with the Raiders, seven with the Jets and now has 18 with the Rams.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Broncos' cheating accusation against Seahawks almost led to lawsuit in 2024, according to Mike Macdonald
summary: This is one of the wildest stories you'll ever hear in the NFL
full_text:
Last season almost ended with the Denver Broncos facing the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl , and if that game would have happened, there likely would have been some serious drama, because it seems the two head coaches don't like each other very much.
Just ask Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald about that.
"He's not my biggest fan," Macdonald recently said of Broncos' coach Sean Payton.
During a recent interview with Graham Bensinger , Macdonald spilled the details on a wild story from 2024 involving Payton.
In his first game ever as a head coach, Macdonald led his team to a 26-20 road win over the Broncos to open the 2024 season. During the game, the Seahawks' defense seemed to always be one step ahead of Denver's offense: They forced three turnovers while holding the Broncos to just 231 yards.
Since it was Week 1, Macdonald didn't have a lot of film on the Broncos, so he decided to turn to Twitter to see if he could find some plays they might use.
"Fans will tape and post plays from training camp on Twitter, so it's public knowledge, so we took like a 100 plays from their training camp," Macdonald said. "We're scouting them."
At some point after the game was played, Payton somehow found out about the Seahawks' social media scouting session and he was NOT happy.
"He got wind of it and he lost it," Macdonald said.
Payton was so upset with what Seattle did that he threated to turn them into the NFL . It got so serious that Payton actually reached out to Seahawks general manger John Schneider.
"So he called John and he basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot, like Spygate type of thing," Macdonald said. "And I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my God, we didn't cheat.' He thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant."
So it appears that Payton thought the Seahawks may have actually sent someone to Broncos' training camp, which would be illegal, but Macdonald says all the plays came from Twitter, which wouldn't violate any NFL rules. The Seahawks were so sure that they didn't break any rules that they threatened to SUE Payton if he reached out to the league.
"So we had to counter with him, to say like, 'Hey, look, if you come out at us, we're going to sue you, because it's not true,'" Macdonald said. "So he backed down, but he was killing John, our GM."
None of this ever leaked out and the reason for that is because Payton eventually put it behind him.
"So the season ends and he let it go," Macdonald said.
Payton might have let it go, but the Seahawks' strategy appears to have led to a major change at Broncos training camp. It is now prohibited for fans to take video at any of Denver's training camp practices. During their 2026 camp, the Broncos posted signs all around the facility so that fans knew they could be kicked out if they were excessively breaking the rules.
These signs greet #Broncos fans at training camp. A security official said the great majority of fans are following rules. The official said fans can get a warning initially and nobody is in jeopardy of being evicted unless actions “excessive.” Nobody was said to be tossed Friday pic.twitter.com/cswT91vnvk
Allowing fans and media to film plays at training camp has become a touchy issue around the NFL. Some teams permit it, but most of them are like the Broncos and have rules against it.
Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley was in a similar situation last season when he was the defensive coordinator for the Packers . At the time, Kevin Patullo, who is now a Dolphins assistant, was the Eagles offensive coordinator and Philadelphia scouted the Packers by using a training camp play they spotted on social media.
"We had a pressure I had never run, so there's no way he could've known about it," Hafley said earlier this month . "And they knew it was coming. (Kevin) said they saw it on video."
With the Payton-Macdonald feud now going public, teams may decide to revisit their social media policies when it comes to fans at training camp.
For Macdonald, scouting plays on Twitter ended up working out, which isn't a huge surprise, because most things seem to end up working out for him. The Seahawks head coach won a Lombardi Trophy last season in just his second year on the job. The Seahawks beat the Patriots in Super Bowl LX and they came close to facing the Broncos: Denver came up just one game short of getting to the Super Bowl with a loss in the AFC title game.
author: John Breech

title: Caleb Williams responds to critics after hamstring injury: 'My character's been attacked'
summary: Williams participated fully in consecutive practices, but the Bears quarterback said he has not yet been cleared to return to game action
full_text:
Following consecutive practices of full participation, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is on track for a potential return in Week 6 from the hamstring injury he sustained in the second game of the season. It remains to be seen whether he will enter Sunday's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons with an injury designation, but he said on Thursday that he still does not know if he will play.
While the understanding outside the Bears' facility is that Williams sustained a Grade 2 hamstring strain in the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the third-year quarterback pushed back against reports detailing the extent of the injury. He said he felt a pop in his hamstring at the time of the injury and described it as a tear rather than a strain.
"It was a hamstring tear and a pretty serious one," Williams said. "We got a grade, but I wouldn't say it's deserved to be put out there after all the false ones. So next question."
Williams repeatedly declined to detail the official diagnosis.
"There's nothing that has come out that has been right about what it is and what it has been," Williams said. "That's been fun to deal with. So I would say from y'all's side and things like that is being able to report it and go through it in the right way and right manner. And then from there, if you haven't heard it from boss man himself or out of the horse's mouth, me, it would probably be wrong, which every single one has been."
Coach Ben Johnson initially labeled Williams as week-to-week after the team received the results of his MRI. Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum split the quarterback duties over the last three games.
Not only did Williams take exception to the reporting on his hamstring injury, but he also noticed the discourse surrounding his on-field demeanor. Williams was in clear distress in the immediate wake of the injury as he yelled in agony and was emotional when he left the field on a cart. He had a towel over his head as he was transported to the locker room and shed tears while giving a thumbs-up to the Chicago crowd.
Caleb Williams gives a thumbs up as he's carted off the field. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/omeGyES2s5
When initial reports and the Bears' handling of the injury suggested that it may not be as serious as feared, fans were quick to judge Williams for what some called an overreaction.
"I'm always gonna show emotion, especially when I can't be out there with the guys when something like that happens," Williams said. "I care about the team, the organization, winning, being out there, my teammates, all of that. I care. That's the biggest thing. This is what I love to do. This puts a smile on my face. It's everything to me.
"Not being able to be out there was frustrating. That was more of the tears or whatever that was. The other half of it was just everybody making jokes and all of that. But that doesn't bother me. It's the other half of the national or the local [media] and them putting out false things that weren't true to then allow people to go run with it."
Dating back to his college career at USC, Williams continues to be the subject of scrutiny for his perceived toughness. The response to his hamstring injury is the latest example, as fans also called into question his nail-painting, the emotions he shed after a tough loss to rival UCLA, and more.
"My character's been attacked for a while," Williams said. "It's just another motivating factor when I get out there and get going again."
author: Carter Bahns

title: Dak Prescott delivers message to NFL players after Jalen Hurts' blood-clot diagnosis
summary: The Cowboys quarterback called Hurts' condition "scary" and encouraged athletes to communicate openly with medical personnel
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- News of Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts being ruled out in Week 6 with a superficial blood clot shook many NFL players, including rival Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott .
"It's scary when you get things like that. Blood clots, you're talking about someone's life, especially with the plane trip and all that they took," Prescott said. "Yeah, it's scary. If you're feeling something, speak up on it. I'm fortunate I have [my personal physical therapist] Luke Miller. He's on things before I'm on things at times. I try to blow things off, and he's like 'no, no let's look at this. Let me get a better check on it.' I encourage people to be open about their body and learn about their body."
In a statement about the injury, the Eagles said Hurts visited the training room on Thursday, Oct. 8, after practice to receive treatment on his calf. Philadelphia had an ultrasound of his calf done on Saturday after the team flew to London for their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , and it picked up a superficial blood clot. In tandem with London doctors, the team's medical staff decided Hurts could play safely. After a follow-up ultrasound, it was discovered Hurts' blood clot had moved, so the Eagles ruled him out for their Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers , saying "his health and safety are our highest priority."
Prescott's message to other athletes in light of this situation is straightforward: have open conversations with your team's training staff. He acknowledged there can sometimes be a stigma to doing so as an NFL player, but there's nothing wrong with putting things on their radar.
"I'm in a fortunate situation now being this far into my career, but it's about making good relationships with those guys [the training staff]," Prescott said. "Tell them everything. You can get a heads up on it. You can tell them and just say 'it's fine, but I'm letting you know.' I encourage all athletes: don't be shy if something is bothering you. Speak up on it. This is a tough man's sport at the end of the day, so let them know if you're fine like 'hey, I'm just warning you. I'm just alerting you, so you can get ahead of things like this.'"
author: Garrett Podell

title: Broncos vs. Seahawks pick: Bo Nix hopes to rejuvenate offense but has tough task vs. Seattle D on 'TNF'
summary: Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers
full_text:
In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks .
The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500.
The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game.
Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote.
The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide.
The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate.
Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles.
In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well.
Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.)
The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often.
Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles.
Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2.
Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season.
Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date.
Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere.
The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit.
Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. Pick: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16
author: Jared Dubin

title: Christian Parker contradicts Jerry Jones, likely to stay on sideline as Cowboys defense seeks answers
summary: Parker says he will "most likely" remain on the sideline, but the addition of Mike Pettine underscores the urgency in Dallas
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Any football fan knows that when a coach or coordinator is moved up to the booth, it's the start of a performance improvement plan that typically does not end well.
Jerry Jones said Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan that Christian Parker would move upstairs for Week 6. Parker himself pushed back on that notion on Thursday, saying he will "most likely" remain down on the sideline.
"There's advantages of both for sure, but I've always been a guy that's usually been down on the field," Parker said.
Parker also received the dreaded vote of confidence from Brian Schottenheimer amid his struggling defense's performance in the Cowboys' 2-3 start to the 2026 season. That came in the wake of Dallas hiring former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019.
"Christian Parker is our defensive coordinator and everything, all decisions, will run through him," Schottenheimer said Wednesday. "We're supporting him. I support him. I believe so strongly in the guy. I do. I think the guy's an incredible football coach. We have to coach better. We got to play better. I think our players will be the first ones to say there's things that they need to do better. There's things I need to do better.  And so no one is sitting here pointing fingers at Christian Parker. But as the head coach, you have to make decisions that you think helps you win games. That's not just adding a Mike Pettine, it's some of the personnel adjustments that I know you guys are dying to know about that are being worked on behind the scenes and communicated to the players."
Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked total defense (395.4 total yards per game allowed), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it.
How fixable are the issues?
"Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable."
The level of urgency Parker and his players have shown through five weeks is far from an overreaction. Matt Eberflus, Parker's predecessor in 2025, had the Dallas defense looking very similar through five weeks. The only significant difference is that Eberflus' unit was the league's worst against the pass, while Parker's is the league's worst against the run.
Completion percentage allowed
One guaranteed personnel adjustment is to make new Dallas cornerback Joey Porter Jr . a full-time starter now that his stomach bug is behind him . He played in 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans . He and the team were ramping up for him to be a full-time starter after being on the roster for a week, but he was scratched shortly before kickoff in Week 5 because he couldn't stop throwing up. Losing his No. 1 corner that close to kickoff was something Parker called "not ideal." However, he and Porter Jr. are ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Green Bay Packers.
Look for rookie first-round edge rusher Malachi Lawrence to get more involved. Lawrence racked up his first career sack as well as a pass defensed in Week 5 against the Buccaneers. His quarterback pressure rate of 14.3% ranks fourth among qualified rookies, according to Pro Football Focus. He trails only David Bailey (16.4%), Sonny Styles (15%) and Cashius Howell (14.8%). Through five weeks, Lawrence co-leads the Cowboys in sacks with 1.0 despite playing significantly fewer pass rush snaps than some of Dallas' other edge rushers and defensive linemen.
"Played very well," Schottenheimer said. "I think he's starting to show the flash and the acceleration and the ability to rush the passer that we knew we were getting when we drafted him. And I thought he had a very, very good game against Tampa Bay and you'll see him get more opps [opportunities]."
They'll need Lawrence to beat Packers left tackle Jordan Morgan with regularity to have any hope of slowing down Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love and his top two speedy receivers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Dallas sees facing a high-powered Packers passing attack as an opportunity rather than a challenge.
"I see that we have a lot of opportunities to make plays on the ball, so I know we're all excited for that," Porter Jr. said. "We really have to rally to the ball and make plays when they call on us to."

title: Who is Tanner McKee? Eagles QB gets biggest opportunity yet with Jalen Hurts sidelined
summary: The former Stanford quarterback takes over for Jalen Hurts with Philadelphia trying to end a three-game skid and remain in the NFC East race
full_text:
The task of breaking a three-game losing streak and keeping the Philadelphia Eagles afloat in the NFC East falls not on Jalen Hurts in Week 6 but rather on Tanner McKee , a fourth-year backup primed for the biggest opportunity of his NFL career. Hurts is out for the matchup against the Carolina Panthers due to a superficial blood clot , which developed after the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and moved following last week's trip to London, resulting in his unavailability for Sunday.
While the Eagles do have a third option in rookie Cole Payton , the expectation is that McKee will trot out with the offense when they return to Lincoln Financial Field. He served as Hurts' primary backup last year and was the third-stringer in 2024 and made a combined six appearances with two starts.
McKee is not entirely unknown in the NFL, considering his pair of previous starts, but this is by far the most prominent role of his career. With so much pressure facing the Eagles in their quest to rebound from a rocky start to the season, McKee will have more eyes on him this weekend than ever before.
So who is McKee, really? Here is everything to know about his football career, from his rise as a highly touted high school recruit to his emergence as Philadelphia's Week 6 starter.
McKee landed on the national radar during his junior year at Corona (Calif.) High School. Centennial. It was the most productive season of his prep career and earned him recognition as a Top247 recruit, and he later climbed as high as No. 38 overall in the 247Sports rankings for the Class of 2018 . McKee closed the recruiting cycle as the top four-star quarterback with only three five-star prospects ahead of him: Trevor Lawrence , Justin Fields and JT Daniels.
As a three-sport athlete who also played volleyball and basketball at Centennial, McKee's future was always in football, and he elevated his stock with strong showings on the all-star circuit. He won the MVP award at the 2018 Polynesian Bowl, earned a spot in the U.S. Army All-American Bowl and reached the finals at both The Opening and Elite 11.
McKee already held scholarship offers from myriad Power Five schools when Stanford called. Programs across the country sought his talents. Even though Stanford was his ultimate choice and much closer to home than the other programs he was interested in, it was not an open-and-shut case that he would end up with the Cardinal. Stanford was the last school to extend him an offer and the penultimate school to welcome him for an official visit. By the time he took his official visit in January 2018, he had already been on campus for regular-season games at Texas, Texas A&M, Alabama and Washington.
Each of those other schools pushed hard to land him, but come National Signing Day in February 2018, it was Stanford that earned McKee's commitment. The only hiccup for the Cardinal was that its prized signee would not arrive for another two years.
As a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, McKee embarked on a two-year mission in Brazil. The COVID-19 pandemic cut his mission short by about five weeks, and upon his return to the United States, uncertainty about the 2020 college football season left him without a firm answer as to when he would join the Cardinal and eventually suit up as a freshman quarterback. His roster spot was waiting for him, though, and he was physically ready to join the team thanks to a workout regimen he and a fellow missionary adhered to in Brazil.
"Because we had that weight room in my last area, I think I gained back 10 pounds," McKee said to Deseret News after returning from his mission. "That was super nice. We worked out every morning and I was able to get a little bit back in shape. He threw the rugby ball and I threw the football. Now, when I throw, my arm doesn't really get sore. It's nice to come back home and work out at full speed."
The Pac-12 delayed the start of its season due to the pandemic and was the last of the power conferences to begin play. Stanford held just six games that year, with one against Washington State canceled due to virus protocols. McKee was supposed to be the No. 3 quarterback on Stanford's roster but was elevated to the backup job in the opener when a false positive COVID-19 test kept Davis Mills out of action. That game against No. 12 Oregon got out of hand, and McKee made his lone appearance of the season late in a 35-14 loss.
Mills departed for the NFL at the end of that campaign, which sparked a competition between McKee and incumbent backup Jack West for the starting job in 2021. West won the job out of fall camp but lost it when he threw two interceptions in a 24-7 season-opening loss to Kansas State. McKee took over and never looked back.
The first start of McKee's college career was an indication of the highlights to come. He orchestrated a 42-28 upset win on the road at No. 14 USC and kept the momentum rolling with two more wins in the next three games, including one over the same Oregon team that defeated the Cardinal the year prior. The Ducks were the No. 3 team in the nation at the time and stood on the wrong end of a breakout performance for McKee in which he racked up 230 yards and three touchdowns in an overtime thriller.
That Oct. 2 victory was the last of Stanford's season, though, as everything went off the rails. McKee missed two games due to injury during a seven-game losing streak to close the year.
While the team's overall struggles continued into a three-win 20222 season, McKee did his part as one of the few bright spots on the roster. He started all 12 games and posted a 62% completion rate with 2,947 passing yards and 13 touchdowns to eight interceptions. He also ran for two scores.
McKee's performance as a two-year starter made him a draftable quarterback and led him to leave Stanford a year early. He declared for the 2023 NFL Draft and was selected with the 188th overall pick in the sixth round. That marked the start of what is now a four-year tenure with the Eagles.
Hurts had already established himself as a star quarterback by the time McKee arrived in Philadelphia. He was fresh off the best year of his career: A 2022 campaign in which he earned second-team All-Pro recognition. McKee was never going to be more than a backup, and he spent his rookie year in the No. 3 role behind Hurts and Marcus Mariota . He did not play that season.
McKee's first opportunity for playing time came in 2024. With Hurts in concussion protocol and backup Kenny Pickett dealing with an in-game rib injury, McKee was thrust into action in Week 17, and he could not have performed much better as two of his three completions went for touchdowns.
GO BACK TO AJ BROWN. Great throw by Tanner McKee. 📺: #DALvsPHI on FOX 📱: https://t.co/waVpO909ge pic.twitter.com/ZeW6Syi6nF
McKee then made his first career start in the regular-season finale and was similarly effective in a 27-for-41, 269-yard, two-touchdown win over the New York Giants . The best part of that season, though? McKee was on the sideline when the Eagles won the Super Bowl .
It was not until Week 18 of the following season that McKee returned to the starting lineup. The Eagles had already locked up their postseason position and rested their starters, and with McKee holding the primary backup job that year, he was the next man up at quarterback. He threw for 241 yards and a touchdown but also logged his first career interception in a loss to the Washington Commanders .
When McKee leads the Philadelphia offense onto the field on Sunday, it will be his first start outside of Week 18. And depending on the severity of Hurts' blood clot and how long it takes for him to return to the lineup, McKee might be in line to make consecutive starts for the first time. Once Hurts is cleared to play, though, the Eagles will almost certainly thrust him back into action. Even amid a difficult start to the year and even as it seems the Eagles could be trending toward a rebuild ,…

title: Jayden Daniels takes blame for Commanders' embarrassing gaffe vs. Giants: 'It was a failure'
summary: Daniels defended Dan Quinn on Thursday and shouldered full responsibility for Washington letting the clock run out in field goal range
full_text:
The Washington Commanders had what will likely go down as the most embarrassing moment of the 2026 NFL season, as they ran the clock out on themselves in field goal range in overtime vs. the New York Giants , leading to a 27-27 tie.
Following a wild game that led directly into a bonkers overtime, the Commanders took over possession at their own 23-yard line with 1:55 remaining in overtime and zero timeouts. A 16-yard gain from Terry McLaurin , followed by a Jayden Daniels scramble of 16 yards and a Treylon Burks reception of 13 yards, got Washington into field goal territory with 55 seconds remaining.
On what ended up being the final play of the game, Daniels took a dive at the Giants' 24-yard line with eight seconds remaining on the clock. His offense couldn't get back to the line of scrimmage to spike the ball before it hit triple zeros.
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0
There's a lot of blame to go around for this catastrophe, including head coach Dan Quinn. However, in speaking to reporters on Thursday, Daniels made sure to declare himself the main reason Washington left Week 5 with a tie rather than a win.
"Ultimately, it's on me at the end of the day," Daniels told reporters. "I know DQ is getting a lot of slack for it or whatever, but regardless of what happens, I'm the person on the field that's supposed to calm everything, control everything and I failed to the standard that I hold myself to and the standard in this organization.
"This is something for me to move on, not saying I'm proud of it or anything. Obviously, looking back, it could have resulted in a loss. We tied, but it was a failure in my eyes, and I know I'm better than that. I hold myself to a higher standard than that. So moving forward, I'll grow from it, learn from it, and it'll never happen again."
Daniels isn't wrong. Whether your head coach is Bill Belichick or a first-year guy, the quarterback is responsible for the operation of the offense. Daniels saw the running clock at 13 seconds when he snapped the ball on that final play. At that point, you're throwing it away to the sideline or throwing it in the dirt. You're not taking a sack or going down inbounds. No starting quarterback should have to be told that.
While Quinn has taken much of the blame from the media after the gaffe, Daniels hasn't been without criticism, too. Packers ' edge rusher Micah Parsons ripped into the quarterback on his podcast , saying he "probably cost Dan Quinn his job."
"All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that, like, I'm a defensive player, and this shit's programmed to me," Parsons said. "I even know what to do in those situations. There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts...And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC Championship game. You've been in big moments before. And to me, like even after a sack, you're casually getting up. ... He's not even urgently getting up. ... That is disgusting, bro."
It was a bizarre sequence. Why did the Commanders' players on the field not show any urgency to get back to the line of scrimmage when Daniels went down? Why did David Blough call for a play with motion as the clock continued to tick? What was Daniels trying to do on that final play? The football world may never know.

title: Jalen Hurts blood clot: What is a superficial blood clot and how long could Eagles' QB be out
summary: Movement in a blood clot detected in a follow-up ultrasound has sidelined Philadelphia's star indefinitely after he initially played through the clot against the Jaguars
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles were dealt quite a blow this week, as they revealed star quarterback Jalen Hurts was managing a superficial blood clot and would not play vs. the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Given the situation, it wouldn't be surprising if Hurts missed more than one game.
In their statement released on Thursday, the Eagles said that four days after the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams , Hurts requested treatment on his calf. He believed he was kicked or cleated in the game, and his leg was bothering him. The Eagles performed an ultrasound on their quarterback's leg after they landed in London last week, and that's when the superficial blood clot was discovered.
However, the Eagles' medical staff determined Hurts could suit up against the Jacksonville Jaguars . On Wednesday, back in Philadelphia, the Eagles conducted a follow-up ultrasound, during which they saw that the clot had moved. That's notable. While the Eagles have not disclosed exact details of the situation, the movement of a blood clot could potentially lead to a pulmonary embolism, which could be very serious.
Hurts told reporters on Wednesday that his "calf injury" was "a very unique experience, to say the least," and that he got "nicked up" in the Rams game. Now, he's dealing with a situation that will hold him out indefinitely.
Let's take a look at what's going on with Hurts.
The Eagles did not go into detail about the clot, but the fact that it's "superficial" is likely a good sign. This could be classified as "superficial thrombophlebitis," per Harvard Health Publishing .
An article found on The Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) describes a condition called " superficial vein thrombosis " (SuVT), where clots develop in superficial veins, typically in the legs or arms. Superficial veins are those closer to the surface of the skin. Risk factors include varicose veins, recent trauma, immobility and surgery.
This is different than "deep vein thrombosis," which is a much more serious condition that requires anti-clotting drugs, and could have completely ended Hurts' 2026 season. We've seen several cases of deep vein thrombosis in the NBA recently, including with Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama, who missed the final 30 games of the 2024-25 season after doctors discovered deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder.
As for superficial thrombophlebitis, Harvard Health Publishing says it can improve over the course of one week to several weeks. However, each case is different.
Yes, there are numerous cases of NFL players missing time due to blood clots, and you don't have to look any further than the opponent Philadelphia faces this Sunday. Panthers star right tackle Taylor Moton hasn't played at all this season because doctors found blood clots in his lungs this summer. This was a much more serious situation that required Moton to immediately be placed on blood thinners.
Just recently, Moton revealed that he had been off blood thinners for a couple of weeks and could return to the field in the near future. He was listed as a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
Former first-round pick center Billy Price announced his retirement in 2024 after undergoing emergency surgery for a pulmonary embolism to remove a saddle clot that was entering both of his lungs. He pointed to the risk of internal bleeding while on blood thinners as a reason why he had to hang up the cleats.
Kansas City Chiefs Pro Bowl right guard Trey Smith fell to the sixth round of the 2021 NFL Draft despite being a two-time First Team All-SEC player because of concern over blood clots. He was held to just seven games played during his sophomore season at Tennessee after it was discovered that blood clots had returned in his lungs. Smith lost weight, underwent a six-month round of anticoagulants after consulting with specialists, and was eventually cleared to play football again. Smith's history with blood clots was a clear "con" on his scouting report, but he's had zero issues since being selected at No. 226 overall. He is a two-time Super Bowl champion.
New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave and New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore are two other players who have dealt with blood clots.
Each situation is different, and most of these situations are different from the one Hurts is currently facing. From what we know at the moment, his clot has thankfully not traveled to his lung.
Ian Rapoport reported that Hurts cannot play football until this situation is solved. As mentioned above, treatment for blood clots can include blood thinners, and you shouldn't play football on blood thinners.
We do not know for a fact that Hurts is going on blood thinners. Other treatments for superficial thrombophlebitis include bed rest, elevating the legs or applying warm compresses, according to Harvard Health Publishing. Every case is different, and it's something that has to be monitored.
This is a tough question to answer, given that we don't have details on Hurts' clot — other than that it's superficial. We know Hurts will miss Sunday's game vs. Carolina, but Rapoport said the best way to describe his status is "out indefinitely."
