title: Jalen Hurts out: Why Eagles need to stay the course in 2026, explore QB trade market
summary: Philadelphia needs to remain focused on an NFC East title, explore QB trades and stay on course in 2026
full_text:
The two-time defending NFC East champion Philadelphia Eagles (2-3) will be without face-of-the-franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts for Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers and possibly beyond.
Philadelphia announced an ultrasound on Hurts' calf following a flight back from their London game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5 revealed a superficial blood clot had moved . The Eagles ruled him out and said in a statement they are determining "the appropriate course of treatment" and that Hurts' "health and safety are our highest priority." There's a chance Philadelphia might be without its Super Bowl MVP-winning quarterback for the foreseeable future.
Some teams might take that as a sign to trade away pieces at the trade deadline to reload for 2027, but the Eagles can't do that and shouldn't do that. Philadelphia needs to stay the course and fight to compete in 2026. Here is a look at why, how that could look for the Eagles, what QB they could seek via trade and more.
The short answer as to why the Eagles need to continue their push to contend in 2026 is that they've invested too much money into their top-end talent. Eagles general manager Howie Roseman made the following significant investments this offseason along the defensive line:
After Hurts' five-year, $255 million contract, these three defensive linemen are the Eagles' next three highest-paid players in terms of total contract value. The Eagles still have one of the more talented rosters in football, especially on defense with those three, former first-round pick edge rusher Nolan Smith Jr., All-Pro linebacker Zack Baun , former first-round pick linebacker Jihaad Campbell , All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell , All-Pro cornerback Cooper DeJean and Super Bowl champion cornerback Riq Woolen. Even though former NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) are battling injuries, they're two high-level playmakers when on the field.
This defense is talented enough to keep the Eagles in almost every game. Yes, it's felt like the sky is falling after consecutive losses to the Los Angeles Rams and the Jaguars, in which they blew the lead in the final two minutes. There's a world where they're just a couple plays away from being 4-1 instead of 2-3.
This isn't a situation like the Kansas City Chiefs in 2025, who went 6-11 amid an up-and-down year that saw quarterback Patrick Mahomes go down with a torn ACL. The 2026 Eagles are a much more talented roster than those Chiefs, and their division is much, much worse.
Last season, the AFC West division champion Denver Broncos were the AFC's No. 1 seed with a 14-3 record. The Los Angeles Chargers gutted out an 11-6 Wild Card campaign with quarterback Justin Herbert playing the role of miracle worker behind a battered offensive line.
This season, no one seems to want to win the NFC East. Week 5 was a prime example of that. The Dallas Cowboys (2-3) lost 24-16 at home on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with Jalon Daniels , an undrafted rookie quarterback, making his second career start. Dallas has the NFL's 31st-ranked total defense (395.4 total yards per game allowed), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed), and last-place third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed). If Daniels can march up and down the field on the Cowboys, so can Philadelphia.
The Eagles had the least embarrassing loss of the week, a 19-17 defeat against the AFC South-leading Jaguars despite kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. People fault coach Nick Sirianni for having the kickoff go in bounds to drain time off the clock. The Jaguars returned the kick 53 yards to the Eagles' 39, which set up the game-winning, 57-yard field goal for Jacksonville.
The NFC East-leading New York Giants (3-1-1) tied 27-27 against the last-place Washington Commanders (1-3-1) even though both teams reached field-goal range in the last two minutes of overtime. New York is without quarterback Jaxson Dart and All-Pro edge rusher Brian Burns for the year because of season-ending knee injuries.
A path toward a third straight division title and a home playoff game in the opening round of the postseason is still well within reach.
Sirianni's 67-33 career record, including the playoffs, is tied for the fifth-best record in the first 100 games by an NFL head coach since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger, per CBS Sports Research. Philadelphia has made the playoffs every year under his watch, including winning the NFC twice and winning Super Bowl LIX.
After the current three-game losing streak the Eagles are on, which began with a lifeless "Monday Night Football" defeat to the Case Keenum-led Chicago Bears , Sirianni is under fire. His background is on the offensive side of the ball, but the Eagles are bottom 10 in the entire league in the following metrics: scoring offense (18.4 points per game, 29th), total offense (262.2 total yards per game, 31st) and rushing offense (91.6, tied for 23rd).
The problem appears to be that Sirianni isn't letting new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion fully implement his scheme. Mannion came to Philadelphia after spending last season as the Green Bay Packers quarterbacks coach under Matt LaFleur. He also played for Sean McVay and the Rams and Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings across his nine-season playing career.
Mannion is a branch off the Shanahan-McVay coaching tree, which tends to have offenses that display heavy doses of motion, quarterbacks lining up under center and play-action passing. The scheme wants the looks for runs and passes to appear the same to defenses. That way, the quarterback should be able to easily run a given play as called and then take advantage of a defense that can't tell what's coming.
In Mannion's offense under Sirianni, the Eagles are just average in motion rate (57.8%, 13th in the NFL) while ranking bottom-five in under-center rate (31.1%, 28th) and dead last in play-action rate (16.7%). Running the Shanahan-McVay offense without its core staples is like trying to play video games without plugging the console's HDMI cord into the TV: It's not going to work.
As odd as it may sound, losing Hurts and having a three-game losing streak (tied for the longest under Sirianni), may create the desperation necessary for Sirianni to let Mannion open up his entire playbook.
It certainly makes sense for Roseman to pick up the phone and call around the league to see what top-flight backup quarterbacks are up for grabs. The problem is that many of the NFL's more experienced backup quarterbacks play for fellow NFC contenders.
The 5-0 San Francisco 49ers likely won't trade Mac Jones to the Eagles. The same goes for the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings and former Philadelphia starter Carson Wentz , and the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (3-2) aren't shipping Drew Lock out east either. No way the Green Bay Packers (3-2) part with Tyrod Taylor to help out Philadelphia.
A realistic one-season target could be Cincinnati Bengals backup quarterback Joe Flacco , an alum of Audubon High School just over seven miles down the road from Lincoln Financial Field (the home of the Eagles). Flacco is 41 years old, but the ex-Super Bowl MVP proved he can be a steady stand-in when needed. He exploded for 342 yards passing and three touchdowns on 31-of-47 passing in a 33-31 "Thursday Night Football" victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 7 last season. He followed up that effort by going toe-to-toe with Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears in Week 9, throwing for a career-high 470 yards, four passing touchdowns and two interceptions in a narrow defeat. He is very comfortable simply getting the ball to his playmakers and letting them do the rest at this age.
If Cincinnati won't part with its Joe Burrow injury insurance plan, then it's worth seeing what backup quarterback Tanner McKee can do. The 26-year-old…

title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs files lawsuit against Wisconsin police department to block release of video
summary: The NFL is seeking the footage as part of its personal conduct review, leaving the running back on the commissioner's exempt list with no timetable for a return
full_text:
Josh Jacobs doesn't want any of the key evidence from his criminal case to be released, and to make sure it stays under lock and key, the Packers running back has filed a lawsuit against the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department in Wisconsin in an effort to permanently block access to the evidence, which includes an alleged video of the incident.
According to the lawsuit, which was obtained by ABC-7 in Wisconsin , Jacobs and his legal team listed a multitude of reasons why the evidence shouldn't be released. For one, Jacobs said he wanted to protect the identity of the woman involved in the May 23 altercation. After being charged in the incident, the Packers running back eventually pleaded no contest to two misdemeanors back in September .
Jacobs' legal team argued that releasing the evidence and video could lead to unwanted public attention for the woman, known as ANM in court documents.
"ANM is a crime victim who seeks closure, not public attention. ANM is not publicly known by her identity and has deliberately avoided public discourse concerning the underlying incident," the lawsuit states. "Public release of records that identify, depict, locate or disclose sensitive information concerning ANM would force unwanted exposure upon her and risk revictimizing her through new public scrutiny."
Jacobs' legal team also mentioned that releasing the video could open the door to possible robberies at his place of residence.
"Public sports figures have been targeted for robbery and related property crimes," the lawsuit states. "The public availability of Plaintiff's schedule or travel information increases the risk that persons could identify periods when Plaintiff is away from home and use released information concerning the residence, garage, access points, security arrangements, or property to target the property."
The key piece of evidence here is the video. After Jacobs pleaded no contest in the case on Sept. 10, there was some speculation that the NFL might soon reinstate him or at least hand out a suspension so he would know how many games he could expect to miss, but that hasn't happened. Instead, the league has kept him on the commissioner's exempt list and one reason for that is likely due to the existence of the video. The NFL wants to see it, but hasn't been able to yet.
The league has filed a public records request to obtain the video, but it still hasn't been provided.
Back in 2014, the NFL suspended Ray Rice for two games after he was arrested for assault. However, that turned into an indefinite suspension after an alarming video of the incident was released . Due to that situation, it seems likely that the league won't make a decision on Jacobs until it gets a chance to see the video.
In a statement on Oct. 11, the NFL wouldn't even offer an estimate on when a decision might be made about Jacobs' playing future.
"The matter remains under review of the personal conduct policy. There's no timeline," the league said in a statement to USA Today .
As for the evidence in the case, it had been sealed, but back on Sept. 23, a judge's order lifted the temporary restriction with the understanding that the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department would "apply a balancing test between the rights of the public, the defendant and the victim in deciding whether to release the records."
That ruling opened the door for the video to be released, but Jacobs' lawsuit has closed that door. At least for now.
What this all means for the Packers is that Jacobs is going to remain sidelined until the situation gets resolved. Although Jacobs will continue to get paid while he's on the commissioner's exempt list, he's not eligible to practice or play in any games. And since there's currently no timeline for a resolution, it's impossible to say when Jacobs will be back on the field.
In five games without Jacobs this season, the Packers have averaged just 60.4 yards per game on the ground, which ranks dead last in the NFL by nearly 20 yards per game.
author: John Breech

title: Jalen Hurts ruled out of Eagles' Week 6 matchup vs. Panthers due to superficial blood clot
summary: A follow-up ultrasound this week revealed movement in the clot, which was originally discovered before the London game
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles will be without their starting quarterback this Sunday against the Carolina Panthers , as the team has ruled out Jalen Hurts due to a superficial blood clot.
On Thursday, the Eagles announced that it was believed that Hurts suffered a calf injury during the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . After the team traveled to London for their Week 5 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars , Hurts underwent an ultrasound that revealed a blood clot. The Eagles' medical staff and doctors concluded Hurts was safe to suit up and play, but did inform the league office about the situation.
During a follow-up ultrasound on Wednesday of this week, the staff discovered movement in Hurts' blood clot, which led the team to rule him out for Sunday.
Read the Eagles' full statement below:
"On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report.
"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia.
"Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter.
"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."
This is something that will have to be monitored closely, and it could force Hurts to miss more than one game. Just hours before the Eagles discovered movement in the blood clot, Hurts addressed the "calf injury" that led him to be listed on the injury report last Friday and on Wednesday.
"It was a very unique experience, to say the least," Hurts said. "I don't want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game."
The Eagles did not go into detail about the clot, but this could be classified as "superficial thrombophlebitis," per Harvard Health Publishing . This is different than "deep vein thrombosis," which is a much more serious condition that requires anti-clotting drugs. We've seen several cases of deep vein thrombosis in the NBA , including with Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama, who missed the final 30 games of the 2024-25 season after doctors discovered deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder. As for superficial thrombophlebitis, Harvard Health Publishing says it can improve over the course of one week to several weeks. Each case is different.
With Hurts out, Tanner McKee is expected to start under center for the Eagles. He's 1-1 in his two career starts over the last two years and has played in a total of six NFL games . In the 2024 regular-season finale, the former sixth-round pick out of Stanford impressed in a 20-13 win over the Giants. McKee completed 27 of 41 passes for 269 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions.
Philly also has rookie Cole Payton on the roster. He was selected in the fifth round of this year's draft out of North Dakota State.
While the Eagles just released Andy Dalton last week, NFL Media reports that the veteran is an option to return. He's reportedly been in contact with a few teams, but he's familiar with Nick Sirianni's offense if the Eagles decide to go that route.
Through five games, Hurts has completed 57.8% of his passes for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions in a 2-3 start. Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in London snapped a franchise-record streak of 76 games where the Eagles were .500 or better, per CBS Sports Research.
The last time the Eagles were under .500, Jason Kelce was the starting center, A.J. Brown was on the Tennessee Titans , Aaron Rodgers was still with the Green Bay Packers winning MVPs, and Tom Brady was in his second-to-last NFL season.

title: Tyreek Hill rumors: Do Chiefs even have room for WR after reworking record-breaking offense?
summary: The Chiefs got their mojo back thanks to Kenneth Walker III, but they are still missing one thing
full_text:
We should have never doubted the Chiefs . But some of us did, including myself, who predicted they would miss the playoffs again in my season preview bold predictions column.
One month into the season, it's already abundantly clear the Chiefs are once again a Super Bowl contender as they've raced off to a 4-0 start.
Their defense has been better than expected even after losing their top two corners, and the addition of Kenneth Walker III has completely transformed their offense, which may still have a hole to fill. There are rumors that Kansas City is interested in bringing back its former WR Tyreek Hill to fill that void, but do the Chiefs need him, or even have room for him? Let's take a look.
The Chiefs were an offensive juggernaut in the first five seasons of the Mahomes era, featuring home runs to Tyreek Hill and YAC for days from Travis Kelce . They evolved into a death by a thousand cuts, ranking 19th in scoring over the past three years. Now, they look like the perfect offense in 2026. Downhill running and play action to combat defenses sitting back to limit big plays.
The Chiefs' new identity is a masterpiece, leading to an offensive renaissance. It's the mesh point when Patrick Mahomes is about to hand off to Walker that is painting defenses into a corner. Pick your poison. Lay back in coverage, and Super Bowl MVP Walker will bludgeon you. Cheat vs. the run and three-time Super Bowl MVP Mahomes will carve you up with play action.
This was the vision when you pair up a Super Bowl MVP combo at QB and RB for the first time since Troy Aikman and Emmitt Smith. You get a lethal play-action combination, the foundation for perhaps a reimagined Super Bowl run.
Over half of the Chiefs total yards are coming from Mahomes play-action passes and Walker runs this season — 57% to be exact. Only one duo has accounted for more in a season in the past 15 seasons: Ryan Tannehill and Derrick Henry in 2020.
Mahomes and Walker have combined for the most play-action passing and rush yards by a duo through four games (944) since Jared Goff/Todd Gurley in 2018 (1,032).
2018 Jared Goff/Todd Gurley ( Rams )
2026 Patrick Mahomes/Kenneth Walker III (Chiefs)
2012 Robert Griffin III/Alfred Morris (Washington)
2016 Matt Ryan/DeVonta Freeman ( Falcons )
2013 Peyton Manning/Knowshon Moreno ( Broncos )
The Chiefs average 7.1 yards per play when Mahomes attempts a play-action pass or when Walker runs the ball. The NFL record for yards per play in a season, regardless of play type, is 7.0 by the 2000 Rams.
It's all a byproduct of a historic start by Walker and his violent running style. He has forced the most missed tackles (42) by any player through four games in the past 10 seasons. He's the third RB in NFL history with 130+ rush yards per game and 6.0+ yards/rush during a 4-0 start. The others? They are on most people's RB Mount Rushmore: Jim Brown (1958 & 1963) and Emmitt Smith (1995).
At this rate, he could be one of the most important offseason moves ever. Remember, the Chiefs went completely against their identity with this move. They made Walker the highest-paid free agent RB ever ($14.4M per year) after ranking 15th or worse in cap spending on running backs every season from 2018-25. Now, Walker is on pace to be the Chiefs' first 1,000-yard rusher with Mahomes ... by Week 9!
Kansas City has leaned into its newfound success by going under center on 42% of its plays, by far the highest in the Mahomes era (25% is next highest). It's been the perfect counterpunch for how defenses have evolved to slow down Mahomes. Now, he's seeing more base defense and more loaded boxes this year, a sight for sore eyes.
On a per-play basis, the Chiefs are actually better this year (0.15 EPA per play) than their first five seasons in the Mahomes era (0.14 EPA per play).
This is the most complete offense they've ever had with Mahomes, but there is one missing piece: a deep threat. The Chiefs are reportedly very interested in a reunion with Tyreek Hill to help there.
Most signs point toward this move. The Chiefs' best home run threat, Tyquan Thornton , dislocated his ankle in Week 4, which puts the rest of his season in doubt. Plus, Mahomes' connection with Xavier Worthy has never materialized. Mahomes is 8-for-37 targeting Worthy on deep balls, the worst completion rate (21.6%) among 38 duos with 25+ targets since 2024. An already thin WR room could take another hit at any moment, too, based on Rashee Rice's track record.
Mahomes led the NFL with 41 touchdown passes on deep balls from 2018-21. He had just SEVEN in four-plus seasons since. Aidan O'Connell has more in that span (eight) for crying out loud! That's the Tyreek Hill effect.
A reunion with Hill is a great fit on paper, but there are so many questions swirling around him:
If the Chiefs can somehow answer yes (or maybe) to all three questions, then what would prevent them from reuniting with Hill? Character concerns? That won't stop them. They brought back Kareem Hunt .
If they did sign Hill, I wouldn't doubt them. I've done that before, and I learned my lesson.

title: Seahawks and Broncos set for rare uniform matchup on Thursday night: This almost never happens in NFL
summary: Neither team will be wearing a white uniform on Thursday night
full_text:
The best uniform battle of the season will be going down on Thursday night in Denver. The Broncos will host the Seahawks in a Week 6 game that will feature something rarely ever seen on the field: Both teams will be wearing colored jerseys.
If you've ever watched the NFL before, you've probably noticed that there's almost always one team wearing white in every game, but that won't be the case in Denver. Both teams will embrace the unofficial Throwback Thursday theme this week by wearing a colored throwback jersey.
The Broncos will be wearing their throwback Orange Crush uniforms for the game. This will mark the sixth time that the Broncos have worn the orange throwback since their return in 2024, and they've gone 5-0 in them.
On the Seahawks' end, they'll wear a royal blue uniform with a silver helmet that's a throwback to the 1990s. The Seahawks wore these throwbacks in three different regular-season games during their Super Bowl-winning 2025 season.
Let's take a look at the uniform matchup.
Throwback Thursday at our 🏠 pic.twitter.com/d6rTpEu5MZ
These are two of the most iconic throwback uniforms in the NFL, and when the teams take the field, it will be color vs. color in what will easily be the best jersey matchup of the year.
A classic matchup. pic.twitter.com/4yhRJSM19f
The Seahawks will actually be rocking their royal blue throwback jerseys in back-to-back games as they'll also be wearing them in Week 7 against the Chiefs . However, Kansas City will be wearing white, so we won't be getting a color vs. color game two weeks in a row.
It's rare to see a color vs. color game in the NFL. Although the league embraced the theme during the Color Rush years from 2015-18 — a span that featured multiple color vs. color games — the Broncos-Seahawks game will mark just the fourth time since the start of the 2021 season that we've seen a color vs. color game in which neither team wore a Color Rush uniform.
In fact, this matchup will mark just the second time since the start of the 2024 season that the NFL has given us a color vs. color uniform game. The last time it happened came in Week 15 of the 2025 season when the Falcons wore black against the Buccaneers , who wore their iconic Creamsicle jerseys.
Before that, the last color vs. color game came in Week 8 of the 2023 season. That game also involved the Falcons when they wore black against the Titans, who wore their baby blue Oilers uniforms .
If you want to get technical, you could argue that black isn't a color (just ask Adobe ). If that's the case, then Broncos-Seahawks will be the first true color vs. color game — one that doesn't involve a black jersey — in four years. The last time we got one came in Week 8 of the 2022 season, when the Bears wore orange against the Cowboys, who were suited up in their navy blue jerseys .
Run it up the gut and break free! @dak 📺: #CHIvsDAL on FOX 📱: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/QMxVpZl61r pic.twitter.com/AzPBuui2VM
The fact that the Broncos and Seahawks will both wear their throwbacks against each other on Thursday night is fitting— these two teams used to be in the same division. From 1977 through 2001, the Seahawks were in the AFC West, so the teams will renew an old rivalry while wearing throwback uniforms that honor the era.

Every week during the NFL season, we rank all 32 starting quarterbacks. The ranking is handled by Garrett Podell, and I have to say, I'm very happy with his ranking this week, so I'm going to share it with you. I probably also would have shared it even if I didn't like it, but we don't have to worry about that.
The reason I like this week's ranking is that Garrett has Jared Goff in his top three, and Goff was my preseason pick to win MVP. Was it a crazy pick? Yes, but it doesn't look so crazy now.
Here's a short explanation from Garrett of how his QB ranking works: "These rankings are fluid and designed to tell the story of each starting quarterback's respective rise and/or fall throughout the season."
Basically, this ranking isn't based on what any QB has done in the past; it's only based on what they've done this year.
After five weeks of action, let's check out the top three names on the list:

After the 49ers ' 32-29 win at Seattle in Week 5, Brock Purdy (189 yards passing, two touchdowns and his first interception of the season on 19-of-29 passing) enters Week 6 as the NFL leader in touchdown passes (13), passing success rate (57.9%), expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.37) and sack rate (2.1%). Mahomes still leads the league in both completions (23) and passing touchdowns (five, tied with Aaron Rodgers ) outside the pocket despite not playing last week. He also ranks in the top 10 in the NFL in both passer rating (106.2, fifth) and EPA per dropback (0.19, ninth). 3. Jared Goff, Lions . The Lions QB has 12 passing touchdowns, one behind Purdy for the league lead, and zero interceptions in 2026. That is tied for the most passing touchdowns without an interception by any quarterback through the first five games of a season in NFL history, along with Russell Wilson in 2019. His 1,485 yards passing — second in the NFL behind Matthew Stafford 's 1,572 — rank as the third-most without an interception through the first five games of a season in NFL history. Goff is playing like a top-three quarterback in football entering his bye week.
Garrett ranked every starting QB in the NFL, and if you want to see his full list, you can do that here .

Also, there's a very real chance we could see two divisions — NFC South and NFC East — crown a champion with a losing record.

title: Bills' Bradley Chubb reveals what he said that led to Alaric Jackson punch and suspension
summary: Chubb was trash-talking Jackson after the Bills' Monday night win
full_text:
Los Angeles Rams tackle Alaric Jackson was suspended by the NFL earlier this week for punching Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb during a postgame altercation following the Bills' overtime win on "Monday Night Football." Jackson was initially suspended for two games, but hearing officer Derrick Brooks reduced the suspension to one game on appeal.
Jackson was trading jerseys with Buffalo defensive lineman Deone Walker when Chubb appeared to walk over and say something to Jackson. Jackson was apparently upset by whatever, and he walked straight over to Chubb and started an altercation. The two started yelling at each other before Jackson swung at Chubb.
Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe
While Chubb was relatively tight-lipped about the incident when asked about it following the game, he had more to say on Wednesday.
"I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb told reporters, per ESPN . "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.'
"He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."
Chubb played 66 snaps against the Rams and lined up on the right side of the defensive line 49 times, meaning he was matched up with Jackson (the left tackle) for approximately 75% of his snaps on Monday night, per Pro Football Focus. We unfortunately don't have data on how often the Rams provided chips or help to Jackson when matched up with Chubb, but according to Chubb, it was apparently quite a lot.
After the punch, Chubb's teammates pulled him back, and he refrained from any retaliation. But he said he's taking it as a learning experience.
"Me personally, I learned I'm either going to have my hands up or have my helmet on," Chubb said.
Chubb ended the game with two tackles, zero sacks and one pressure. He decided to assign the blame to the Rams devoting him extra attention, rather than a strong performance by Jackson. Jackson, clearly, overreacted to that claim, and now he'll have to sit out a week to learn his lesson.

title: Brewers bash champion Dodgers to brink of NLCS sweep; CBS Sports Preseason All-America team revealed
summary: Plus, A.J. Brown is one of several injured NFL stars would could return soon
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.
That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh .
As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.
When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference , it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.
Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.
Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.
It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.
Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault , making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko . After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.
Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.
Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.
Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table . If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?
Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons . After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

title: NFL reduces suspension of Rams' Alaric Jackson for punching Bills' Bradley Chubb
summary: Alaric Jackson hit the Bills' pass-rusher with an apparent sucker-punch following Buffalo's wild Monday night win
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills picked up one of the wildest wins of the season on Monday night with an overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams , and somehow, things actually got even wilder after the game. Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb and appeared to make contact with his face.
The NFL initially suspended Jackson two games for the incident. However, Jackson appealed the suspension, and it has been reduced to just a one-game ban. He will be eligible to return to the active roster on Monday, Oct. 19, which sets him up to miss the Week 6 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals and be eligible to return for the Week 7 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders .
Following Buffalo's 37-34 win, several players from both teams stayed on the field to do a jersey exchange, and that's when the drama started. Jackson was trading his jersey with Buffalo's Deone Walker , and while that exchange was going on, Chubb was talking trash to Jackson.
The Rams' offensive lineman clearly didn't like what Chubb had to say because he walked straight over to the Bills' pass-rusher and got in his face. Jackson and Chubb then started yelling at each other, and that's when things got ugly.
At that point, the two players had to be separated by their teammates. You can see a video of the incident below.
Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe
"After the game, as players were shaking hands and exchanging jerseys, Jackson struck Buffalo linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face after a brief confrontation, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to 'any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship,'" the NFL said in a statement.
As you can see, Jackson's punch was pretty blatant, and the suspension is unsurprising given the historical precedent for that punishment.
During the 2025 season, Lions safety Brian Branch got hit with a one-game suspension for instigating a post-game fight following a loss to the Chiefs . That altercation actually took place on Oct. 12, 2025, exactly one year before Jackson's punch.
Jackson was suspended for two games in 2024 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, so this is not his first time standing under the league's watchful eye.
Based on the postgame video, it appears that Chubb was talking trash to anyone and everyone.
Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb had to be restrained by teammates following Monday night’s game against the Rams. pic.twitter.com/f5ltQs1xin
After he left the field, Chubb was asked about the altercation.
"Just emotions. You know what I mean," Chubb said of what happened, via the California Post . "Emotional game. It was a close game."
In the video, you can see that Chubb put his hand in Jackson's face just before Jackson threw the punch and that may have instigated the situation.
"They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back, so I just chilled," Chubb said.
Chubb was also asked if he was quarreling with anyone specifically and it appears that Jackson wasn't the only Rams player he was talking trash to.
"It was just the whole team," Chubb said.
Chubb finished the game with just two tackles, but his team won and that's what matters.
author: John Breech

title: Revisiting the Micah Parsons trade: Who got the better of the deal between Cowboys, Packers?
summary: It hasn't been a lose-lose situation, but it's not going the way either team planned
full_text:
Just over one year ago, the Packers visited the Cowboys in one of the most anticipated early-season games in recent memory: Micah Parsons ' return to Dallas a month after one of the most stunning trades in NFL history.
It didn't disappoint. Jordan Love and Dak Prescott combined for 656 passing yards and seven total touchdowns, Parsons had a crucial sack, and the game ended in a 40-40 tie.
Parsons, still recovering from tearing his ACL late last season, won't be available to welcome his former team to Lambeau Field this week. It's a crucial contest for both teams, with Dallas at 2-3 coming off an embarrassing home loss to the previously winless Buccaneers and Green Bay 3-2 after a big win over the Bears .
So now, 13 and a half months after an all-time blockbuster move, we revisit how both teams fared.
The lead-up to the trade was nearly as dramatic as the trade itself. Months of back-and-forth between Parsons and Jerry Jones. Quips from CeeDee Lamb , Prescott and Stephen Jones (Jerry's son). Parsons' trade demand. Jerry Jones saying he hadn't talked to Parsons' agent. A war of words between the owner and said agent. And finally, on Aug. 28, the trade.
Parsons' injury complicates things, but early on, it was a win for the Packers. Entering a Week 15 matchup with the Broncos last year, Green Bay was 9-3-1 and looked very much like a Super Bowl contender on both sides of the ball.
Parsons had 12.5 sacks in just 14 games, despite a slow ramp-up period to start the season. Parsons was so good, in fact, that he finished as a first-team All-Pro despite missing the final three games of the season.
But that one fateful misstep while trying to sack Bo Nix ... The Packers crumbled, not just on that day, but during the rest of the season. The loss to Denver was the first of five straight (including a playoff collapse against the Bears) to finish the year. The Packers went from fifth in yards per play allowed to 26th. Their sack rate went from 14th to dead last.
The Packers have righted the ship after an ugly 1-2 start this season, but the wins have been over the Buccaneers, headed by undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels in his first NFL start, and the Bears without Caleb Williams . Issues remain, and injuries on defense are piling up. Much hinges on how and when Parsons returns. If he looks like his old self and the offense can prove its progress last week was no fluke, the Packers are a playoff team. But if Green Bay can't return to the postseason, there will be big questions ahead of what should be an all-in 2027.
ACL tears can't be foreseen, unfortunately, but they do happen. It's just a really unfortunate injury that leaves us wondering "What if?" from last season and wondering what it will look like later this season.
The Cowboys, meanwhile, haven't shown any signs of being a winner — whether this trade or on the field — since the Parsons blockbuster. They went 7-9-1 last year and are 2-3 this year. The defense remains one of the worst units in the league.
As it turns out, replacing a historically great pass rusher isn't easy.
In the short term, Jones defended the trade by lauding Clark and saying he could use the extra draft capital acquired to aggressively pursue another big name. They did just that, acquiring Williams at the trade deadline.
The issue? Clark and Williams have proved more "name" than "game." That was always the way it was trending for Clark. Though "three-time Pro Bowler" sounded nice attached to Clark's name, it was clear he was no longer that caliber of player. After 7.5 sacks in 2023, he had one in 2024.
Clark has three sacks in 22 games with the Cowboys, including zero this season. His 6.3% pressure rate is on pace to be the worst of his career, too. Out of 28 interior defenders with at least 200 snaps played, Clark is 22nd in PFF's grades. He is, at best, an average starter.
The Williams trade and subsequent three-year, $105.9 million extension he signed this offseason look like questionable decisions at best. At the very least, he, like Clark, isn't producing at his peak level. The issue? The Cowboys paid for — in terms of trade compensation and contract extension — a player at his peak.
Long story short, the Cowboys hailed Clark as a Pro Bowler and Williams as a superstar. That was true in the years before Dallas acquired them, but it hasn't been true since.
Lawrence, whom the Cowboys acquired in the first round of the 2026 draft after a Packers trade back, has flashed in limited snaps. Still, he doesn't project as a massive needle-mover for a team trying (and so far failing) to compete for a Super Bowl. You know who a massive needle mover was? Micah Parsons.
This offseason alone, the Cowboys brought in ...
They also traded for Joey Porter Jr . a couple of weeks ago, though it's still too early to draw any conclusions there.
Simply put, the Cowboys have failed to replicate Parsons' star talent (Williams was their big attempt) or improve the product around the gaping hole Parsons' departure left. Their Super Bowl aspirations are being destroyed by a bottom-of-the-barrel defense ... again.
When it comes to just Packers vs. Cowboys, the Packers are the "winner" of this deal. Simply put, if you could have the Packers' defense with Parsons or the Cowboys' defense as currently constructed, it's the Packers by a landslide. Parsons' return to full health is obviously a big question, but he is still just 27 (another reason the Cowboys' move looks worse in hindsight) and should be a force for many more years.
When we throw the Jets into the equation, there becomes a clear winner. When the Cowboys acquired Williams, they sent the better of their two 2027 first-round picks — either their own or the Packers' from the Parsons trade — to New York. The Cowboys probably figured those would be late first-round selections. But if the draft were held today, they would be sending the ninth pick to New York.
The Jets also have their own 2027 first-round pick and the Colts ' 2027 first-round pick from the Sauce Gardner trade.
The pressure is always on for the Cowboys. It's on even more so when they're losing, and even more more so when they're losing after they've gone all-in on winning. The Jets' front office will gladly watch both the Packers and Cowboys struggle to find consistency, knowing it could reap a big reward.

title: Super Bowl stock report for NFL Week 6: 49ers emerge as new favorites, Bears await Caleb Williams' return
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 5 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
Entering the 2026 NFL season, prognosticators had their choice of the two perceived NFC West frontrunners in projecting the eventual Super Bowl champion. The Los Angeles Rams were the popular pick because of their masterclass of an offseason, while the Seattle Seahawks were the logical "we can't bet against them until they give us a reason to" choice coming off their championship run.
Most everyone forgot about the other contender in football's strongest division.
Injuries derailed the San Francisco 49ers ' 2025 campaign, but perhaps the fact that Kyle Shanahan still managed to lead his undermanned squad to a 12-5 record and a playoff berth should have served as an indication of the dominance to come. They are still not completely healthy, yet they are off to a 5-0 start and have the inside track to a division title and the Vince Lombardi Trophy.
Perhaps their seemingly never-ending ailments will catch up to them again, but the same could be said for any team in the league. It is time to simply enjoy what the 49ers are doing and stop worrying about their ability to stay healthy. Frankly, they might just win the Super Bowl regardless of who is available. Through five weeks, it feels like their year.
Here is how the rest of the Super Bowl race shakes out as the season approaches Week 6.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
No matter how you slice it, the 49ers look like the best team in the NFL . They are one of two 5-0 squads and own the widest point differential at +61. Their offensive EPA/play ranks second, behind only the Buffalo Bills, while their defensive EPA/play allowed is the league's fourth-best mark. This is as complete a team as there is in pro football.
Most impressive are the contributions San Francisco continues to receive from its most experienced players. While an aging roster comes with its health issues, it also represents a collection of proven, veteran talent. Christian McCaffrey . Trent Williams . Fred Warner . Everyone is in vintage form, including Mike Evans , who has a strong case as the most impactful free agent acquisition of the offseason with his 326 receiving yards and three touchdowns. Even George Kittle has been as reliable as ever despite being a mere nine months removed from a torn Achilles. A supreme collection of talent paired with a highly renowned coaching staff makes the 49ers the complete package.
These 49ers appear better suited than previous iterations to not only reach the postseason but finally break through for the franchise's first Super Bowl victory in 32 years. They already have a win over each of the other teams in the NFC West, making them the clear-cut top dogs in a division that was expected to be a season-long brawl. If they can make the Rams look foolish and beat the Seahawks on the road, there is no team they cannot defeat on the path to a championship.
Would the Chicago Bears be 5-0 if Caleb Williams did not get hurt in Week 2? Suppose he stays on the field for that critical fourth-quarter drive in the 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He would have had at least two more looks at the end zone. If he were available in Week 5, the Bears probably would not throw three interceptions in a 31-7 rout at the hands of the bitter rival Green Bay Packers . That is all hypothetical, of course, but Williams' talent makes it fair to wonder.
Instead, the Bears are two games back of the NFC North lead and stand in the middle of the conference's slog of three-win teams. They seek a rebound effort on the heels of the second-worst loss of Ben Johnson's head coaching career. That will be harder to obtain with edge rusher Montez Sweat out for two games for a violation of the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy .
The good news (and Chicago needs some right now) is that Williams is on track to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons . His hamstring strain is behind him, which cleared the way for a return to practice on Wednesday. Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent kept the ship afloat but had clear limitations — most notably in the frustrating loss to the Packers — whereas Williams seems to be blossoming into a top-tier quarterback capable of leading his team deep into the postseason.
It was easy to sneer at the Pittsburgh Steelers in the offseason when they hired a past-his-prime coach, let Aaron Rodgers drag them along with his decision-making process as to whether to return for another year and got embarrassed by the Philadelphia Eagles on draft day. They say everything happens for a reason, and they might be onto something when it comes to the Steelers. All of those developments, somehow, seem to have played out perfectly.
The offense is cruising right now with Rodgers throwing for at least 235 yards in each of his last three games, and Jaylen Warren rushing for no fewer than 93 in that span. Rookies Max Iheanachor and Germie Bernard make it appear as though the Steelers actually benefited from the first-round snafu at the draft . McCarthy and Rodgers, despite their occasional butting of heads, are doing exactly what they did during their time together in Green Bay, while the defense does just enough to help them win or stay competitive. Last week's 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts was the best encapsulation of all that thus far in 2026.
The AFC North is anyone's for the taking, as all four teams are at least 3-2 and no better than 4-1. It will be as much of a grind as ever to take the division, but even if the Steelers fall short, they appear strong enough to compete for a Wild Card berth.
Thursday, 8:15 p.m., Prime Video
Either the Seahawks or the Denver Broncos will fall to .500 this week. That is not where either team envisioned standing through six games after their postseason runs a year ago. Seattle needs to get its ground game moving and has a prime opportunity to do so against the league's fourth-worst run defense, while Bo Nix — in the throes of a regression year — faces another difficult test in what is a gauntlet of a six-game start to the campaign.
Sunday, 9:30 a.m., NFL Network, stream on Fubo
It took remarkable special-teams execution for the Jacksonville Jaguars to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat in their first London game. They will need to execute better in the first 59 minutes of their second overseas contest to defeat a Houston Texans squad that is finally in the win column and ready to build momentum. The Jaguars might be the best Super Bowl contender outside of the league's top tier , and this is a chance to prove it against a division rival that should be better than its 1-4 record. Houston, on the other hand, needs every win it can find in order to pull off the rare feat of reaching the postseason after an 0-4 start.
Sunday, 1 p.m., Fox, stream on Fubo
There was a chance this would be a clash between backup quarterbacks given Williams' hamstring issue and the rib injury Michael Penix Jr . sustained on "Sunday Night Football," but both are on track to play . This game will be more about the running backs, though. The Bears and Falcons present the two most prolific rushing attacks in the NFL, and the Falcons need theirs to outperform the other in order to secure their first home win of the year.

summary: Could Tennessee notch its first win of 2026? Will a Packers' RB erupt?
full_text:
No, I'm sorry. I can't give you the winning numbers for the upcoming lottery. Oh, you didn't ask? My mistake. I figured you would, considering we basically predicted the future in this very column last week, and I assumed you thought I was some sort of sorcerer. Alas, I'm just a dude who knows way too much about football, despite what my 0-5 fantasy football team would have you think.
Our finger was on the pulse of some of the biggest developments of Week 5, and some even came before the action officially kicked off. In what felt like hours after last week's story was posted, word came down that Sean Payton was going to take over the offensive play-calling duties from David Webb. That was an angle we put in the crosshairs and predicted would come to fruition.
We were also right on target with Justin Herbert getting sacked a season-high five times, Nick Sirianni's seat reaching a fever pitch after a loss in London, and the San Francisco 49ers firmly establishing themselves as the new Super Bowl favorite. The only call we missed was Jacoby Brissett throwing for 350 yards. That said, he finished with a season-high 292 yards through the air, so the logic was sound.
So, what's left to do? Pat myself on the back? I already did that with this already-too-long lede. No, the only thing left to do now is roll up our sleeves, comb through the Week 6 slate, and identify some underrated storylines/performances that wouldn't shock us if they happened.
The Packers rushing attack has been nonexistent so far this season. As a team, they're last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and 31st in yards per carry (3.1). When it comes to Lloyd, Green Bay hoped he would be the main contributor after Josh Jacobs landed on the commissioner's exempt list, but he hasn't exactly answered the bell. Of the 36 running backs who have logged at least 40 rushing attempts so far this season, Lloyd is 36th in rushing yards and 35th in yards per carry. He's also last among those backs in yards per carry after contact.
And yet, it wouldn't surprise us if he went off in Week 6 to the tune of 100 yards on the ground. Why? Simple. He's playing the Dallas Cowboys .
Dallas has one of the worst defenses in the NFL coming into Week 6, and they've particularly struggled to stop the run. So far this season, the Cowboys are last in the NFL, allowing teams to pile up 168.4 rushing yards per game. Just last week, they let Bucs running back Bucky Irving run wild for 165 yards.
Gambling angle to note : MarShawn Llyod's Over/Under rushing yards prop sits at 40.5 (-112) to the Over.  Lloyd is +250 to reach 60 rushing yards, +610 to reach 80 rushing yards, and +1300 to rush for at least 100 yards (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
On the whole, Trevor Lawrence has played great this season. He has the Jags at 4-1 entering Week 6 with a healthy lead in the AFC South and is fourth in the NFL in passer rating. However, he could be in some trouble this week as Jacksonville concludes its two-week stint in London with a matchup against the Texans .
Houston has endured a miserable start to 2026, beginning the year 0-4 before finally notching a win last week against the Tennessee Titans . While no one will mistake that as a marquee victory, I do think it may have been a get-right spot for DeMeco Ryans' team, particularly on defense. They held the Titans to a field goal and sacked Cam Ward four times in the contest. Could that have been enough to wake what is unquestionably a supremely talented defense back up? If so, that's not great news for Lawrence.
In his career, Lawrence is 3-7 against the Texans and has thrown eight touchdowns compared to 11 interceptions. Houston is eighth in the NFL in pressure so far this season, so Lawrence could be under siege quite a bit in this game. When pressured this season, Lawrence ranks 18th out of 26 qualified quarterbacks in completion percentage (41.7%). To his credit, he does have a passer rating when pressured that squeaks in at 10th highest among those quarterbacks, but it's still just 66.1. Lawrence may also be fortunate that figure isn't lower, as his turnover-worthy throw rate when pressured is tied for the third-highest.
If Houston can get pressure, Lawrence will give the secondary chances to create turnovers.
Gambling angle to note : Texans ML is +120 (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
As crazy as it might sound when factoring in Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury in Week 2, the New York Giants are still atop the NFC East entering Week 6. Moreover, they hold a 1.5-game lead over the rest of the division, which is the largest division lead they've held since 2012. Don't be shocked if that jumps to a 2.5-game lead by the time the dust settles on Week 6.
New York is currently slotted as a home underdog to the Saints this Sunday, but the margin is razor-thin, with the line sitting at 1.5 and the Giants' moneyline currently priced in at -102. New Orleans is stumbling into this matchup, losing three straight to drop to 1-4 on the season, and Tyler Shough has started to come back down to earth.
After totaling 917 passing yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions over the first three weeks, Shough has thrown for just 382 yards, one touchdown and two picks over the past two games. When you factor that recent slump in with the fact that New Orleans could be looking ahead on its schedule to their Week 7 trip to Paris, France, against the Steelers , the Giants should be looked at as a live home dog.
Meanwhile, the Cowboys and Eagles (tied for second behind the Giants at 2-3) both have difficult matchups in Week 6. Dallas is heading into Lambeau Field as an underdog against the Packers, while the Eagles are coming back from London and hosting a Panthers team that was just on the bye. Despite that game being played in Philly, Carolina is the road favorite.
So, by the end of the weekend, we could see both the Cowboys and Eagles dropping to 2-4, and if New York can take care of business against New Orleans, it'd rather remarkably be 4-1-1 and have a growing lead in the division.
Gambling angle to note : A Giants, Packers, and Panthers moneyline parlay is +573 (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
I've written this in a couple of different spots, but it won't shock me if Tennessee finally gets into the win column this weekend. While I don't have them pulling off the upset in my official picks column, I do have them covering the spread as one of my five locks of the week .
Really, it's more of a play against their opponent, the Indianapolis Colts . The Colts' defense is 28th in the NFL in total yards allowed (384.2), so there's an opportunity here for this lackluster unit to prop up what is a bad Tennessee offense. Meanwhile, Indy's offense doesn't inspire much confidence. The defense ranks 29th in yards per play allowed (4.6), while Daniel Jones has registered more turnovers (7) than touchdowns (4) so far this year.
This is the type of recipe that cooks up upsets. The Colts may play down to Tennessee's level, and if Jones' turnover issues continue to plague him and the defense can't stop a nosebleed, it's a pretty light lift for Cam Ward to put points on the board.
Gambling angle to note : Titans ML is +260 (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
Pittsburgh's home/road splits are quite drastic this season. In the friendly confines of Acrisure Stadium, the Steelers are 3-0 and averaging 28 points per game. On the road, they're 0-2 and averaging just 13.5 points per game. While the Steelers haven't started a season 0-3 on the road since 2012, it's certainly within the range of possibilities in 2026.
Not only will they lack a home-field advantage in this game, but Pittsburgh will also be at a rest disadvantage against the Bucs, who played last Thursday. On top of that, Tampa Bay matches up pretty well against some key pieces of the Pittsburgh offense. Specifically, they've done quite well containing the run, allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game (72.8) and yards per rush (3.3) in the NFL…

title: NFL Week 6 upset alert: Can Titans beat TD-favorite Colts? Will rested Bucs upset Steelers?
summary: These favorites are not only at risk of not covering, but they could lose outright in Week 6
full_text:
No matter what you think going into a given contest, the beautiful thing about the NFL is that it largely doesn't matter once the game kicks off. At that point, anything can happen, which is why the league has us in a chokehold throughout the fall.
That said, as we roll along in a given season, the schedule begins to dictate where upsets could occur, simply due to the fact that one team may be a little more rested than the other, particularly as bye weeks come into play.
For instance, we see that this week , between the Panthers and Eagles . Philadelphia opened as a home favorite, but has since seen those odds flip. Why? In part, because Carolina is coming off its bye, while the Eagles are coming off an international game in London in Week 5. Even before getting into the head-to-head matchups on the rosters, that lopsided rest disparity could be a major factor.
While we won't highlight that game as one of our possible upset alerts, there are some rest components we'll highlight this week as we identify five favorites who could be on the brink of a surprise loss.
To steal a basketball analogy: Sometimes you just need to see the ball go through the net. Could that be the case for the Houston Texans defense? While the Titans provide little resistance to just about anyone, the Texans' defense put together its best effort of the season vs. Tennessee and helped Houston get its first win of the year. The unit held Tennessee to a field goal, a measly 3.2 yards per play average and sacked Cam Ward four times (three coming from Will Anderson Jr. ). I wonder if that was a little bit of a get-right game for what was a reeling Texans team. Pair that with the arrival of C.J. Stroud's Ohio State buddy, Marvin Harrison Jr. , and the vibes might be shifting in a more positive direction for Houston as it hops on a plane to London to face the Jaguars .
Jacksonville pulled a victory out of its hat in the first leg of its two-week stint in England, narrowly beating the Eagles. While it got the win, it didn't look great doing it. The Jags were way too cute in the red zone and did not score a touchdown on any of their three trips. If they play with their food like that again, Houston's defense could once again keep them out of the end zone.
Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence is 3-7 in his career against the Texans, throwing eight total touchdowns and 11 interceptions over those previous 10 games.
This is more about fading the Colts than it is buying stock in the Titans. This is a divisional matchup where I think the line is simply too big, and Tennessee could end up surprising some folks because Indy keeps them in it. I could see this Colts defense helping prop up what has been the worst offense in the NFL, as the Titans rank last in scoring (11.6) and total yards (246.4). For as bad as Tennessee's offense is, it gets a soft opponent in the Colts, who are 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6) and 28th in total yards allowed (384.2). If there was any week for Cam Ward and Co. to move the ball effectively, it'd be this one.
Meanwhile, Indy's offense hasn't exactly lit the world on fire either. Specifically, Daniel Jones is 2-3 as the starter, averaging just 5.8 yards per attempt, and he has more total turnovers (7) than touchdowns (4). As we've seen plenty of times from watching the NFL, the longer you keep an underdog hanging around, the more likely they are to steal the win.
Remember when we chatted about the schedule being a factor in some of these games? Well, this could be one of them. The Buccaneers could be a live home underdog for two key scheduling reasons. For one, Tampa Bay is coming off an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday. That gives them a straight-up rest advantage over the Steelers , who played on Sunday. Second, Pittsburgh has an international game in Paris against the Saints next week, and I'm curious whether or not they fall into the trap of looking ahead to that game while overlooking the 1-4 NFC South team.
Meanwhile, Tampa Bay might be well-equipped to slow down some of the key figures on Pittsburgh's offense. The Bucs have allowed the second-fewest rushing yards per game (72.8) through Week 5, which could help negate Jayen Warren's impact. As for Aaron Rodgers , the Steelers QB doesn't have the best splits against Todd Bowles over the course of his career as a defensive coordinator or head coach. Rodgers is 1-2 against Bowles' defenses and averages 6.4 yards per attempt, while his teams average just 16.7 points per game.
Another scheduling quirk to note in this one is that the Bills will be playing on short rest when they square off against the Raiders in Las Vegas. Not only did Buffalo play on Monday night, but it found itself in a track meet with the Rams . The Bills were able to pull out the overtime win, but the defense was on the field for a season-high 78 plays. That unit has already been reeling, allowing the fifth-most points per game (28.2) and the third-most total yards per game (388.6) in the NFL this season. If they're a bit fatigued on top of it, that could help the Raiders offense go toe-to-toe with Josh Allen .
I wonder if this could be a letdown spot for the Packers . They're coming off a dominant win against a division rival where they were home dogs at Lambeau Field. That has the winds hitting the sails a bit, but they do have a much tougher task this week against the Cowboys. Dak Prescott and the Dallas offense should provide more of a challenge than the seven points Chicago mustered with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum under center.
Meanwhile, the Cowboys will have the rest advantage over the Packers after playing last Thursday and losing to the Bucs at home.
The big concern with Dallas possibly pulling off the upset is, of course, their defense. It remains one of the worst units in the NFL, allowing the second-most total yards per game (395.4) in the NFL this season and the eighth-most points per game (27.2). What'll be interesting to see is who wins on the ground, specifically when it comes to the Packers' rushing attack and Dallas' run defense. The Cowboys are giving up the most rushing yards per game (168.4) this season, but the Green Bay offense is registering a league-low 60.4 rushing yards per game.
If the Packers continue to struggle to run the ball effectively, it takes away one of the key concerns for Dallas.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL Week 6 picks: Our experts face off on Seahawks at Broncos, Ravens at Browns and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games
full_text:
We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games.
We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime.
Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Dajani ( Seahawks -2.5): Through five weeks, I have only bet against the Denver Broncos once. It's an uncomfortable position to be in, since Bo Nix is "captain comeback." For example, I had zero doubt they would come back from down 16-0 against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3. Denver has the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025. However, I'm going to fade the Broncos in this spot for a couple of reasons.
One, Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties did not help anything against the Los Angeles Chargers . Getting this offense off the ground is, unfortunately, going to take some time -- and it probably won't happen against the No. 1 defense in the NFL. Secondly, the Seahawks have to be mad after that loss to the 49ers. Seattle has won five straight games following a loss, having not lost back-to-back games since 2024. The Seahawks have also won seven straight prime-time games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL.  … Prediction: Seahawks 23, Broncos 20
Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have resulted in the Broncos coming away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Patrick Surtain II here, which is obviously a problem against Jaxon Smith-Njigba .  … Prediction: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16
Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home.  … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18
Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20
Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back.  … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27
Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta.  … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17
Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20
Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped.  … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14
Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes…
