title: Tyson Bagent Week 5 QB Grade: Bears @ Packers Film Breakdown
summary: Well, remember last week when I ended this article by asking which version of Tyson Bagent would show up at Lambeau Field? We got our answer. And unfortunately, it was about as bad as it could have been. There was actually quite a bit of optimism surrounding the Bears entering Week 5. Chicago had won […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears leaves the field after a loss against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, remember last week when I ended this article by asking which version of Tyson Bagent would show up at Lambeau Field? We got our answer. And unfortunately, it was about as bad as it could have been. There was actually quite a bit of optimism surrounding the Bears entering Week 5. Chicago had won two straight games, two of them without Caleb Williams, and Bagent was getting something none of the Bears’ backup quarterbacks had really been afforded yet: a second consecutive start with a full week of preparation knowing the offense was his. Last week, I came away from the Jets game encouraged by some of the growth Bagent had shown since we last saw him start games in 2023. He looked more comfortable operating within structure. He was getting through concepts with more confidence, keeping the offense on schedule and, when the pocket stayed clean, was borderline automatic. Against New York, Bagent completed 21 of 23 passes from a clean pocket for 202 yards. There were warning signs, particularly when pressure arrived and with a handful of turnover-worthy throws, but overall it looked like a more polished version of Tyson Bagent. Against Green Bay? Almost all of those encouraging signs disappeared. Bagent completed just 12 of 21 passes for 87 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions, finishing with a 27.4 passer rating before being benched in favor of Case Keenum. One week after averaging 7.9 yards per attempt against New York, that number cratered to just 4.1 at Lambeau. And honestly, the box score doesn’t completely capture how difficult the afternoon was. Green Bay consistently sped Bagent up, forced him off his initial reads and made it difficult for Chicago to find any sort of rhythm offensively. The Bears finished with only 246 yards, averaged 3.6 yards per play and turned the football over five times in a 31-7 loss. That is about as sharp of a reversal from Week 4 as you’re going to find. Against New York, Bagent generally took what the structure gave him. Against Green Bay, he too often tried to manufacture answers that weren’t there. His first interception was a good example. After Green Bay opened the game with a touchdown, Chicago had an opportunity to answer, but Bagent tried to force the football to Luther Burden III over the middle. Javon Bullard got underneath the route, deflected the pass and Xavier McKinney came away with the interception. Green Bay took over in Chicago territory and quickly made it 14-0. After the game, Bagent acknowledged that he needed to trust his progression and work down to Colston Loveland rather than forcing the ball where he initially wanted to go. Chicago eventually put together a 16-play touchdown drive late in the second quarter to cut the deficit to 14-7, but that ended up being just about the only sustained offensive success the Bears found all afternoon. Bagent’s second interception essentially ended any realistic hope of a comeback. Green Bay initially showed what Bagent believed was a zero blitz before rotating into Cover 2 after the snap. Bagent recognized the change, but not quickly enough, forcing another pass over the middle that McKinney intercepted. Bagent’s explanation afterward was pretty simple: he was late, and he forced it. At that point, Ben Johnson had seen enough. Keenum replaced Bagent after three quarters, with Johnson later saying Bagent never seemed to find a rhythm and that the second interception played a major role in the decision to make a change. Keenum wasn’t able to rescue the offense either, eventually throwing an interception of his own and losing a fumble as Chicago finished the afternoon with five turnovers. This certainly wasn’t all on Bagent. The running game that controlled the Jets matchup never got going, while Jordan Love carved up Chicago’s defense for 367 yards and two touchdowns. Green Bay finished with 428 total yards and averaged an absurd 7.3 yards per play. Nobody wearing a Bears uniform is going to enjoy watching this tape. But for the purposes of this series, Bagent’s performance is where things get particularly ugly. Last week, I talked about legitimate signs of development. I thought he looked more comfortable within the offense, more confident in what he was seeing and better equipped to operate within his physical limitations. Sunday was a reminder of just how small the margin for error can be for Bagent. The accuracy wasn’t consistently there. The processing that looked improved against New York took a major step backward. He forced throws when Green Bay changed the picture, struggled when the defense sped him up and ultimately put the football in danger often enough that Johnson pulled him from the game. To Bagent’s credit, he didn’t run from it afterward, saying he couldn’t “ look any further than the mirror ” when evaluating what went wrong. That’s the response you want from your backup quarterback. It doesn’t make grading the tape any easier. I’ve charted plenty of bad quarterback performances since starting this project, but once everything from Sunday was graded and the necessary adjustments were applied, Bagent finished with the lowest adjusted game grade I have ever handed out. So…This should be fun. Let’s get into the numbers. Benchmarks Stat Formatting Key: This week we will be comparing Tyson Bagent’s week 5 start against Williams’ Season Totals and Averages. (Season totals are underlined , Season Averages in Italics , and this week’s stats appear in regular text.) C/A: 36/55 (65.5%) | 18/27.5 (65.5%) | 12/21 57.1% Yards: 407 | 203.5 | 87 Touchdowns: 4 | 2 | 0 Turnovers: 1 | 0.5 | 2 QB at Fault Sacks: 0 | 0 | 2 aDOT: 7.7 | 7.1 Passer Rating: 92.0 | 27.1 True Passer Rating : 113.4 | 10.1 Time to Throw: 3.34s | 3.17s Time to Pressure: 2.75s | 2.86s Pressure Rate: 41.57% | 24.00% On-Target Rate: 83.3% |60.0% Poor Play Rate / Big Play Rate: 7.5 % PPR / 5.0% BRP | 29.6% PPR / 0.0% BRP EPA per dropback: +0.31 | -0.41 ANY/A : 6.2 | -0.9 Game Scorecard The full grading sheet for each play can be found here. Game Notes Note: Last year, I included PFF grades in these breakdowns. With PFF continuing to expand its use of AI across its platform, and with my confidence in how accurately its grades reflect quarterback performance declining, I’ve decided to move away from them this season. In their place, I’ll be using PFN’s Impact Score , which will be notated as PFN on grading sheets moving forward. NFL Passer Rating / True Passer Rating / PFN Impact Score: 27.4 / 10.1 / 65.9 The NFL’s average passer rating through Week 4 sat at 92.2. For some added perspective, if Bagent simply threw every pass harmlessly incomplete without an interception, his passer rating would still be 39.6. His actual mark was 27.4. So, yeah… not great. A 10.1 TPR is an absolute disaster of a start. A lot has to go wrong to post a TPR this low. Bagent was inefficient over a decent-sized sample, took two sacks, threw two interceptions and generated almost nothing downfield. By my charting, he completed just one pass more than 10 yards downfield. All of that converged into a 10.1 TPR, the lowest mark I’ve recorded in any QB start I’ve graded. On the PFN scale, where 75 represents an average qualifying starter and 90 is elite territory, Bagent finished Week 5 with a 65.9 Impact Score, ranking 24th of 30 qualifying quarterbacks. The underlying numbers fell off a cliff as well. His EPA/dropback dropped from +0.22 in Week 4 to -0.41, while his CPOE fell nearly 20 percentage points, from +8.0% to -10.9%. His Week 5 EPA/dropback ranked 26th, while his CPOE ranked 28th of 30 qualifiers. His success rate also fell from 61.1% in Week 4 to 40.0% against the Packers. On-Target Throws: 2026 Average: 83.3% | Week 5: 60.0% Reminder: Completion…

title: Does Samaje Perine deserve a larger role at running back over Chase Brown?
summary: Samaje Perine was the Cincinnati Bengals’ leading rusher on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins, and he provided a spark that this ground game hasn’t had enough of so far this year. The veteran running back logged 14 carries for 68 yards during the game. That 4.9 yards per carry is the highest number for a […]
full_text: Samaje Perine was the Cincinnati Bengals ’ leading rusher on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins , and he provided a spark that this ground game hasn’t had enough of so far this year. The veteran running back logged 14 carries for 68 yards during the game. That 4.9 yards per carry is the highest number for a Bengals running back this season. Perine also added 2 receptions for 10 yards, and found the end zone for Joe Burrow’s second touchdown pass of the game. Chase Brown has not been able to get fully going consistently this year in the running game. He had 20 carries for 80 yards against Houston, and followed that up with a respectable 13 carries for 61 yards in Pittsburgh. Against Jacksonville in Week 4, he only ran the ball 9 times for a total of 10 yards. This week he ran the ball 13 times for 39 yards. One thing I still like about what Brown brings to the table is being a receiving threat out of the backfield for the Bengals. He hauled in three receptions for 21 yards against the Dolphins. One of those came on a play with Perine in the backfield, and a play-action fake to get Brown the ball out in the flat. He was able to make a guy miss and picked up the first down. Bengals are under-center, play-action to Perine, and they get the pass out in the flat to Brown who makes a guy miss for the 1st down. pic.twitter.com/2KYmfk8hM4 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 Perine, on the other hand, is never going to wow anyone with his speed or elusiveness ( except for the Chiefs in the 2021-22 AFC Championship ), but he is a dependable player who consistently moves the chains when given opportunities. His 14 carries on Sunday actually outnumbered the 13 carries he had during the first four games of the season. I think getting the two players closer to a 60-40 split on carries each game makes sense going forward. With that split, you can afford to give either guy closer to the 60% based on who has the hotter hand during that particular game. Do you think Samaje Perine deserves a larger role in the offense moving forward? Sound off in the comments. Samaje Perine vs. Miami 14 carries for 68 yards (4.9 YPC) 2 catches for 10 yards and a TD 1 magnificent beard pic.twitter.com/DESX3nT5WB — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 13, 2026

title: Amarius Mims is a top candidate for NFL Protector of the Year award
summary: For Cincinnati Bengals fans, few sights are more reassuring than Joe Burrow having time to throw. Amarius Mims is doing his part to make that happen, and his work is drawing national attention. In his Quarter-Season NFL Awards Rankings, ESPN’s Bill Barnwell placed Mims third in the race for NFL Protector of the Year, behind […]
full_text: For Cincinnati Bengals fans, few sights are more reassuring than Joe Burrow having time to throw. Amarius Mims is doing his part to make that happen, and his work is drawing national attention. In his Quarter-Season NFL Awards Rankings , ESPN’s Bill Barnwell placed Mims third in the race for NFL Protector of the Year, behind San Francisco tackle Trent Williams and Denver guard Quinn Meinerz. Barnwell described Mims as “arguably the best pass-protecting right tackle in the league.” According to Barnwell’s four-game assessment, Mims faced pass rushers one-on-one at the third-highest rate in the NFL. Despite that workload, he allowed only half a sack and two quick pressures across 169 pass-rush snaps. Those numbers matter for an offense built around Burrow’s ability to find the open receiver. As Barnwell explained, Burrow likes to have all five eligible receivers available in passing routes. When Cincinnati gives a tackle extra protection, that assistance generally goes to Orlando Brown Jr. on the left side, leaving Mims responsible for his assignment on the right. Every time Mims handles that assignment himself, the Bengals have more freedom to use their tight ends and running backs as receiving options. It gives Burrow another place to go with the football and gives the defense another player to account for. Mims also ranked 12th in run-block win rate in Barnwell’s assessment, providing another encouraging measure of his early performance. But there is still a long way to go. A ranking based on four games is an early checkpoint, and sustaining that level through a full season is the next challenge. But this is the kind of development Cincinnati needs. An offense with Burrow at its center depends on blockers who can hold up when defenses know a pass is coming. And, at least through the first four games, Mims was doing exactly that. It’s still early, but the Bengals already have a presence at right tackle who belongs in the conversation with the NFL’s best.

title: Bengals Film Room: Cincinnati’s goal-line stand vs. Miami Dolphins
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals held a 21-7 lead during the third quarter of the game against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. Miami ran for 69 yards on their second possession of the 2nd half, getting down to the 1-yard line. The Bengals were able to make a stand and held them to just a field goal […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals held a 21-7 lead during the third quarter of the game against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. Miami ran for 69 yards on their second possession of the 2nd half, getting down to the 1-yard line. The Bengals were able to make a stand and held them to just a field goal on the possession. Let’s take a look at the critical plays that helped them to do so. The Bengals brought in the beef defensively with the Dolphins starting at the 1-yard line. They had Myles Murphy, BJ Hill, TJ Slaton, Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, and Cedric Johnson all on the line. Even Joe Giles-Harris was up at the line a bit outside of those six guys. Murphy was able to knife through and get pressure behind the line, forcing Ollie Gordon to try and bounce the run to the outside. Demetrius Knight Jr. was able to come up from his linebacker position and make the tackle for loss. That play forced a 2-yard loss, moving the Dolphins back to their own 3-yard line. Myles Murphy with a tremendous play here to force Gordon to try and bounce this run outside pic.twitter.com/Yw3R87Wkvi — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 On 2nd-and-goal, the Dolphins went with play-action. The Bengals were not fooled, specifically Boye Mafe sticking with the tight end until Dax Hill could make his way over to help in coverage. Barrett Carter was another guy who read the play immediately. Carter did well to stay in front of the mobile quarterback Malik Willis. He didn’t bite on anything, and ultimately was able to sack Willis for an 8-yard loss on the play. Barrett Carter with the sack on 2nd and goal pic.twitter.com/In6Hemaiej — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 On 3rd down, the Bengals rushed just four, but were still able to generate some pressure from Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe. This forced Malik Willis to make a tough throw on the run. DJ Ivey was in good coverage and was able to knock the ball down, holding the Dolphins to just 3 points on the drive. Dexter Lawrence with some initial pressure forces a Malik Willis throw on the run and incompletion with DJ Ivey in coverage. Dolphins have to settle for a field goal after having the ball on the 1 yard line. pic.twitter.com/OEgatqbxsZ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 This allowed the Bengals to maintain a two-score lead at 21-10. The Bengals would go on to add to it with a Burrow-to-Chase touchdown later in the third quarter. They ultimately held on for a 35-28 victory over the Dolphins. A crucial goal-line stop was nice to see out of this Bengals defense.

title: Boye Mafe has been a fantastic NFL free agency signing for the Bengals
summary: On the first day of free agency in March, the Bengals made two splashes with signing edge rusher Boye Mafe and safety Bryan Cook. Both won Super Bowls with their previous teams, and both players are entering the prime of their careers. In particular, Mafe has given the Bengals exactly what they paid for… and […]
full_text: On the first day of free agency in March, the Bengals made two splashes with signing edge rusher Boye Mafe and safety Bryan Cook. Both won Super Bowls with their previous teams, and both players are entering the prime of their careers. In particular, Mafe has given the Bengals exactly what they paid for … and more. “Right now, it’s a mindset to go out there and show who I can be as a player,” Mafe said after Sunday’s win over Miami. “With the coaches trusting me to be that player, it’s up to me to uphold that in my end of the bargain.” Mafe signed a three-year, $60 million deal with the Bengals in free agency. Through five games, Mafe has three sacks, five tackles for loss, four quarterback hits, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one pass defensed. Sunday in Miami, Mafe had a sack, a tackle for loss, two quarterback hits, and a pass defensed. Mafe also pressured Malik Willis and forced a wobbly pass that Jordan Battle intercepted. “He has a lot of juice, man,” defensive tackle BJ Hill said. “He can get after the quarterback. He can do it all. He’s the guy you want on your team. I knew we had something special when he got here. He’s a different cat,” Hill said. “He’s just different. That’s all I can say. You’ll have to ask him. He’s different. You love to have that energy. You love having guys like that.” It’s also the stats you don’t see on Mafe that stand out. Mafe’s PFF grade Sunday was 88.0, the highest of his career. His second-highest was in Week 1 this season at 86.5. In addition, Mafe’s 77.1 pass-rushing grade is tied for 13th among 103 edge players who’ve played in at least 20% of their team’s defensive snaps. Among all NFL players, his 25 pressures rank sixth. Mafe is 27 years old, which is the same age Trey Hendrickson was when the Bengals signed him in free agency in 2021. But Mafe brings far more versatility than Hendrickson. He can defend the run, pressure the quarterback, and cause turnovers. Look no further than his strip-sack of Baker Mayfield in the fourth quarter of Week 1. “He’s willing to do anything,” Zac Taylor said about Mafe. “Stop the run. Drop. Rush. Rush inside … That didn’t surprise me. That’s what we were banking on, that he’d give you that type of effort. He’s completely bought in.” Finishing has been an issue for the Bengals’ defense in recent seasons. Who’s their closer? It’s a question we asked a lot in those recent seasons, but Mafe could be that for this team. “He has come in and been extremely competitive from Day 1,” said left tackle Orlando Brown Jr., who faced Mafe in 2023 when Mafe was with the Seahawks and played against him throughout training camp this summer. “He’s just a really good and smart football player who knows when to show up. What’s most impressive is some of the clean wins that he has. He figures out a way to finish. That’s a sign of a great defensive end. It’s crazy. I feel like he has gotten better even since he got here.” While Dexter Lawrence grabbed a lot of the headlines this offseason in the Bengals’ signings and trades, Mafe may turn out to be their most important signing. So far, the Bengals are getting a great return on investment with him.

title: Can the Browns defeat the Ravens? How about like this!
summary: The Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens square off this weekend in a key AFC North Division contest. The Pittsburgh Steelers are on the road against the […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens square off this weekend in a key AFC North Division contest . Currently, every team in the division has a positive record, with Baltimore on top with a 4-1-0 record. A Cleveland win would tie the Browns for the division lead. The Pittsburgh Steelers are on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers while the Cincinnati Bengals are on their bye week. RELATED: BROWNS, RAVENS LIST OF 36 INJURED PLAYERS Cleveland has done well hosting Baltimore in the past five years, going 3-2-0. So far this year, the Browns have not defeated a single team considered to be one of the league’s best teams, and essentially, the two contests against the Ravens are their only difficult challenges. Cleveland is playing the league’s “last-place schedule,” being pitted against the majority of division cellar-dwellers from last year. A split with Baltimore will become an advantage later in the season. The Ravens feature their usual ground-and-pound running game, featuring Derrick Henry, who is ranked #5 it total rushing yards this year. The Browns haven’t done well as far as stopping the run, so this may set up what this game is truly about. According to FOX Sports, Cleveland is ranked #18 against the run. Can the Browns defeat the Ravens? Here are a few ideas: Monken’s familiarity and the Browns’ receivers Cleveland head coach Todd Monken had run Baltimore’s offense for the past three years successfully. He knows every nook and cranny of this side of the ball. He understands the advantage of Henry running the ball, and that WR Zay Flowers is a league menace. But Monken has a few new tricks he can deploy. The Browns have a strong (enough) armed QB in Deshaun Watson. Baltimore’s defensive backfield can be beaten long, or spin the ball into intermediate zones quickly. The Ravens have given up 16 plays of 20+ yards and one that went for over 40 yards. Monken has a trio of very good receivers that are able to stretch the field, plus tight end Harold Fannin. Test the Ravens’ defensive backs early and often. A quick note: Watson is 2-0 against Baltimore at home. Ravens’ injury list Hate to see a team win by default, but this may become a reality with the Ravens. Currently, they have 19 players on their first injury report going into Week 6, according to Nikhil Mehta of Baltimore Beatdown . That is an army of players. The key players listed that remain questionable to play are QB Lamar Jackson, C Cam Jurgens, CB Marlon Humphrey, LT Ronnie Stanley, DT Calais Campbell, OG Andrew Vorhees, and LB Trenton Simpson. They added a few more on Thursday . Not great for Baltimore, but will take it. Last week, backup QB and former Brown Tyler Huntley played decently in Baltimore’s 30-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Home field advantage For whatever reason, the Ravens struggle playing in Cleveland. Even in victory games, things just happen. Baltimore has a history of getting involved in unpredictable and sloppy games when they should dominate the Browns. Strange things tend to happen. The “Factory of Sadness” is a real thing. Baltimore players getting hurt, defenders dropping interceptions, dropped passes, losing good leads going into the fourth quarter, and ugly losses. Not to mention, the Browns fans get up for Baltimore because they realize they are always in the division title mix. In 2024, Cleveland went 3-14-0, but beat the Ravens at home 29-24. The 33-31 win over Baltimore at home in 2023 became the 11 th win, which secured a playoff seed. A 7-10-0 record in 2022 included beating the Ravens 13-3 at home, just like the year before when Baltimore came into FirstEnergy Stadium and left town with a 24-22 late loss. title: Week 6 versus the Ravens is a litmus test for the Browns
summary: If you were to tell me that the Cleveland Browns would be 3-2 by the time they would face the Baltimore Ravens in Week 6, I wouldn’t have believed you. The loss to the New York Jets was predictable for those who saw it coming, but many believe that the loss was more of a […]
full_text: If you were to tell me that the Cleveland Browns would be 3-2 by the time they would face the Baltimore Ravens in Week 6 , I wouldn’t have believed you. The loss to the New York Jets was predictable for those who saw it coming, but many believe that the loss was more of a lost opportunity for the Browns to showcase that things have changed. Granted, this Cleveland team is young in terms of age and comes with minimal expectations . However, Sunday’s divisional tilt against the Ravens should be considered a litmus test. As of now, Baltimore looks to be the clear favorite to win the AFC North. On paper, the team appears to be better than last season. Quarterback Lamar Jackson is still there, but the question remains whether he will play this Sunday . Running back Derrick Henry is still an issue, and wide receiver Zay Flowers has started to emerge in Baltimore’s passing game. Flowers was added to the injury report on Thursday, something to watch. The Ravens offensive line, which has shuffled chairs in the interior, has some weaknesses that can be exploited. Defensively, the unit is talented, but like the offense, it has weaknesses that can be exposed. Baltimore is not a perfect team by any means, but they are the standard of what the Browns hope to be. It’s not a secret that the Ravens are a playoff-level team that can be a Super Bowl contender if everything clicks for them. For Cleveland, it’s more about proving that they can compete with the playoff-level teams, no matter who is on the field, in Week 6. It’s not a question of whether the Browns are ahead of schedule, but if they want to start entertaining the “is this team a playoff team” conversation, it starts on Sunday. It’s not a must-win for Cleveland, but they have to show they are competitive enough to hang with the upper echelon of the AFC. What would you think if the Browns beat the Ravens in Week 6? full_text: The Cleveland Browns are preparing to take on Todd Monken’s former team, the Baltimore Ravens . It will be the team’s second divisional matchup of the season, making a win crucial. Facing the 4-1 Ravens won’t be easy, and the Browns will need to make several key improvements to secure the win. The biggest concern heading into this week is which version of the offense will show up. Cleveland recorded just 198 net yards against the New York Jets, and that level of offensive production won’t cut it against Baltimore. The running game still hasn’t hit its stride, but this would be an ideal week for Judkins to take off, if he’s able to play . They also need to finish drives with touchdowns rather than settle for field goals. Lamar Jackson seems unlikely to play this weekend , and if he steps on that field, containing him will be one of the defense’s biggest challenges. Between Jackson and Derrick Henry’s ability to take over games, the Browns’ run defense will need to be dialed in. Henry is tough to contain, so the defense should aim to put the Ravens’ offense in difficult situations that limit his ability to dominate the game. Let me know what you think in the comments – What do the Browns need to do to bounce back against the Ravens?

title: Browns WR Jerry Jeudy ‘fits the bill’ as a trade target for a top team
summary: The NFL trade deadline is not until November 10th this year, leaving a lot of time and games on the schedule for rumors to come and go. Some rumors will occur, like QB Shedeur Sanders yesterday, for oddly specific reasons. Others, like those we’ve covered with WR Jerry Jeudy, DE Khalil Mack, and DE/OLB Josh […]
full_text: The NFL trade deadline is not until November 10th this year, leaving a lot of time and games on the schedule for rumors to come and go. Some rumors will occur, like QB Shedeur Sanders yesterday, for oddly specific reasons. Others, like those we’ve covered with WR Jerry Jeudy , DE Khalil Mack , and DE/OLB Josh Sweat , will occur due to team and player performance. Given how well rookie WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have looked and played, Jeudy’s future in Cleveland seems tenuous at best. The veteran has been a good influence on the younger players but only has one more year on his contract and isn’t being used regularly by the Browns. According to our Kansas City Chiefs site , Jeudy “most fits the bill for a Chiefs midseason trade” as the team continues to deal with injuries while being undefeated through five weeks: If Kansas City can send a Day 3 pick for the 27-year-old wideout, it could be a strong option to replenish the Chiefs’ playmaking for this season and the future without taking a huge risk. He is signed through the 2027 season, with a $13.4 million cap hit next year. Arrowhead Pride noted that former Cleveland wide receiver coach Chad O’Shea is now in the same role in Kansas City. That familiarity could help not only lead to a trade, but help Jeudy get adjusted to a new offense quickly. The Browns and Chiefs are familiar with working deals together, as the two teams combined on a deal near the top of the 2026 NFL draft , allowing Kansas City to move up a few spots to select CB Mansoor Delane . Getting a high Day 3 pick, opening up more snaps for the young players, and saving some salary cap space would be helpful for Cleveland, while the Chiefs would get another veteran receiver that QB Patrick Mahomes and HC Andy Reid could try to make the most of as they push toward another deep playoff run. summary: It is Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are coming off of a tough loss in the rain against the Jets. It’s one of those games that I can forgive them for because of the elements, but also, they were oh-so-close to being 4-1, which would’ve been incredible. Now, at […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 11: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns leads the offensive huddle during the third quarter of the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are coming off of a tough loss in the rain against the Jets. It’s one of those games that I can forgive them for because of the elements, but also, they were oh-so-close to being 4-1, which would’ve been incredible. Now, at 3-2, some of the national media has given them a cooler for their late-game mistakes, while still keeping them on the level of respectability. Overall, the Browns went up by 3.6 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 19.7 . Ranking-wise, that is still third in the division. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 19 (down 3 spots) They came back to reality some in the loss to the Jets. But at 3-2, they have to be thrilled with their start. ESPN – No. 23 (down 4 spots) Biggest issue on defense: Run defense The Browns’ defense rebounded after giving up 34 points to the Jaguars in Week 1, but the inability to stop the run has been a consistent theme this season. Cleveland is giving up 4.5 yards per attempt, the ninth-worst mark in the NFL. And its success rate on opponent rushes (52.8%) is the second-worst mark in the league. Tackling has been an issue; opponents are averaging 2.53 yards after contact per rush, which ranks 30th. NFL.com – No. 21 (down 4 spots) Cleveland’s method of leaning on defense and hoping the offense finds a fourth-quarter rhythm nearly worked out in the Browns’ favor, but a miserable sequence that included a regrettable-at-best approach while nursing a late lead, a botched snap on a punt and a disastrous final possession proved they can’t keep getting by with late-game heroics. They also still cannot run the ball, which won’t help matters in the future, no matter how effective rookie receiver Denzel Boston is in the second half. Sporting News – No. 20 (down 3 spots) The Browns came crashing down to earth around Deshaun Watson as he was denied a fourth consecutive fourth-quarter game-winning drive. Being pounded on the ground by the Jets was odd, too. Watson is on pace for 65 sacks after being dropped by the Jets eight times. That would be the most for him in his career, surpassing his second NFL season with the Texans, when he was sacked a league-high 62 times. Yahoo Sports – No. 22 (down 2 spots) The Browns were close to a much better day. Receiver Isaiah Bond was pressed into action after KC Concepcion’s concussion and he had a big drop in a big moments and once ran out of bounds when it seemed he could have pushed upfield for more yardage. One drop came in the end zone and another was on a second-and-19 that could have given the Browns a first down just ahead of the two-minute warning. Those plays were huge in a five-point loss. Still, the Browns failed to top 200 yards against a Jets defense that had just given up 492 yards to a Tyson Bagent-led Bears offense. Cleveland’s 3-1 start came with some close wins and the Browns were due some regression. Week 6’s game against the Ravens, who may be without Lamar Jackson, will be telling. Bleacher Report – No. 17 (down 5 spots) The Cleveland Browns are who we thought they were a few weeks ago. To their credit, they briefly held the lead in the fourth quarter Sunday. The defense is keeping the team in games week after week, but the offense remains a major weakness. Facing a Jets defense that the Chicago Bears dominated a week ago, the Browns did next to nothing. Bad weather or not, Cleveland managed just 198 yards of offense. There were no running lanes. Deshaun Watson was dropped a whopping eight times. After three straight wins, the Browns delivered an ugly, mistake-filled performance. Next week’s AFC North matchup against the Baltimore Ravens may not be a must-win, but Cleveland needs a strong response to bolster its credibility as a contender in 2026. USA Today – No. 16 (down 4 spots) Rookie WR Denzel Boston is leading the league with 20.6 yards per reception out of the gate − his three TD catches averaging 43.3 yards in length. full_text: Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images | Diamond Images/Getty Images The talk around the Dallas Cowboys after another disappointing start to the 2026 season remains rather pessimistic. But just a few days ahead of their trip to Lambeau to take on the Green Bay Packers, most of the conversations are centered around the hiring of long-time defensive coach Mike Pettine. With a new veteran defensive coach on staff, there is some hope that the Cowboys defense can turn things around. They will get a good shot on Sunday night to prove themselves against a solid Green Bay offense coming off the best game of their season so far. Christian Parker ‘likely’ to remain coaching on field, talks Mike Pettine hire – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com After Jerry Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that Christian Parker would be moving to the booth, both Parker and Brian Schottenheimer denied that rumor. With Parker still likely to be on the sideline, the question now is, where will Mike Pettine be? Earlier in the week, Cowboys owner/GM Jerry Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that defensive coordinator Christian Parker would be moving from the sidelines up to the coaches booth to call the defense. As the week has gone on, it appears that may not be the case. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Wednesday “none of those decisions have been finalized,” and Parker had a good chance to remain on the field. On Thursday, Parker reiterated that sentiment. “Still working through some of that, but [I’ll] most likely going to be down [on the field] still.” Parker said on Thursday. 2 Cowboys Miss Thursday Practice, DeMarvion Overshown Progressing In New Injury Report – Josh Sanchez, SI.com The Cowboys defense continues to be banged up, but it looks like they may get some reinforcements back in week six. After a nice showing in week five, Ameer Speed returns to the practice field in limited fashion, as well as Joey Porter Jr. While Cobie Durant is still not expected to return, the Cowboys secondary is inching towards full strength in the coming weeks. On Thursday afternoon, the Cowboys returned to the practice field and dropped their latest injury report . On Wednesday, five players did not participate in practice, but on Thursday, that number was down to two. The good news for Dallas is that starting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is making progress and taking a step toward returning to the field, while veteran linebacker Von Miller also returned after a rest day and cornerback Ameer Speed was upgraded to limited. The Cowboys’ plan to unleash first-round rookie Malachi Lawrence could mean time is running out for former All-Pro to make an impact – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports With Malachi Lawrence expected to see an uptick in playing time, someone’s playing time is about to take a hit. Which outside linebacker could see their role diminish with the Cowboys wanting to see more from their 2026 first-round pick? Schottenheimer did share some of the personnel plans, though. The biggest one involves first-round rookie EDGE Malachi Lawrence, and the short version is that he is going to play more. That shouldn’t be a surprise given how Lawrence has been playing. He got his first sack last week versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. His pressure rate of 14.3% in 2026 ranks him fourth among qualified NFL rookies per PFF , behind David Bailey (16.4%), Sonny Styles (15.0%) and Cashius Howell (14.8%). But the Cowboys’ plans to play him more raise a question I find fascinating: Where are Lawrence’s new snaps coming from? Brian Schottenheimer OK with Cowboys’ players-only meeting panned by Mike Tomlin – ESPN.com There has been a lot made of the report that the Cowboys defense had a “players only” meeting earlier this week. The meeting was heavily criticized by former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin on the “New Heights” podcast, but Brian Schottenheimer seems not concerned with the meeting. The players-only meeting recently held by the Dallas Cowboys ‘ defense has become such a topic around the NFL that even Mike Tomlin weighed in with a concerned response. But Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer is not pushing the panic button, saying that the meeting doesn’t bother him and that it “means everyone’s rowing in the same direction.” Dallas star linebacker DeMarvion Overshown revealed Monday that the defensive players held the meeting after last week’s home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Overshown said the players “went by bullet point, bullet point,” discussing whether they were meeting the team’s various standards. Cowboys at Packers: Matchups to watch in Week 6 – Brian Martin, Blogging the Boys After dropping their week five game to the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Cowboys are in a must-win scenario in week six heading to Green Bay. What are some of the key matchups the Cowboys will need to win, in order to come out with a road victory against a long-time NFC rival? The Packers are coming off a game in which they held D’Andre Swift to just 43 yards on nine carries and only allowed Chicago to rush for a total of 81 rushing yards. They’ll be hoping to do the same this week against Javonte Williams and the Cowboys. Williams probably has other plans. He’s been a touchdown scoring machine so far this year with six, but is currently struggling to find consistency as a runner, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry. If Williams has success on the ground, it should sway the game in Dallas’ favor.

title: 2026 Week 6 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: The Cowboys face a tough task on Sunday night in Green Bay. If they can pull it off, they’ll be 3-3 and right in the thick of both division and conference contention. But in addition to Dallas’ efforts, what else from the Week 6 schedule could improve our standing in the NFC East and the […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys face a tough task on Sunday night in Green Bay. If they can pull it off, they’ll be 3-3 and right in the thick of both division and conference contention. But in addition to Dallas’ efforts, what else from the Week 6 schedule could improve our standing in the NFC East and the NFC as a whole? Things are still fairly jumbled this early in the season. The 49ers and Vikings are pulling away from the pack with their 5-0 records, but no other NFC team has even four wins. The NFC East and South divisions are completely up for grabs, and the wild card race is anyone’s guess at this point. Things are starting to take shape as we get close to the midpoint of the 2026 season. Along with beating the Packers, here’s what the Cowboys need from Week 6 to help shape things in their favor. NFC East teams Saints d. Giants Panthers d. Eagles Commanders d. 49ers Winning the division is always the preferable path to the playoffs, so we’d love assistance from Carolina and New Orleans. The Giants have done well against weak competition so far this year, so the Saints may not be much help. But the Panthers have been solid on their way to 2-2, showing more than enough to threaten the Eagles. Philly still feels like more of the key rival in this year’s NFC East, so if we can only get one of these games to go our way, let it be that one. With Washington at 1-3-1 and a midseason coaching change possibly coming, it’s getting safer to dismiss them. If anything, more wins for them means a worse draft pick for our longtime rival. And this week, it would also mean putting a loss on the undefeated Niners. No, we don’t realistically expect Dallas to go on some 12-win run to finish the year. They probably won’t be breathing the same air with the 49ers or Vikings by January. But in a sport where one QB injury can change everything, it’s still early enough that we can’t ignore any scenario. NFC vs. NFC Falcons d. Bears Cardinals d. Rams If the Cowboys can get to 3-3 this week, we’d love to see as many other NFC teams at or below that record. Chicago is 3-2 and Atlanta’s 2-3, so that’s an easy call there. The Bears could easily go on a run with Caleb Williams returning, and are one of the key threats to Dallas if we end up in the wild card race. The Rams are even more shocked and disappointed to be 2-3 right now than the Cowboys. Like Chicago, they’re a team that could figure things out and get hot at any point. It’s an easy pick to root for Arizona to drag them further into the hole. NFC vs. AFC Broncos d. Seahawks Bucs d. Steelers Generally, we’ll root for AFC teams to hang losses on our NFC competition. That’s the case tonight with Denver hosting Seattle. The Seahawks are 3-2 and one of the top threats in an eventual wild-card scenario. Despite being in the AFC, Pittsburgh owes Dallas their 2027 fourth-round pick, so we look at their games a bit differently. Tampa Bay may have embarrassed us last week, but it was embarrassing because they were 0-4 and not a threat. The Bucs don’t get to face the Cowboys’ disastrous defense every week, so they still feel like a non-factor in the grand scheme. AFC vs. AFC Jets d. Patriots Texans d. Jaguars We have a couple of all-AFC games worth paying attention to. Dallas owns the Patriots’ 2027 seventh-round pick by means of the Nate Thomas trade with Houston. The pick that the Texans sent us originally belonged to New England, so it’s where the Pats finish this year that dictates the pick’s value. Speaking of Houston, we can root for them this week for a different reason. Next week, they’re hosting the Giants. They’ll be coming off this Sunday morning’s London game against Jacksonville, so they may be at a slight disadvantage with rest and preparation. At the very least, good vibes and added confidence from a win could help them against New York.
author: Jess Haynie

title: Cowboys at Packers: Matchups to watch in Week 6
summary: The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers enter their Week 6 matchup at opposite ends of the momentum spectrum. The Packers are riding high after a dominating victory over the Chicago Bears last week while the Cowboys are still licking their wounds after the embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As we all know, […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers enter their Week 6 matchup at opposite ends of the momentum spectrum. The Packers are riding high after a dominating victory over the Chicago Bears last week while the Cowboys are still licking their wounds after the embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As we all know, Lambeau Field hasn’t been kind to the Cowboys in recent memory. They’ll need to play traumatically better than they did a week ago, and maybe even have some luck on their side to secure a “W”. To do that, they may need to have certain matchups go their way. If not, and could be another disappointing week around Cowboys Nation. Below are the matchups that could be difference makers. RB Javonte Williams vs. Packers run defense The Packers are coming off a game in which they held D’Andre Swift to just 43 yards on nine carries and only allowed Chicago to rush for a total of 81 rushing yards. They’ll be hoping to do the same this week against Javonte Williams and the Cowboys. Williams probably has other plans. He’s been a touchdown scoring machine so far this year with six, but is currently struggling to find consistency as a runner, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry. If Williams has success on the ground, it should sway the game in Dallas’ favor. Cowboys secondary vs. Packers pass offense If there’s one area where the Packers have the advantage over the Cowboys entering this Week 6 matchup, it’s their passing offense. QB Jordan Love threw for 367 yards and two touchdowns last week and is probably licking his chops to face the Cowboys secondary, which is currently ranked 30 th in the league in passing yards allowed. Dallas’ secondary is beat up at both cornerback and safety, but the return of Joey Porter Jr. to the lineup after missing last week’s game (illness) will help. This matchup could heavily impact the outcome of the game. Cowboys pass offense vs. Packers secondary If there’s a matchup that’s going to decide the outcome of this game, it’s probably going to be between the Cowboys aerial attack and the Packers pass defense. Green Bay is currently ranked fifth in the league allowing only 181 passing yards per game, but they haven’t faced an offense as talented as the Cowboys, and most teams like to run on the Packers anyway. Dallas is averaging 269.6 passing yards per game, which is fifth the league, and have arguably the best WR duo to exploit the Packers secondary. Dak Prescott and Company need to play better than last week, but this matchup could be the difference between a win or loss.

author: RJ Ochoa

title: Why the Cowboys can respond at Lambeau Field
summary: The Dallas Cowboys dropped to 2-3 after a disappointing loss to Tampa Bay, and things don’t get any easier with a trip to Lambeau Field. But Green Bay isn’t unbeatable. The Packers are 3-2, but have major injuries on defense, and some of their weaknesses match up well with what Dallas needs most. One reason […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys dropped to 2-3 after a disappointing loss to Tampa Bay, and things don’t get any easier with a trip to Lambeau Field. But Green Bay isn’t unbeatable. The Packers are 3-2, but have major injuries on defense, and some of their weaknesses match up well with what Dallas needs most. One reason to stay optimistic is the fact Green Bay’s biggest defensive weapons may still be unavailable. Former Cowboys pass rusher Micah Parsons has not yet been medically cleared to practice as he continues recovering from knee surgery. Matt LaFleur said Monday that Parsons is getting closer, but he will still need time to get back into football shape once cleared. Missing Parsoms is obviously a huge boost for a Dallas offensive line that struggled badly with Tampa Bay’s pressure. But the injuries don’t end there. The Packers have already lost linebacker Edgerrin Cooper for the season with an Achilles injury. Now defensive tackle Javon Hargrave has suffered the same fate and will also miss the rest of the year. Green Bay is already thin at defensive tackle, with Warren Brinson still on injured reserve. That gives Dallas an opportunity to attack the middle of the defense with Javonte Williams. And sticking with Williams, he’s having a hot scoring start to the season having already scored six rushing touchdowns in five games, including five over the last three weeks. Green Bay has allowed 638 rushing yards and eight rushing touchdowns this season. Only the New Orleans Saints have allowed more rushing touchdowns so far this year and Green Bay ranks 26th in rushing yards allowed. Dallas needs to get back to running the football consistently rather than putting everything on Dak Prescott. This looks like a good week to do it. Conversely, on the other side, Dallas has also struggled badly against the run. But Green Bay enters the game with only 302 rushing yards through five games, the lowest total in the NFL and are averaging just 3.1 yards per carry. They only scored its first two rushing touchdowns of the season against Chicago last Sunday, making them one of the most ineffective rushing teams in the league right now. Dallas desperately needs an opponent that doesn’t dominate on the ground and the Packers provide exactly that. As for the passing game, we saw CeeDee Lamb leaving the Tampa Bay game early, but George Pickens stepped right up. Pickens caught nine passes for 130 yards and a touchdown, his first 100-yard performance of the season. He has now produced 287 receiving yards over the last three games. That gives Prescott another weapon regardless of how much Lamb can do coming off his quad injury. Green Bay cannot simply focus all of its coverage on Lamb. There is finally some encouraging news regarding the team getting stronger. It is possible we could see DeMarvion Overshown make an appearance soon. Overshown returned to individual work this week and said he feels capable of running and moving normally again. His status remains uncertain, but he is hopeful of returning against Green Bay after missing four games with a hamstring injury. Dallas added veteran coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant which is extremely important for this week’s game. Pettine previously served as Green Bay’s defensive coordinator, meaning he knows Matt LaFleur and the Packers organization extremely well. That familiarity certainly doesn’t hurt when Dallas is desperately searching for defensive answers. The Cowboys ahve a chance this week, they jsut need to seize it.
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys edge player will see a playing time increase vs Packers
summary: When the Dallas Cowboys drafted Malachi Lawrence in the first round back in April, their were immediate high expectations placed on him, especially with where he was drafted and the need the team had to find another productive edge. He’s gotten playing time in each of the first five games, but he’s logged just 117 […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images When the Dallas Cowboys drafted Malachi Lawrence in the first round back in April, their were immediate high expectations placed on him, especially with where he was drafted and the need the team had to find another productive edge. He’s gotten playing time in each of the first five games, but he’s logged just 117 snaps defensively, which is just over 23 per game. So far in 2026, it’s been a struggle for the Cowboys defense as a whole, but the glaring lack of a pass rush is sticking out like a sore thumb. Dallas has registered just five sacks so far, which is the second fewest in the NFL. According to head coach Brian Schottenheimer, help is coming in the form of Lawrence who will see his snaps go up. Cowboys OLB Malachi Lawrence (57) is "absolutely" in line to get more snaps this week, according to HC Brian Schottenheimer: "He's played very well. I think he's starting to show the flash and the acceleration and the ability to rush the passer that we knew we were getting when… pic.twitter.com/z8nJ3GcSEV — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) October 14, 2026 Lawrence showed a flash of what could be from him as a pass rusher last Thursday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He ended up recording the first sack of his young career in the third quarter, which had to feel good for the youngster. Lawrence came into the league after racking up 20 sacks in his collegiate career at UCF, and he also had a ton of pass-rush upside. The additions of Rashan Gary and Von Miller simply haven’t been good enough, and Donovan Ezeiruaku is still trying to find his way to be a consistent presence off the edge. The Cowboys’ defense needs a spark somehow when it comes to getting to the quarterback, and with the potential that Lawrence has, he certainly has a chance to be just that.
author: Matthew Lenix

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: DaRon Bland, Tampa Bay, and the Packers
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  Should the coaching staff think about benching DaRon Bland at this point? Mike – I think so, and it’s down to Bland […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. Should the coaching staff think about benching DaRon Bland at this point? Mike – I think so, and it’s down to Bland playing on reputation rather than production right now. Dallas can’t afford to keep giving him a free pass because of what he accomplished in 2023. His coverage has been bad, his confidence looks shaky, and the dropped interception against Tampa Bay was another example of a player struggling to make the plays that once defined him. With Joey Porter Jr. in the building and available Christian Parker has alternatives worth exploring. I’m not saying Bland should be permanently benched, but reducing his snaps and moving him into the slot-only role could benefit him. That’s where he’s been most productive in the past. Tom – If he continues to fail at his assignments, of course. Not only is it logical to try and find a better solution, maybe it would light a fire under some other underperforming players. And if you haven’t noticed, there are a lot of them on the roster right now. I would consider adding Jake Ferguson for consideration. These don’t have to be permanent, but it is hard to see how going back to the well with players who keep making mistakes helps. Dyllan – Dallas should consider more of a rotation at this point. There is a place for Bland out there. But if money weren’t a factor, I’m not sure he would be considered one of the top two guys when the DB room is healthy. Jorge – Yes, plain and simple, falling down on routes, blowing coverages, and not even being able to secure a gimme pick-six. Pretty clear Bland is a shell of his former self; he’s playing with zero confidence on the field. They almost have to do him the favor and rotate him until he can at least get some confidence back; until then, we’ll just be counting the days until his contract is off the books. It’s a shame; he’s an NFL all-time record holder. Tough way to go. Sean – At this point my overall thought on the Christian Parker defense is that I want to see the team fully commit to “his guys” at as many spots as possible, so that we can get the best possible evaluation and know for sure if fans calling for his job already are overreacting or not. It’s been my opinion and hasn’t wavered that they are, but here comes another tough test against a Packers team that threw the ball at will in their win on Sunday. Bland showed he wasn’t a scheme fit in week one against the Giants, and it hasn’t gotten any better. It’s hard to imagine the Packers not taking advantage of him at least a few times if he is out there getting the same starter snaps. What was the biggest issue the Cowboys faced against the Buccaneers? Mike – The biggest issue was Dallas got bullied on both sides of the ball, and the coaching staff had absolutely no answers. Tampa Bay arrived winless, with a rookie quarterback, yet somehow dictated the entire game. The Cowboys surrendered 241 rushing yards, including 165 to Bucky Irving, allowing Tampa Bay to control possession for nearly 40 minutes. Offensively, Brian Schottenheimer failed to adjust leaving Dak Prescott under pressure and the offense completely out of rhythm. Christian Parker deserves just as much criticism for a defense that couldn’t stop the run. This wasn’t simply poor execution, it was a failure to prepare. Tom – Wow, it’s hard to pick one to single out. I’ll go with a broad one, and say it was the defense allowing so many explosive plays. The Dallas defense makes third and 15 look more like third and five for their opponents. There is no doubt the huge run they surrendered at the start of the second half was a big part in the loss. Dyllan – Missed tackles were a huge issue. The defense accounted for 12 missed tackles on the night, including several on the big Bucky Irving run after half time. Maybe it’s tied to the exhaustion from the schedule, maybe not. But missing that many is certainly not a recipe for success, as we saw with the Buccaneers rushing total. Jorge – Not playing hard. A very real culture is festering in Dallas where they are simply jogging plays out, if you will. I’m not seeing fight; I’m not seeing energy; I’m seeing a team that folds when the going gets tough. The missed tackles and explosive plays are just a symptom of that. Where is the Cowboys’ dog? Sean – “Most concerning” is one way, for me at least, to frame what the “biggest” issue is. For that I’m going to go with yet again overcomplicating things on offense. The run game worked like a charm on the first drive, then it was forgotten about. The slant route to George Pickens sparked a 99-yard drive, but the Cowboys were down two scores by that point. This is coming directly from the head coach, and the margin of error to get it corrected now is much smaller than we ever hoped of with so many hard games ahead. It’s the most concerning thing that came with dropping to 2-3. What does Christian Parker need to change to make sure the defense holds its side of the bargain to accomplish victory? Mike – Parker needs to fix the basics before worrying about being clever with his defensive schemes. Tampa Bay exposed some really poor tackling and gap discipline, so the priority has to be stopping the run and making teams earn their yards. Getting a pass rush that finally makes quarterbacks uncomfortable would be nice. Moving Parker into the coaching booth and bringing in Mike Pettine might help with adjustments, but neither will magically fix poor execution. But most importantly, Parker needs to adapt when things start going wrong rather than watching another offense dictate the game. Tom – Almost everything? I can’t think of one part of the defense that is even passable right now. It seems very possible that Parker is just out of his depth. Maybe Mike Pettine will be a big help, but he is unlikely to make much of an impact for this game. Dyllan – Parker needs to be more aggressive – especially after bringing in Pettine. Playing Joey Porter Jr. on the outside in press man coverage allows you to be more active around the line of scrimmage. More disguises, more blitzes. Jorge – Welp, I thought a move to the booth would come sooner or later; that should help them get lined up properly to start, but really they just have to start doing the little things right. Tackling properly, maintaining rush lanes, securing gaps, etc. If they do that, this defense will lift immensely, getting us closer to the only thing fans have asked for from this defense. Which is to be average. Sean – Even on some of the explosive plays allowed from the Bucs, Schottenheimer and Parker both said the calls were correct, so I guess amazingly part of the answer here is… more of the same? Any sarcasm aside though, there does need to be real changes too. Hiring Pettine and moving Parker to the box are some real changes to hopefully get it going the right direction. Parker should be able to see the coverage aspects while Pettine can focus on the front seven, the areas each coach knows the best. This makes the biggest thing I’ll be looking for from the defense, and answer to the question about Parker, not blowing coverages to allow guys wide open. Give yourself a chance in coverage. RAPID FIRE Who scores first for Dallas? Tom – Javonte Williams seems the safest bet Dyllan – CeeDee Lamb Jorge – George Pickens Sean – George Pickens Total defensive sacks, over/under- 1.5 Tom – I won’t believe the over until I see it happen Dyllan – Under. Too inconsistent. I’d love to see Ezeiruaku drive through the QB after winning a rep against the OT instead of slowing down/missing the tackle. Jorge – Under Sean – I’ll actually go over, I think Love holds the ball in a few spots. Dak Prescott passing touchdowns, over/under- 2.5 Tom – Under Dyllan –…
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: The embarrassment of being in the NFC East
summary: Well, at least the Dallas Cowboys are not alone in their misery. The Philadelphia Eagles let the Jacksonville Jaguars steal a game from them in London, then the New York Giants and Washington Commanders put on an amazing display of ineptitude at the end of their overtime tie. First, the Giants handed the Commanders a […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Well, at least the Dallas Cowboys are not alone in their misery. The Philadelphia Eagles let the Jacksonville Jaguars steal a game from them in London, then the New York Giants and Washington Commanders put on an amazing display of ineptitude at the end of their overtime tie. First, the Giants handed the Commanders a golden opportunity to kick the winning field goal. Then, with time running out, Jayden Daniels apparently forgot they were out of time outs and let the clock run down to zero with his team in range for what should have been an easy field goal. That hardly makes us feel better. But it does bring up the question asked here, and heard from the announcers of the Giants-Commanders game: Does anyone want to win the NFC East? Sean – After all the dust settled on this comical, disastrous week for the NFC East, I had the following thought – which team actually benefits the most from winning the division, if it stays the way it’s going and continues to look like the winner won’t be a real threat in the playoffs? The Giants have the longest playoff drought, but also a season-ending injury to their starting QB. The Eagles in some ways appear to be making a statement that just winning this lousy division isn’t good enough, if they aren’t true Super Bowl contenders they rather build for a future where they are. The Dan Quinn experiment in Washington feels like it’s all but over, but a playoff berth could see him stay. I really think the answer is our team, Tom. Coach Schottenheimer’s predecessor was let go because he couldn’t advance in the playoffs, but at least he proved consistently he could get there. We don’t even know if Schotty can guide the team to the postseason yet, and it still doesn’t feel like any team around the NFC at large is “unbeatable”. In order for the Cowboys to turn this around and actually grab the NFC East’s low-hanging fruit of a playoff spot, and do so with any conviction, they’re going to have to fix a lot of defensive issues against the Packers. Matt LaFleur is going to be licking his chops seeing the Cowboys defensive tape from the Bucs game, doing so fresh off a win against the hated Chicago Bears too. There’s been a lot of talk in recent weeks about desperate teams, desperate coaching staffs, and on and on. I don’t exactly have a lot of faith in the Cowboys staff, one that added Mike Pettine on Monday, to really embrace this mantra and be as prepared for the Packers as they need to be. Tom – It is hard not to cringe about what is likely going to face the Cowboys in the storied confines of Lambeau Field. Jordan Love went off on the Chicago Bears. We are all well aware of just how woefully vulnerable the Dallas defense has been this season. Yet this game has the potential for the Cowboys to get right. I’m not saying it’s a big potential, but it still exists. The Packers are an even more one-dimensional offense than Dallas, ranking dead last in rushing yards per game. One possible way for the visitors to eke out a win is to play ball control offense and keep Love on the bench for long stretches, while scoring consistently on their own possessions. That may be a tall order, however. Dallas is barely ahead of Green Bay in running the ball. The Packers have a clear edge in both points allowed and sacks. And Dak Prescott has to have a much better game than he did against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As good as he can be some times, Prescott also can have games where he is just off. That seemed to be the case in their latest loss. We have to hope he has a bounce back when they head north. Maybe the real question is not who wants to win the NFC East. It might be who has the ability. None of the teams in the division have demonstrated that so far. Whoever manages to do so could make the playoffs to represent the NFCE. Now we have to see if the Cowboys have that in them. Sean – My hope for this game is that Love’s deep ball performance against a Bears defense that was suspect to such throws last year as well can be a bit of an outlier, but man the Cowboys cornerback and safety play shouldn’t make anyone feel great about winning this differential. The Cowboys may not have to, if they really do stick with the run game and play a little bit more ball control like you said. All that said, I’m not sure why I still feel as optimistic as I do about this team. I am far from the level of doom and gloom that’s coming out of the Bucs loss, but we said a bit of the same after the Ravens loss too so maybe I’m just staying aboard the same ship. The defense needs to get healthier before we can fully assess how much they will help this team going forward. The offense is a different story, they need to come out looking pissed off about what happened to them last Thursday night in this game. When it comes to that ability to win the NFC East you mentioned Tom, the difference maker feels obvious to me. Whichever team can string together a win streak of any significance. The Cowboys don’t have back to back wins since last November, and that is certainly bad. The Eagles only back-to-back wins this year are against the Commanders and Titans, though. The Giants also beat the Titans then the Cardinals back to back. The Commanders have the most impressive single win of anyone in the division by beating the defending Super Bowl champs with a backup QB, but no win streak to speak of. The time is definitely right here and now for the Cowboys to get two wins against the Packers and Eagles to change the mood of the season the best they can. Tom – One thing that has been worrying me lately is the spreading opinion that the Dallas players are just kind of giving up on too many plays. There just doesn’t seem to be much of that dog in them that winning teams exhibit. I think that has to be laid at the feet of the coaching staff. They need to light a fire under this team. It may be time to bench a starter or two to push the rest of the roster. I would suggest that DaRon Bland and Jake Ferguson have both had too many errors of late and would be prime candidates for at least a temporary demotion. It may seem a drastic move, but this team needs to do something drastic. And the recent hire of Mike Pettine could be seen as just such a move, which would make some roster shakeup logical. Despite a couple of really bad games this season, Dallas is still in contention for the division title thanks to some similarly bad games played by the rest of the NFC East. Bouncing back and getting a win on the road in Green Bay could get this team back on track. But if they lay another egg, they risk letting a golden opportunity to get back to the playoffs slip through their grasp just like the football has been doing far too often of late. Sean – Coach Schotty has already teased that there will be personnel changes going into this game, so in this case we’ll have to “wait all day for Sunday night” to really keep a close eye on the lineups. Brew some extra coffee before kickoff. This might be a bit too far outside the box, but I’m wondering out loud if the Pettine hire can lead to more of James Houston at linebacker/pass rush. I agree with you completely on Ferguson. The Cowboys best offensive plays against the Bucs (and there weren’t nearly enough of them) came when they had extra blockers in against the blitz, let Prescott stand in there, and fire the ball to either CeeDee Lamb or more often than not, George Pickens. The idea of Ferguson being the third seam-stretching element to this offense is enticing, I get it. But he wasn’t even contributing to that blocking, it was mostly Javonte Williams at the RB spot. Keep it simple and rely as much as you possibly can on Pickens, Lamb, and Ryan Flournoy. That trio is good enough to win with on offense, I really believe that. Clearly getting too high off a win is something this team is still struggling with, but now they’re in a position of having to hope that applies to the Packers who just beat the Bears…

title: 8 Things we learned from the Broncos 17-14 OT win over Seattle
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Another week, another stress-inducing game for the Denver Broncos. It wasn’t pretty, especially in the second half for Bo Nix and the Denver offense. But the team gritted out another win. All that matters is the Broncos beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime. Denver now sits […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 15: Kicker Wil Lutz (3) of the Denver Broncos celebrates his game-winning kick to beat the Seattle Seahawks in overtime on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colo. (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Another week, another stress-inducing game for the Denver Broncos. It wasn’t pretty, especially in the second half for Bo Nix and the Denver offense. But the team gritted out another win. All that matters is the Broncos beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime. Denver now sits at 4-2 after a brutal six-game stretch to start the season. Now the Broncos get a mini-bye before heading to the desert to face the Arizona Cardinals. Wil Lutz with the clutch kick You always hold your breath when the Denver kicker attempts a field goal. And all of Broncos Country did that at the end of the game. Thankfully, it was an exhale of celebration after Lutz nailed the game-winning 53-yard field goal. On this day, he was big nuts Lutz, and absolutely clutch Lutz. Helluva kick. Give Denver’s defense its flowers Down the best cornerback in the NFL in Patrick Surtain II, the team’s best safety in Talanoa Hufanga, and the Broncos hold Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seattle offense to 14 points? Damn impressive showing by Denver’s defense. On top of that, the Broncos forced three turnovers, got five sacks, five tackles for loss, and nine passes defended. Perhaps the stat of the night, Denver got 17 quarterback hits on Sam Darnold. In a defensive battle, the Broncos outshone one of the best defenses in the league. The Broncos secondary was fantastic Without the two best players in the unit, and Riley Moss limited most of the night, Denver’s secondary played an unreal game. Yes, JSN got his yards, but when the Broncos needed a play, the guys stepped up. Two of the biggest plays coming from Kris Abrams-Draine and Ja’Quan McMillian forcing huge turnovers, the latter getting the game-winning interception. McMillian is making a habit of this for Denver in clutch moments. He also got a sack. McMillian finished with five tackles (five sol0), one sack, one tackle for loss, two passes defended, and one quarterback hit. Abrams-Draine had six tackles (four solo) and three passes defended. All without PSs and Hufanga. Bo Nix must get better What we saw from the Broncos quarterback in the second half will not cut it. He must play better. What’s perplexing is how good the offense looked on back-to-back touchdown drives in the first half. Why does it have to be one or the other? Obviously, some of the credit goes to the Seattle defense. The Seahawks rank at the top or near the top for each statistical category. But Nix is going to have to start playing with more consistency because what he’s putting on the field is not good enough. It no doubt helps to sit at 4-2, having faced five of the best teams in the NFL, but figure it out. Denver’s running game is terrible The Broncos finished with 74 yards rushing on Thursday night. How the heck did they get that many? I don’t know if it’s J.K. Dobbins or the offensive line suddenly being terrible at run blocking, but this is bad. Perhaps rookie Jonah Coleman is the savior, and he’ll be back in Week 7 against the Cardinals. But similar to Nix, the running game issues have to get fixed. It’s brutal to watch Denver attempt to run the football right now. Dominance at home continues The Mile High Magic has returned. The Broncos improved to 3-0 at home this season after going 9-2 if you include the postseason. Denver has always been one of the best, if not the best, home-field advantages in the NFL. To see the success at home return like this is great to see. Throwback jerseys shine again There is no better throwback jersey in the NFL than the Broncos. And to have Seattle rock their throwbacks gave us veteran fans flashbacks to the old AFC West days. Just like at home, the Broncos remain unbeaten when they rock the snot rocket. Sitting at 4-2 is quite the feat As noted at the top, Denver just faced a brutal six-game stretch to start the season, and they sit at 4-2. When the schedule was released, every single person in Broncos Country would take that record. What should give fans hope is that the Broncos haven’t played their best yet. Similar to last season, we didn’t see the team start putting it all together until the calendar turned to November. Yet despite ugly games and performances, Nix and the offense being a disaster, they’ve beaten four of the best teams in football. That’s reason enough to feel good about this team.
