title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 17-14 victory over the Seattle Seahawks
summary: Our Denver Broncos have perfected the ability to “win ugly”. We saw it last year when they won many one-score games, and it is continuing this season. Tonight, the Broncos offense went out and put up an early 14-3 lead in the first half and packed it in after that. Meanwhile, the Broncos defense dominated […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Wil Lutz #3 and Jeremy Crawshaw #16 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after making a 53 yard game winning field goal against the Seattle Seahawks in overtime of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Our Denver Broncos have perfected the ability to “win ugly”. We saw it last year when they won many one-score games, and it is continuing this season. Tonight, the Broncos offense went out and put up an early 14-3 lead in the first half and packed it in after that. Meanwhile, the Broncos defense dominated throughout and held the Seahawks to just 14 points and made life a living hell for quarterback Sam Darnold. Again, it wasn’t pretty, but this game was always destined to be a defensive slugfest. The Broncos and Seahawks have two of the better defenses in the NFL, but their offenses are weaknesses right now, and that is exactly how it played out tonight. As for winners and losers for this game, it’s pretty simple. Defense good, offense bad. WINNER – Denver Broncos defense/Vance Joseph Through the first handful of games, the Broncos’ defense has been good but has not been as good as it was at times last season. On top of that, they were down multiple starters, including All-Pro Pat Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga, and a limited Riley Moss. However, they stepped up tonight and put together one of their best all-around efforts in the Vance Joseph defensive coordinator era. They had 5 sacks, 17 quarterback hits, a ton of pressures, 9 passes defended, a forced fumble/fumble recovery, and 2 HUGE late-game interceptions. Defense had it on 🔒 pic.twitter.com/CzF8e57Z36 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 16, 2026 Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen played lights out, Que Robinson flashed multiple times, Alex Singleton played a damn good ball game, DJ Jones may have had his best career game with the Broncos, and the Broncos secondary stepped up big. Yes, JSN made some plays late, but he’s the best in the NFL for a reason. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine, two very inexperienced corners, played very well all things considered. KAD should have had a game-ending INT on Darnold late in the 4th quarter, and Ja’Quan McMillian called game (again) with a HUGE INT in overtime that set up Wil Lutz’s game-winning FG. Credit to Vance Joseph for a coaching masterpiece against a talented offense while down multiple key starters. The reserves played well, and the pass rush came alive. The Broncos’ defense is why the Broncos sit 4-2 right now, and Joseph deserves a lot of credit again. LOSER – Broncos offense/Bo Nix Listen, that wasn’t pretty. There is no denying it. However, I think a lot of fans need to take a step back and take a deep breath. They played a very, very good and well-coached defense and never were going to have a “get right” game vs. the Seahawks. We also saw this last year. Early season, Bo Nix struggled and looked lost. We saw it his rookie year, last year, and again this year. Those previous two seasons, he has turned it on as the season went on, so let’s hope that happens again this season. Still, that was ugly. Nix looks lost, lacking confidence, and maybe not fully healthy? I personally believe it’s all mental right now. He is coming off a missed offseason, played a tough schedule to start the year, may not be fully trusting of his ankle yet, and it’s all in his head right now. I still Bo-lieve and think they will figure it out. The Nix we saw vs. the Bills simply didn’t disappear. He has a mini bye week to get right, an easier upcoming schedule, and, like the second half of these games, the second half of the season is Bo Nix time. As for the rest of the offense, it was pretty meh. Outside of a few runs, JK Dobbins provided very little and averaged 2.4 yards per carry. RJ Harvey showed some life, but didn’t see a ton of touches, and they lost Tyler Badie to a finger injury. The OL, specifically Ben Powers and Luke Wattenberg, had some issues. Powers was beat a few times, and Wattenberg’s off-target snaps are an issue. Wasn’t pretty and was non-existent in the second half, but those two first-half touchdowns were enough to send it to overtime and eventually to win the game. Oh, and the fact that they could not get a first down to end the game after the KAD INT in the 4th quarter, and again to get into closer field goal range in OT after the J-Mac INT, is unacceptable. I have faith that they will turn it around, because they have in the past, but it is not looking pretty right now. WINNER – Pass Rush The Broncos’ pass rush came alive on Thursday Night. Nik Bonitto, Zach Allen, Ja’Quan McMillian, Que Robinson, Jonah Elliss, Malcolm Roach, and Justin Strnad all combined for sacks. They had 17 total QB hits, many pressures, and terrorized QB Sam Darnold all night. An ode to the Orange Crush 💥 📺: NFL+ pic.twitter.com/JID7ExsPDC — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 16, 2026 They don’t have John Franklin-Myers or Jonathon Cooper, but this pass rush looked a lot like the ones that led the NFL in sacks in back-to-back years. They had a slower start than usual this season, but this showing could ignite a big second half for the Broncos defense and pass rush. WINNER – Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine Was it perfect? No. JSN got them a handful of times throughout the game, and Barron was beat deep on one play vs. Shaheed, but overall, they played well. Barron had tight coverage throughout and was against JSN a few times, which is tough for any corner. He wasn’t flawless, but he showed real potential tonight, in my opinion. As for Abrams-Draine, he simply makes plays. His INT late in the 4th quarter should have ended the game, but still, it was an incredible play. KRIS ABRAMS DRAINE INT pic.twitter.com/lkc9O276sm — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 These are the Broncos’ fourth and fifth corners, and I believe they have held their own and proven they can be future starters if they let Riley Moss and/or Ja’Quan McMillian walk this offseason. WINNER – Ja’Quan McMillian He has the clutch gene. Ended the game last week with a sack of Justin Herbert Ended tonight’s game with an INT in OT that set up the game-winning field goal. Oh, and his heroics in the postseason that led to the Broncos’ thrilling overtime victory over the Bills. J-MAC INT!!!! pic.twitter.com/b2KORAVxiG — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 J-Mac has earned himself a nice contract this offseason, whether it is from the Broncos or another team. The Broncos have to decide between Moss and McMillian this offseason, in all likelihood, and J-Mac is making it tough to not pick him. WINNER – Sean Payton/ugly wins I am giving Sean Payton credit. The Broncos’ start to the season was brutal. Week 1 vs. the Chiefs in Arrowhead. Never easy. Week 2 vs. the only team to beat you by double digits last season, the Jaguars. The Super Team Rams in Week 3, a Week 4 matchup vs. the undefeated Niners (and the injury-creating substitution), a home game vs. the rival Chargers, and a short-week TNF against the defending champion Seahawks. On paper, this was a brutal start, and it hasn’t been much easier in reality either. The Chiefs and Niners are 4-0, the Jaguars are 3-1, the Seahawks are 3-2, and the Rams are 2-3. Yet, the Broncos, despite all their struggles, are 4-2. I would have been happy with 3-3. Survived the brutal start and can now have a second-half run against an easier-on-paper schedule. Yet, they are 4-2, and their only two losses came on the road against two undefeated teams. Broncos are 4-2 after a brutal start to the season against some of the better teams in the NFL right now. Their only two losses are two undefeated teams. They have their issues, but I'm happy with 4-2. The schedule gets easier on paper from here on out. Enjoy a win. Those 10… — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 A lot of credit has to go to Sean Payton. They won ugly last…

title: Instant reaction: Broncos upend Seahawks in overtime thriller on Thursday Night Football
summary: The Denver Broncos hosted the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. It was another nailbiter for the Mile High faithful across Broncos Country, but the Broncos were able to win in overtime by a score of 17-14. Here are some instant reactions from today’s game. After two first half scoring drives, Broncos’ offense flames out […]
full_text: Oct 15, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton (14) reacts in the first quarter against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos hosted the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football . It was another nailbiter for the Mile High faithful across Broncos Country, but the Broncos were able to win in overtime by a score of 17-14. Here are some instant reactions from today’s game. After two first half scoring drives, Broncos’ offense flames out hard in second half The Seahawks entered tonight’s primetime matchup as one of the premier defenses of the National Football League. Whether it was limiting opposing aerial attacks to just 150 yards a game, a Top 3 third down defense, or generating turnovers—very few teams have been successful going up against them. Everyone across Broncos Country knew it would be a tough game for Bo Nix and the offense to get back on track. However, early on in the game, it appeared the Broncos were poised to do just that. After a three-and-out to start the game, the offense put up an impressive 19 play, 79-yard scoring drive that lasted nearly nine minutes. They followed that up with a 9 play, 74-yard drive that went the distance and was capped off with a short RJ Harvey touchdown run. Denver converted just one third down last week, but had three in the first half, as well as a key fourth down conversion. Even though the offense had just 130 yards, they ran 32 total plays, had 11 first downs, and dominated the time of possession. Unfortunately, the success the Broncos had in the first half didn’t translate to the second half. They were an absolute disaster by every measure possible. By the final possession of the game, they achieved just one third down in the final half of play. On eight total drives in the second half, they had just 36 yards of offense. Quite honestly, I don’t even know what to say about this side of the football anymore. What we are witnessing is simply unacceptable. Absolutely nothing looks good and big part of that is because the quarterback is playing absolutely awful. It’s just bottom of the barrel play from Nix every single week. But let’s turn to the defense, who were pretty darn good tonight. Denver’s defensive effort is the major reason they won One of my big questions entering tonight’s game was how Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph gameplan to limit star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s impact on the game. Although Riley Moss was active for tonight’s matchup, Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine saw a majority of the reps at boundary corner. In the first half, Denver’s defense did extremely well. They held the Seahawks to just 91 total yards of offense. Quarterback Sam Darnold was 7-of-15 with only 52 yards passing. Smith-Njigba, who was averaging over 115 receiving yards per game, was limited to just 2 catches for 11 yards through thirty minutes of play. Multiple first half sacks by Que Robinson and Ja’Quan McMillian were big tone setters on third down. Additionally, a Nik Bonitto forced fumble was a big momentum shift to keep the Seahawks from scoring additional points toward the end of the half. With the offense struggling mightily in the second half, Denver’s defense began to wear down a bit. Smith-Njigba was able to get some big plays, but Kris Abrams-Draine and Ja’Quan McMillian had interceptions on Darnold that proved to be game-changing plays. The Broncos may have given up some yards, but they finished the game with five sacks and ten different players on defense registered a quarterback hit on Darnold. Their penchant for turnovers once again proved to be difference makers. Color me impressed with this performance with Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga out. This is a championship caliber defense that would be even better if the offense would just do their part on a weekly basis. Hats off to Vance Joseph and his players for securing this W . The Broncos are in a great spot at 4-2 after six games Denver finding a way to be a 4-2 team despite their offense being so inept is quite the outcome. They’ve faced a gauntlet of teams to start the season. All things considered, Broncos Country should be happy with their record. Now, they will get to enjoy a little extra rest before they head on the road to take on the Arizona Cardinals for their Week 7 gridiron matchup. I don’t know if that will be enough time to fix their issues on offense, but getting more time to prepare is always a good thing. Hopefully, somehow—someway, Denver’s offense can find a way to be much better moving forward.

title: Broncos’ defense did everything possible to beat Seahawks; offense went three-and-out
summary: What is wrong with Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense? That is the question for the next 10 days. However, for tonight let’s celebrate the effort from the defense. They held on and did what they needed to do to secure the win for the Broncos. They harassed Sam Darnold and generated the turnovers […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos scrambles against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images What is wrong with Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense? That is the question for the next 10 days. However, for tonight let’s celebrate the effort from the defense. They held on and did what they needed to do to secure the win for the Broncos. They harassed Sam Darnold and generated the turnovers needed to secure the 4-2 start for Denver. 10 different players have at least one quarterback hit so far this game, which is the most Broncos to record a QB hit in a game since at least 2006 — Tyler Gorse (@Tyler_Gorse_) October 16, 2026 Broncos vs. Seahawks final score Team 1st 2nd 3rd 4th OT Final Seattle Seahawks 3 0 0 11 0 14 Denver Broncos 0 14 0 0 3 17 First Quarter The Broncos defense showed up early and put Sam Darnold in a blender on their first drive with back-to-back sacks to take them out of field goal range. QUE ROBINSON SACK!!! pic.twitter.com/OcDxifChhp — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 But Bo Nix and the Broncos offense would go three-and-out and with that short field the Seahawks were able to capitalize with a field goal from their second drive. Denver’s offense woke up though on their second drive and drove the length of the field the rest of the quarter and entered the second inside the Seahawks’ red zone area. Seahawks 3, Broncos 0. Full first quarter recap . Second Quarter Denver would conclude that drive from the first quarter not long into the second. Capping the 16-play, 74 yard drive was this J.K. Dobbins touchdown run from four yards out. TOUCHDOWN JK DOBBINS pic.twitter.com/Gv2UEx4e81 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 Their next drive was a 9-play, 79 yard drive. The big play came on a run play that Bo Nix checked out of for a shot to the end zone to Courtland Sutton. The pass was incomplete, but the defensive pass interference call set the Broncos up at the one yard line where RJ Harvey would add a rushing touchdown of his own in this game. RJ HARVEY TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/rM2AbB0StH — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 Nik Bonitto would force a fumble late in the half to give Denver a chance to add to their lead, but they ended up going three-and-out and having to punt despite being near midfield. Even so, it was easily the best second quarter of the season for the Broncos. Broncos 14, Seahawks 3. Full second quarter recap . Third Quarter The Broncos’ offense continued their three-and-out stretch for three more drives to start the second half and did absolutely nothing to help. The defense had to hold the water and made the big plays through their pass rush on third downs. The first big one led to a missed field goal. JONAH ELLISS SACK ON 3RD DOWN!! Seattle would miss the FG on the following play 😎 pic.twitter.com/2SBrKedJa3 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 The second put them into a fourth and 19 and a punt. The issues on offense seemed to be some pretty bad offensive line play by Ben Powers and others, but primarily Powers. He was consistently getting manhandled in the run game and on one third down get beat so bad off the line by a Seahawks defender that he belly flopped touching no one. Bo Nix had to roll outside hurried and misfired on the third down pass. Pretty ugly quarter by the Broncos offense, but the defense was keeping them in a comfortable lead heading into the final quarter. Broncos 14, Seahawks 3. Full third quarter recap . Fourth Quarter Denver’s defense every time it seemed that Seattle was getting close to field goal range would unleash the fury of their pass rush. This drive would be no different with a Dondra Tillman sack on third down that took the Seahawks out of field goal range. The punt would pin the Broncos offense inside their own 10 yard line, but the defense preserved the 11-point lead early in the fourth quarter. BRONCOS GET THEIR 5TH SACK AND KNOCK THE SEAHAWKS OUT OF FG RANGE pic.twitter.com/mfQSLJsOdx — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 Denver’s next drive started off with a quick pass outside to Marvin Mims Jr. for a five yard gain, then RJ Harvey burst through the hole for Denver’s first first down of the half. The drive came to an end when Jaylen Waddle caught the ball just a foot shy of the first down marker at their own 30 yard line. Sean Payton flirted with the idea of going for it, but that could have been the same mistake the Los Angeles Chargers made just four days ago that sparked a Broncos comeback win. No need to give Seattle life there and they smartly punted it away. Sam Darnold converted a fourth down after being terrorized leading up that, with JSN beating Jahdae Barron on a quick slant. The drive would cross the halfway mark of the quarter before Darnold would face another third and long from Denver’s 33. He would face outside pressure and then take off running for a 15 yard gain and a first down inside the red zone. They would punch it in from there with a touchdown and a two-point conversion to make it a three-point game. Denver would go three-and-out for the sixth time in the game to give Seattle plenty of time to tie the game or even get the game-clinching touchdown with less than four minutes to go. JSN made the big play to midfield with an incredible catch and it looked like Denver’s defense would succumb to the comeback. Enter Kris Abrams Draine who stepped in front of a deep pass outside to intercept the ball to keep the dream alive for Broncos fans. KRIS ABRAMS DRAINE INT pic.twitter.com/lkc9O276sm — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 Denver’s defense did literally all they could and Denver’s offense answered with their seventh three-and-out and was only able to take 15 seconds off the clock. The Seahawks streaked down the field to setup the game-tying field goal to send the game into overtime. Broncos 14, Seahawks 14. Overtime The Broncos won the overtime coin toss and elected to kick. That was probably a smart choice at the time given their offense had eight drives for about 38 yards in the second half. The thinking there might have been “hopefully the defense can get a turnover or something” type thing. It looked like the defense was gassed and after a couple of first downs, I began to worry, but Darnold went deep on a third down and Ja’Quan McMillian stepped in front to intercept it at the Seahawks 43-yard line. J-MAC INT!!!! pic.twitter.com/b2KORAVxiG — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 Denver ran it three times and tried a Wil Lutz 53-yard field goal attempt that went through. Praise the ghosts of Elway for this one! Broncos 17, Seahawks 14.

full_text: Detroit Lions executive vice president and general manager Brad Holmes speaks during media availability at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, Jan. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Earlier this week, we checked in on the popularity of Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell . As of Friday morning, Campbell had an approval rating just over 91 percent among Lions fans. Now, let’s turn our attention to general manager Brad Holmes. Without a doubt, Holmes has faced more scrutiny than just about anyone in the Lions organization these days, save perhaps defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. Upset fans point to the fruitlessness of Detroit’s 2024 NFL Draft class—particularly with the first three picks: Terrion Arnold (cut), Ennis Rakestraw (0 starts, 11 games), and Giovanni Manu (four games, one start). Lately, fans have been frustrated about his insistence prior to the season that they liked the players in their cornerback room (not sure what else he was supposed to say), only to see cornerback clearly be the team’s biggest issue through the first month of the season. And while Holmes certainly deserves plenty of criticism for how the secondary has turned out this year, it’s also important to point out the clear improvements he’s made on the roster this season. The Lions’ offensive line has made a significant turnaround thanks to the recent investments in Blake Miller, Tate Ratledge, Juice Scruggs, and Christian Mahogany—and we haven’t even seen what Detroit has in Cade Mays yet. Similarly, the defensive line is finally producing at a top-tier level. Thanks to draft investments in Aidan Hutchinson, Alim McNeill, and Tyleik Williams—along with free agent/waiver adds DJ Wonnum and Tyler Lacy—Detroit has an impressive pass rush and strong run defense presence up the middle. Holmes even found an unlikely contributor in sixth-round rookie Skyler Gill-Howard. And, again, we haven’t even seen the full potential of second-round pick Derrick Moore. And if you look at most of the players Detroit opted to move on from this offseason, they have not been producing on par with the contracts they signed elsewhere . Still, you have to take the entire outlook into mind before you vote. Before you do, here’s a look at Holmes’ approval ratings throughout the years. title: Report: Detroit Lions sign veteran returner to the practice squad
summary: The Detroit Lions are reportedly signing veteran returner and wide receiver DeAndre Carter to their practice squad, according to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero, potentially giving them another competitive option for their return game. After losing their primary punt and kick returner, Tom Kennedy, for the season due to a knee (MCL) injury that will require […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2024; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Chicago Bears wide receiver DeAndre Carter (30) returns a kick against the Kansas City Chiefs during the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Detroit Lions are reportedly signing veteran returner and wide receiver DeAndre Carter to their practice squad, according to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero , potentially giving them another competitive option for their return game. After losing their primary punt and kick returner, Tom Kennedy, for the season due to a knee (MCL) injury that will require surgery , the Lions need a new starting returner. As our own John Whiticar pointed out in a recent article evaluating potential returner options , the Lions have several solid internal options who are expected to compete for the role—including eight players on the active roster and four on the practice squad—but none have the level of experience that Carter possesses. Carter went undrafted out of Sacramento State in 2015 and bounced around four different practice squads over his first three seasons in the NFL, before getting his first opportunity with the Eagles and Texans in 2018. Carter stuck in Houston the next two seasons before moving on and making several one-year stops with a variety of teams, including the Bears (twice), Commanders, Chargers, Raiders, and most recently in 2025 with the Browns. Carter is best known for his toughness, quickness, ability to separate, and create yards after the catch (YAC). Over his eight-year career, Carter has played in 111 games, primarily as a punt and kick returner, and has also registered 21 starts at wide receiver. Carter has returned 155 punts for 1508 return yards (averaging 9.7 yards per punt return) and 144 kick returns for 3399 return yards (averaging 23.6 yards), including a 101-yard touchdown. As a receiver, he has 117 career receptions for 1331 yards and six touchdowns, along with 16 rushes for 99 yards. The Lions have yet to officially announce this transaction, but they did have an open spot on their practice squad after releasing safety Jalen Mills earlier in the week .

full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell takes the field for during the first half against Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s been a while since we’ve checked in on the popularity of Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell. Like…. way too long. The last approval poll we ran on Campbell was in May of 2025, and the results of that poll were lost to the internet archives. So the last known datapoint we have for Dan Campbell’s popularity in Detroit was almost exactly two years ago. Back in October of 2024, the Lions were 3-1 at the bye week. They had just made their deep NFC Championship run, and little did we know that Detroit was in the midst of a record-breaking 15-win regular season. Things are quite a bit different now. The Lions are coming off a 9-8 season in which they missed the playoffs. They’re off to a bit of an uninspiring 3-2 start in 2026. Vibes are better after Detroit waxed the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, but I can’t help but think about how bad the vibes were going into that game—and after the first quarter of the Cardinals game. If you need a reminder, days before that game, 12 percent of Lions fans said they believed things were headed in the right direction. Now, whether or not that’s Campbell’s fault is a matter of opinion. Through just over five years, Campbell has posted a 51-38-1 record in Detroit, with an additional 2-2 record in the playoffs. Some of the current struggles appear to be on the defensive side of the ball, but Campbell is still ultimately culpable for that, even if he’s more of an offensive-minded coach. Campbell is the one who continues to show support and belief in defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, and ultimately it’s on the head coach to ensure the team is playing to their fullest potential. title: The Detroit Lions are getting back ‘a top-10 center’ in Cade Mays
summary: As soon as next game, the Detroit Lions will finally get to see what they’ve got in free agent signing Cade Mays. Detroit invested a three-year, $25 million contract in Mays, only to see their biggest offseason addition suffer a fractured wrist in training camp. But with his practice clock already started, there’s an expectation […]
full_text: Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64), left, talks to offensive tackle Penei Sewell (58) as they walk off the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co As soon as next game, the Detroit Lions will finally get to see what they’ve got in free agent signing Cade Mays. Detroit invested a three-year, $25 million contract in Mays, only to see their biggest offseason addition suffer a fractured wrist in training camp. But with his practice clock already started, there’s an expectation Mays could take the starting center position as soon as Detroit’s next game against the Green Bay Packers. A couple weeks back— as part of our Pride of Detroit Direct “First Byte” podcast —we talked to Panthers analyst and radio host John Ellis to preview the Lions vs. Panthers game. Toward the end of the show, we picked Ellis’ brain about Mays and how he played in Carolina for the past few years. Needless to say, he’s a big fan of Mays. “You guys will be thrilled with everything he brings to the table,” Ellis said. “On the field, he’s a mauler in the run game, he can climb to the second level, he’s got great anchor ability in the pass game. He’s not without flaws, but he’s a top-10 center in my book in this league. And he’s been a big liability in terms of his loss here in Carolina. He’s also a funny dude off the field, and a great follow on social media. So, you’ll love him. He’s a Dan Campbell guy. When I saw Dan got Cade Mays, I said, ‘Shit, that’s perfect, man.’” One of the most important roles Mays will eventually fill is a pre-snap diagnoser. NFL centers must do their best to read the defense’s pressure looks, adjust the protection accordingly, and communicate that to the entire team. Even though Mays has only been at the center position for a couple of seasons, Ellis believes that’s another strength in his game. “He plays with intensity and leadership, and he is tremendous in terms of anchoring the center, not just physically, but also commanding everything in terms of the checks, pre-snap stuff,” Ellis said. “He’s a very refined player in that department.” Of course, all of that begs the question: Why did the Panthers let him go? In Ellis’ opinion, it was simply a matter of finances. “They had to make a business decision, and I think it was pretty clear that they were going to have to move on. They drafted Sam Hecht last year, and Luke Fornter is a stop-gap,” Ellis said. Earlier in the week Lions coach Dan Campbell noted that while they’re going to get Mays some time during the bye week to continue to work out and get ready to return to the field, there are still some decisions that have to be made with how the offensive line will shake out vs. the Packers. That’s especially true considering backup center Juice Scruggs has been playing well in Mays’ absence. “It’s going to be nice to get Cade in the mix. And look, so much of this is, we’ve got to see exactly where he’s at,” Campbell said. “We’ve got basically two days of half practices with him and so let’s see what it looks like next week. He’s going to continue to train here and then we got to make a decision on how do we work this. That’s what’s a little unique, he plays center. It’s not like you’re rotating a guard. So how do we handle this? What’s the best way? Can he go 70 reps? So, there’s a lot of factors that go into it right now.” Regardless, at some point Mays will take his spot at center, and the Lions offensive line— which is already one of the best in football —could take the next step.

title: Survey: Which Lions player returning from injury will have the biggest immediate impact?
summary: Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host NFL fan surveys, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook. For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and since the Lions are on a bye in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, we are shifting from our regular opponent-based question to a roster-focused […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch (32) watches a drill after practice during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, June 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host NFL fan surveys, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook . For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and since the Lions are on a bye in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, we are shifting from our regular opponent-based question to a roster-focused one. Here are our two questions for Lions fans this week: Which Lions player returning from injury will have the biggest immediate impact? (weekly question) Are you confident the Lions are headed in the right direction? (recurring poll) Our recurring “confidence the Lions are headed in the right direction” survey results hit an all-time low in the Dan Campbell era last week, plummeting to a meager 12%. However, after hanging 45 points on the Cardinals in Week 5 and the defense showing signs of improvement, it’ll be interesting to see if this survey rebounds this week. As for our new survey this week, the Lions are on the cusp of returning two key starters from injury in the next two weeks, as safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays have opened their 21-day evaluation windows and could return as soon as Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers, as Campbell noted last week: “They won’t have other teammates around, running plays and all that stuff, but they’re going to be here continuing to condition, get ready (during the bye week),” Campbell said on Friday. “As (much) football stuff as they can do without it being that with the training staff. Then let’s get them going Green Bay week. Let’s get them going, and then we’ll assess. Hopefully by midweek, we’ll have a pretty good idea (if they can return to play).” Note: Since we’re looking a bit ahead this week, the Lions Week 7 opening betting line against the Packers, set by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook , is already at Lions -3.5 points and could shift if the Lions can return Branch and Mays. While each player’s return is still to be determined, our question this week hopes to uncover which Lions player returning from injury do fans think will have the most immediate impact? When Branch returns, he should jump directly into a starting role, creating a rippling effect on the Lions secondary. However, Achilles’ injuries are notoriously difficult to return to form from, and it could be a while before we see the Pro Bowl version of Branch that Lions fans have become accustomed to. Mays is also expected to step back into a starting role once he returns, but with Juice Scruggs playing well, might the Lions consider taking their time returning their prized free agent to play? We have also added an “other” option for fans this week, in case anyone believes another player expected to return from an injury list this year might be more impactful. The players eligible for this include safety Kerby Joseph, safety Thomas Harper, running back Isiah Pacheco, and offensive lineman Giovanni Manu, who was recently spotted at practice working with trainers. And with that, it’s time to vote in the Feed surveys below, sound off in the comments, and check back with Pride of Detroit later in the week for the results. Which returning player is most important? Are you confident in the Lions? Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys:

title: Packers Injury Report: Keisean Nixon returns to practice
summary: As we wrote earlier today, the Green Bay Packers no longer have the freedom to have players on the 53-man roster miss games with injury without making some sort of corresponding moves to bring in their replacements. Here’s the good news: One player who did not practice on Wednesday, cornerback Keisean Nixon, practiced on Thursday, […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we wrote earlier today, the Green Bay Packers no longer have the freedom to have players on the 53-man roster miss games with injury without making some sort of corresponding moves to bring in their replacements . Here’s the good news: One player who did not practice on Wednesday, cornerback Keisean Nixon, practiced on Thursday, even though he was limited. The bad news? Receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (Achilles), defensive lineman Jonathan Ford (calf) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) missed a second straight day of practice. The assumption is that Hargrave will go on the injured reserve soon for his torn Achilles, while it appears that Moore will miss a couple of weeks with an ankle injury that has left him in a boot and on a scooter. While St-Juste’s and Ford’s injuries haven’t been discussed much in press conferences, their missing back-to-back practices means that their chances to play on Sunday are likely in doubt. At minimum, the team will need to bring up an extra receiver this week, be it Savion Williams (who is currently practicing with the team despite being on the injured reserve list) or a practice squad option (Isaiah Neyor, Quincy Skinner Jr. or Coleman Owen). Once Hargrave goes on the injured reserve, the Packers will have two open roster spots on the 53-man roster, and they’ll also have the option to use two game-day practice squad elevations this week, which should help smooth out the holes on the roster if the injured players can’t suit up against the Dallas Cowboys. To keep it simple, think of the Packers’ roster situation this way: Functionally, with the expectation that Hargrave will go on IR soon, the team has a 51-man roster. A game-day roster is made of 48 players, and the Packers rarely carry more than 8 offensive linemen into games, but they’re currently carrying 11 on the active roster. You can basically lock in that Green Bay will scratch three offensive linemen already, leaving them with the minimum of 48 players — the amount needed to fill a game-day roster…but that’s with the assumption that all of those players will be healthy. So for every injured player who can’t play on Sunday (besides offensive linemen or Hargrave), the team will need to backfill (likely at the same position). #Packers injury report: NT Jonathan Ford was a DNP, which means they may be very thin at the position Sunday vs. the #Cowboys . pic.twitter.com/UF0fNfYfNI — Tom Silverstein (@TomSilverstein) October 15, 2026 Beyond the non-participants, the following players were listed as limited for a second-straight practice: guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), defensive lineman Anthony Campbell (ankle), offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles, practice window player), receiver Savion Williams (ankle, practice window player) and defensive lineman Devonte Wyatt (ankle, practice window player). On the Cowboys’ end of the injury report, their non-participants on Thursday were cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring). Their limited players in practice were linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). To say the least, one of these teams is a bit more banged up than the other.

title: Josh Jacobs sues to stop video evidence from being released
summary: According to WBAY, Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is suing the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department, which is in charge of deciding whether or not a video from Jacobs’ garage will be released as part of his battery and criminal damage to property case. Yesterday, it was reported that the police department delayed the release […]
full_text: (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to WBAY, Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is suing the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department , which is in charge of deciding whether or not a video from Jacobs’ garage will be released as part of his battery and criminal damage to property case. Yesterday, it was reported that the police department delayed the release of evidence , requested by media outlets, on the basis that the department “has received written notifications from attorneys representing the record subjects of their intentions to seek judicial orders restraining disclosure.” One would guess that the subjects would be Jacobs, who initially filed the first temporary seal of evidence in the case, and the victim, who filed a permanent seal of evidence in the case, but we do not have confirmation of that. Earlier in the legal process, a judge ruled that the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department should make the final judgment on whether or not to seal the evidence permanently, not the judge. Reports claim that the NFL is attempting to access the video, but that they haven’t been able to yet. On record, head coach Matt LaFleur has stated that neither he nor the Packers have seen the video, either. Currently, Jacobs is on the league’s commissioner exempt list, a placeholder for a suspension. The league will treat Jacobs’ time on the exempt list as time served toward a suspension, but they only have one opportunity to suspend Jacobs for a single violation of the personal conduct policy, as the NFL learned the hard way after the Ray Rice incident — when Rice was originally suspended for two games, later suspended indefinitely when video of his domestic abuse incident was published by TMZ and then the league had to eventually pay Rice back for all the games he missed beyond the two-game suspension. Below is what WBAY wrote about the lawsuit: Online court records show Jacobs filed a lawsuit Thursday for, “Permanent Injunction, Protective Order, and Order Restricting Access to Records Under Wis. Stat.19.356.” The materials include police reports, dispatch audio, investigative notes, and specifically video footage recorded inside Jacobs’ private residential garage that was obtained via a search warrant. Jacobs argues in the suit that releasing interior footage of his garage exposes his home’s layout, access points, security setups, and valuables. Because his professional sports schedule and travel dates are public, he argues this creates a severe, irreversible risk of targeted burglary, break-ins, or harassment. Jacobs joins and supports the requests of the identified victim (identified as “ANM” in the document), arguing that public disclosure would violate Wisconsin victim privacy rights (known as Marsy’s Law), cause re-victimization, and lead to public exposure that cannot be prevented by simple redaction due to modern AI identification tools. “ANM is a crime victim who seeks closure, not public attention,” the suit states. Jacobs is asking a judge to issue a permanent injunction barring the police department from releasing the garage footage and any identifying or sensitive details regarding the victim, arguing that personal safety and privacy far outweigh the public’s interest in seeing the records. According to the document, the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department has 20 days to respond.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Bigger challenge awaits Packers’ secondary on Sunday night
summary: The Green Bay Packers’ defense had a marvelous performance in Week 5. The unit recorded nearly as many turnovers (five) as they allowed points in a 31-7 victory over the Chicago Bears. That team, which cycled through backup quarterbacks Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum, had put up 375 yards or more in its two games […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 17: (L-R) George Pickens #3 and CeeDee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys celebrate a touchdown during the second quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on November 17, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers’ defense had a marvelous performance in Week 5. The unit recorded nearly as many turnovers (five) as they allowed points in a 31-7 victory over the Chicago Bears. That team, which cycled through backup quarterbacks Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum, had put up 375 yards or more in its two games without Caleb Williams coming in, but they couldn’t cross the 250-yard mark against Green Bay. This week, however, the Packers should have a tougher challenge on their hands. Chicago’s offense centers on the run game, but the Dallas Cowboys, who come into Lambeau Field for Sunday Night Football, have been doing their work through the air. Dallas has one of the most efficient offense in football on a per-drive basis to this point in the season, and most of that is due to a passing game that features a top wideout tandem of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The Packers have their own ascending receiver pairing, and although the Dallas duo are certainly more established, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should have plenty of opportunities against a Dallas defense that ranks 31st in yards per pass attempt allowed. But on the other side of the ball Green Bay needs to find a way to limit Lamb and Pickens defensively. Lamb did not play in last year’s 40-40 tie at AT&T Stadium, but Pickens caught 8 passes for 134 yards and two scores. Injuries could impact the Packers’ secondary this week as well, so let’s take a look at that as we slowly make our way towards Sunday Night Football. Packers ‘can’t shy away’ from Cowboys’ explosive offense | Packers.com Dallas is 7th in the NFL in scoring, 3rd in points per drive, and first in yards per drive and plays per drive. It’s going to be a challenge for Green Bay’s defense to get off the field without giving up points. Packers safety Xavier McKinney back to hunting interceptions | Packersnews.com ($) On the encouraging side, McKinney had a huge game last Sunday and looks rejuvenated after a bit of a down 2025 season. Packers CB Keisean Nixon misses practice ahead of matchup with Cowboys WR duo | Packers Wire Not encouraging is two of the Packers’ cornerbacks missing practice (Nixon and Benjamin St-Juste). We Asked About Play-Action Passing; Packers Provided Explosive Answer | SI.com The Packers did identify an advantage with play-action against the Bears, however, as Jordan Love went 12-for-13 for 245 yards and a score. Micah Parsons wants to ensure ‘all the small things fixed first’ before return | ESPN It sounds like the big concern now before he can return is making sure that everything is balanced and he won’t be overcompensating for the recovering ACL with different muscles. That said, if it were playoff time, he said he’d be playing, so he’s hopefully getting close. What do you think? Is the Cowboys’ terrible defense bad enough to let this running game finally get on track? title: The Packers have a locker room sledgehammer
summary: In a sentence I’m nearly positive has never been written before: the Green Bay Packers are trying something different with a rotating team sledgehammer. We’ve seen things like AJ Dillon’s positivity rabbit in the Eagles locker room, and Chicago White Sox pitcher Mike Vasil’s magic wand, and now the Packers are getting in on the […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a sentence I’m nearly positive has never been written before: the Green Bay Packers are trying something different with a rotating team sledgehammer. We’ve seen things like AJ Dillon’s positivity rabbit in the Eagles locker room , and Chicago White Sox pitcher Mike Vasil’s magic wand , and now the Packers are getting in on the fun. There’s a sledge hammer in the #Packers locker room labeled with the team’s three wins on it vs. the Jets, Buccaneers, and Bears with Isaiah McDuffie’s, Javon Bullard’s and Barryn Sorrell’s numbers burned into it: — Carson Fowler (@CarsonFowlerTV) October 14, 2026 When asked about the sledgehammer, LB Barryn Sorrell clarified that it’s passed around week to week when a player has a big hit on special teams. Sorrell is the proud owner of the hammer this week (is that another new sentence?) after his big hit on “some Bear” during Sunday’s rout of Chicago. Barryn Sorrell earned the sledgehammer after delivering a big special teams hit against the Bears on Sunday. The award is passed around the locker room each week. @NBC26 pic.twitter.com/sq3DXct5b5 — Kelly Hallinan (@kellyhals) October 14, 2026 Sorrell explained that, yes, it’s just a hammer, but it brings a “competitive nature to the locker room”, and you know what? WHATEVER WORKS. The winner of the hammer will have his number engraved into the handle each week. No word on who gets the hammer at the end of the year or if they’ll have to lead a sing-along with one of the greatest music videos in history , but I have to assume they’ll all be fighting over who gets to hold the Lombardi Trophy at that time, so the hammer will be an afterthought.

title: Packers Injury Report: How will Green Bay use its open roster spots?
summary: For the most part, my injury analysis this season has basically boiled down to “next man up on the 53-man roster.” The Green Bay Packers’ cluster of injuries has mostly hit two units, the offensive and defensive lines — where the team has been over-signed since they made their initial active roster — leaving them […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the most part, my injury analysis this season has basically boiled down to “next man up on the 53-man roster.” The Green Bay Packers’ cluster of injuries has mostly hit two units, the offensive and defensive lines — where the team has been over-signed since they made their initial active roster — leaving them without needing to call players up from the practice squad. The two exceptions so far have been the promotion of running back Pierre Strong Jr. (for Chris Brooks, who went on IR) and linebacker Kristian Welch (for Edgerrin Cooper, who went on IR). This week, though, the Packers’ active roster might be stress-tested beyond a one-off injury at a position for the first time. Let’s take a look at Green Bay’s current roster and where it stands going into Week 6, as the team prepares to face off against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football . Roster Situation – 51 “healthy” Excluding defensive lineman Javon Hargrave, who should go on the injured reserve for a season-ending Achilles injury soon , the team functionally has a 51-man active roster (along with a full 17-man practice squad). Here’s the positional breakdown of the roster (again, excluding Hargrave): QB: Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor RB: MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson WR: Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Skyy Moore, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant TE: Tucker Kraft, Mark Redman, Jonnu Smith and Josh Whyle OL: Jordan Morgan, Laken Tomlinson, Sean Rhyan, Travis Glover, Anthony Belton, Aaron Banks, Kevin Zeitler, Jager Burton, John Williams, Jacob Monk and Donovan Jennings DL: Karl Brooks, Devonte Wyatt, Chris McClellan, Jonathan Ford and Anthony Campbell ED: Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr. and Dani Dennis-Sutton LB: Zaire Franklin, Isaiah McDuffie, Ty’Ron Hopper, Nick Niemann and Kristian Welch CB: Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse, Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste and Kamal Hadden S: Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams, Javon Bullard and Kitan Oladapo K: Trey Smack P: Daniel Whelan LS: Matt Orzech On paper, if all these players were healthy, no position screams “we need a warm body” for the Packers, but the team isn’t fully healthy. If all of these players could 100 percent suit up against the Cowboys, they could easily piece together a 48-man game-day roster without breaking a sweat (the three inactives would likely all be offensive linemen, as the team currently carries 11 on the 53). The Packers’ Injury Situation Keisean Nixon listed as DNP with a groin on the first injury report of the week. pic.twitter.com/URq49GKD43 — Eric Boynton (@ericboynton) October 14, 2026 On Wednesday, the Packers’ non-participants in practice (the non-Hargrave players we should worry the most about missing Sunday’s action) were: WR Skyy Moore – ankle DL Jonathan Ford – calf CB Keisean Nixon – groin CB Benjamin St-Juste – hamstring That…puts the team in a bind. Let’s say there’s a worst-case scenario situation for Green Bay and all of those players are unable to suit up for the Packers; it would leave the team with four receivers, four interior defensive linemen and just three cornerbacks (including Kamal Hadden, who has almost exclusively been a slot defender in both the preseason and regular season this year). To my memory, Green Bay has never kept numbers that low at any of those positions for a game-day roster in head coach Matt LaFleur’s time with the Packers. Simply put: If any of these players can’t dress for the Dallas game, a body needs to come up to replace them, be it an addition to the 53-man roster or a game-day elevation from the practice squad (which are different, and we’ll get into why the Packers may use one instead of the other). Potential Reinforcements Here’s some good news: receiver Savion Williams (ankle) had his practice window with the team open up last week and was a limited participant on Wednesday, along with defensive lineman Jordon Riley — who began to practice with the team much sooner than expected from his 2025 season-ending Achilles injury. It’s probably hard to count on Riley jumping up to the active roster with just one week of practice under his belt, but at least he’s trending in a positive direction. It seems much more likely that Williams would be activated this week to help replace Skyy Moore’s reps on offense and in the return game. For what it’s worth, Moore was seen in a boot after his ankle injury on Sunday and on a scooter on Wednesday . It wouldn’t be out of left field for him to land on the injured reserve, based on the little we know about his injury — if the team needs the numbers. So the Packers can sort of handle the Moore injury (if Williams can go) without tapping into the practice squad, but the defensive line and cornerback rooms would probably rely on practice squad movement if guys can’t play. Right now, Green Bay’s interior defensive lineman on the practice squad is David Blay Jr., who was signed in Week 4, and their cornerbacks are Domani Jackson, a rookie draft pick, and Elijah Culp, who was signed this week. Notably, the Packers went out of their way to sign a second practice squad cornerback on Monday, the first time all year that the team has had two at the position. Green Bay has been pretty thin at defensive back this year, from a numbers perspective, a result of the team being “oversigned” at the offensive line, defensive line and tight end positions for 2026 on the full 70-man roster (potentially at running back and edge defender, too, depending on your definition). The pinch at the cornerback position is pretty explainable. Two injuries at one position usually demand a move. On the defensive line, it’s been a stretch of bad luck for the team. Warren Brinson is already on the IR, and Hargrave will meet him there soon. On top of that, Nazir Stackhouse was claimed on waivers at the cutdown deadline (after the Packers carried seven interior defensive linemen on their initial roster) and Jaden Crumedy, the team’s initial practice squad option, was poached by the Houston Texans’ 53-man roster. This led the team to eventually fill the practice role with Blay, and the Ford injury means that there’s a chance Blay actually is a game-day active in Week 6. What to Watch in Week 6 Pay attention to the injury report this week. The Packers aren’t exactly a skeleton crew, but their last remaining healthy scratch options on the roster as it stands today are just three offensive linemen. For every non-offensive lineman who doesn’t play on Sunday, Green Bay will probably need to make an activation from either the IR/PUP list (Williams/Riley) or the practice squad. Worth mentioning here: If the Packers do call a player up from the practice squad to the 53-man roster (rather than a game-day elevation), they might not have a chance to get them back to the practice squad. With how the league’s rules work, teams are much more interested in claiming a player who is waived (when the original team is trying to get them back down to the practice squad) than poaching a player from another team’s practice squad. When players are claimed on waivers, they are not guaranteed any weeks of service by their new team. On the other hand, if a new team poaches a player from a different team’s practice squad, that player is guaranteed three weeks of game checks and his spot on the 53-man roster must be exhausted by that poaching team for that entire period. In short, teams have to make a bigger commitment to a poached practice squadder than to claim a waived former 53-man member. That may sound counterintuitive, but it’s true. For example, the Packers had offensive lineman Brant Banks on their practice squad last year, and he was never poached from their practice squad, but when Banks was elevated to the 53-man roster and then waived (as the team attempted to get him back down to their practice squad), he was claimed by the Tennessee Titans (for less than three weeks, at which point he…

title: Texans trade for Pollyanna
summary: With an ever present smile, Houston Texans head coach Demeco Ryans ended his latest post-game presser with “Yes, alright, we traded for Marvin Harrison. See ya!” Dictionary.com Pollyanna, NOUN an excessively or blindly optimistic person. Even when the team is 1-4, with the only win coming against the Tennessee Titans, literally the worst team in […]
full_text: Oct 1, 2022; Columbus, Ohio, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) and wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (18) celebrate after the game against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Ohio Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-USA TODAY Sports With an ever present smile, Houston Texans head coach Demeco Ryans ended his latest post-game presser with “Yes, alright, we traded for Marvin Harrison. See ya!” Dictionary.com Pollyanna, NOUN an excessively or blindly optimistic person. Even when the team is 1-4, with the only win coming against the Tennessee Titans, literally the worst team in pro football, Ryans is smiling. He’s upbeat, joyful, seemingly convinced that no matter how dark the day gets, the sun is rising. All this, despite the current up-ending of the Texans hopes and dreams for 2026, which has left fans in everything but a smiling mood. DeMeco Ryans to @jharrisfootball on getting Marvin Harrison Jr. & speaking on the phone with him: “I’m fired up. To add a guy of Marvin‘s caliber, it’s a huge get for us. Huge get for the Texans. I’m fired up for Marvin, when you’re in a situation & it may not be going great, to… pic.twitter.com/BrnPFraOTT — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) October 12, 2026 Max Barlow over at Casino Gurus, unveiled a new number cruncher for tracking teams dubbed the NFL Pressure Index. In this, we see the following reasons for fans’ frowns to remain upside down The NFL Pressure Index combines underperformance against preseason expectations (27.8%), recent form (22.2%), painful defeats (15%), playoff pressure (15%), injuries (10%) and performance red flags (10%) to produce a score out of 100. The Texans rank as the NFL’s 7th most pressured team: Scoring 68.8/100 on the NFL Pressure Index. They have suffered the NFL’s biggest drop in playoff hopes: Their estimated postseason probability has fallen by 33.3%, from 59% to 25%. Houston is falling short of preseason expectations: The Texans entered the season with a projected win total of 9.5 games, but have started 1-4, 1.8 wins behind their expected total at this stage. They suffered a particularly painful defeat against Dallas in Week 4: Houston reached an 82% in-game win probability before eventually losing 34-30. The Texans pressure has however reduced since Week 3: Their score has fallen 17.0 points, from 85.8 to 68.8, moving from 2nd to 7th in the rankings. Thankfully, the Texans index score has risen to 68.8, as listed in the last bullet point above. Who currently holds the biggest disappointment? The Los Angeles Chargers roll into the weekend at 89.2/100. At least they have plenty of beaches to enjoy in January. In trading a 2nd round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr. last weekend, Nick Caserio and the Houston Texans attacked this index. While many people think the price was too steep, word on the street was: The Arizona Cardinals demanded a 2nd round pick for MHJ C.J. Stroud lobbied for Houston to bring MHJ to town The Indianapolis Colts were working to land him So, giving up a future 2nd round pick to A) land a player your QB wants to play catch with and B) prevent that player from going to your division rival is a win/win on paper. Especially with 1) there’s no guarantee that 2nd round pick was going to bring a player of MHJ’s caliber and 2) Caserio is a horse-trading, card shark who likely will package up something in the off-season to get someone else’s 2nd round pick. Will the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade fix all that ails the Texans? Anyone who thinks this team was 1 player away from the Super Bowl hasn’t been paying attention. C.J. Stroud has been balling out, having the best season of his career. And that’s in spite of the abysmal offensive line play, ghosted running game, and head-scratchingly bad defense. #Texans QB CJ Stroud so far this season: • 119/185 (64.3%) • 1,402 passing yards • 7 total TDs • 0 INTs • 98.1 passer rating I wouldn’t count out Houston digging its way out of an 0-4 start if Stroud keeps this up. pic.twitter.com/UTRdunfQ36 — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 12, 2026 While bringing in MHJ to play catch with his former college QB is certainly a positive on the surface, all the passing yards and receiving touchdowns won’t prevent the defense from giving up last minute game winners to the opposition. Trading for Derrick Henry might have done more for the team’s fortunes, especially with David Montgomery in the MASH tent. Woody Marks is a quality tailback, but he’s not going to run for 2k behind this poorly coached O-line. Yet, hope remains. This is the last time Marvin Harrison Jr. caught a pass from C.J. Stroud by the way: pic.twitter.com/5oMUEecXr9 — Stephen Means (@Stephen_Means) October 11, 2026 A lot of people are throwing around the term “bust” when it comes to Marvin Harrison Jr. right now. In his rookie year (2024), Harrison had 16 starts, 116 targets, 62 catches, 885 yards, a 14.3 yard per catch average and 8 touchdowns. All this on the arm of Kyler Murray, who hasn’t exactly been the greatest QB in the league. He did, however, have his 2nd best season when MHJ was a rookie, then fell off soon there after. While a lot of talking heads are calling MHJ a bust, saying he shouldn’t have been drafted that high, Houston overpaid for him, etc., some people who should know, say things that give Ryans a reason to keep smiling. "I had never seen him not go 100 percent on his routes. When I started seeing that the last couple weeks… I knew it was time" HOFer Cris Carter on the return of Maserati Marv in Houston. @criscarter80 | @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/Nj8h9Jqo7q — Up & Adams (@UpAndAdamsShow) October 12, 2026 Steve Smith on Marvin Harrison Jr last week pic.twitter.com/BZNmgQxYgp — Forever Trill🇳🇬 🇰🇪 🇧🇸 (@mccauley318) October 12, 2026 This Sunday’s London game in Wembley Stadium against the Jacksonville Jaguars is likely too soon to see a true glimpse into what a Stroud>Nico Collins>Harrison Jr. passing attack looks like. But, don’t be surprised if he makes a statement to show the world the Arizona Cardinals mis-used him. Will Marvin Harrison Jr. fix all that ails Nick Caley? In this is where the smile might sink. Harrison was drafted into a poor situation in Phoenix, marginalized, underutilized, and ultimately shelved. How much of this is bad coaching, a poor-scheme fit and a product of the design-the-airplane-in-flight approach to the Cardinals offense over the last several seasons remains to be seen. It’s easy to believe the narrative, that Harrison has been saved from the bad guys, brought to the good guys, and will now save the day. Especially when watching Ryans light up when he talks about the new wideout. But we all know the bad coaching existed in Arizona because we’re all too familiar with seeing it here in H-Town. Nick Caley would likely struggle to run a top tier offense in the Big Ten, much less the AFC South. Ben McDaniels (wide receivers/passing game coordinator) and Jerry Shuplinski (QB coach) seem to be the lone bright spots on the Texans offensive coaching staff, however. Here's where I'm at with the whole Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans deal and I'll try to be objective as I can be. -From what I have heard and seen, the Cardinals asked MHJ to do a lot of stuff that just doesn't match his specific skillset & tools. Playing middle of the field… https://t.co/i86ohs04Zj — Merrill Hess (@ICDeadPpl95) October 14, 2026 And, MHJ will operate largely under their guidance. Which means, Pollyanna might just thrive in Space City after all. For those who love to complain: if MHJ does thrive, it might buy Caley more time before the axe eventually falls. A stellar passing game masks the inadequacies of just how bad this offense really is, and Caley benefits most from that masking. For those who embrace Pollyanna: Winning cures all. And if MHJ can help this team take another AFC South win this weekend, hope will reignite. At this stage, the only real chance this team has of making the playoffs is securing the 4th straight…

title: Value of Things: By the Numbers
summary: Last week we did some internal scouting on the Texans offense. This week we shift our attention to the defense. As we do with most things, we break down the overall numbers into their individual parts. The key to the Texans defense has always been two-fold. You shut down the opponents running game and then […]
full_text: Last week we did some internal scouting on the Texans offense. This week we shift our attention to the defense. As we do with most things, we break down the overall numbers into their individual parts. The key to the Texans defense has always been two-fold. You shut down the opponents running game and then make the opposing quarterbacks day miserable. The Texans have been particularly good under DeMeco Ryans on the last part of that statement. Instead of doing totals it is usually better to look at these things game by game. When you have only five games on the schedule you can have one or two games that skew results one way or another. Only the 2000 Baltimore Ravens and 1985 Chicago Bears have been dominant enough to dominate all of their opponents. For most teams we are looking at a preponderance of the evidence. So, let’s start with the game by game running defense results. Rushing Defense Attempts Yards YPC Bills 21 86 4.1 Bengals 23 85 3.7 Colts 31 89 2.9 Cowboys 25 75 3.0 Titans 18 57 3.2 So, when you look at it this way you would have to say that the Texans defense is as good as it has always been against the run. Furthermore, they have been getting steadily better since the Buffalo game. That makes perfect sense since Josh Allen is one of the better running quarterbacks in the NFL. Additionally, the Texans have been getting healthier as they got Kayden McDonald back in the defensive tackle rotation. They also got Alzeez Al-Shaair back as well. The big key are the attempts. The opponents are not even trying to run the ball anymore. This is even though every game except for the Titans game has either been competitive or opponents have been playing ahead. That should tell us something. It tells us one of two things. Either teams are giving up on the run because it has been ineffective or because the pass has become more effective. Again, we can look at totals and that could tell us a lot, but I would prefer to look at the quarterbacks and how successful they have been. The Texans defense has famously made some really good quarterbacks look really awful on the season. The good news is that three of the first four quarterbacks are generally regarded as top ten quarterbacks in the NFL. However, the numbers might tell us something else. Passing Defense COM ATT PCT Yards TD/INT Rating Josh Allen 20 29 69.0 334 2/0 130.5 Joe Burrow 20 31 64.5 207 2/0 105.2 Daniel Jones 24 36 66.7 235 1/1 82.5 Dak Prescott 32 45 71.1 335 1/0 99.8 Cam Ward 23 36 63.9 170 0/1 63.4 So, this is a glass half empty and half full deal. The three elite quarterbacks played like elite quarterbacks. The two that aren’t didn’t. So, the good news is that we aren’t making bad or average quarterbacks look good. We just aren’t making any of the good ones look bad. Obviously, what this means for the future depends on where you would peg Trevor Lawrence and the quarterbacks that follow. To put it another way, we are looking at C.J. Stroud as having his best season since his rookie year. How would we feel about his performance if these were his games? For one, his completion percentage would be higher than it is now, but he would have fewer yards. The six touchdowns and two interceptions would be slightly worse overall than what he is currently producing. The aggregate pass rating is almost exactly what Stroud is putting up at 96.3. Those are the numbers. The whys and what fors are generally more difficult to pinpoint. For one, it is clear that Kamari Lassiter is not having the same kind of season he had last year. Is it a blip on the radar or have other teams figured him out? Secondly, Reed Blankenship obviously struggled in his first few games as a Texan. Again, is this is a situation of him feeling out his place in the defense or was his signing a mistake? These are all important questions moving forward. DeMeco Ryans taking back the playcalling is only in its first week. We honestly don’t know if this last week was an uptick or just the Titans being the Titans. One thing is also true. This team hasn’t generated turnovers like they did last season. That could be blind luck or a sign that they are not as good. Either is equally likely at this point and probably both are true in some respects. One thing is for certain, if defenses keep carving up the Texans in the passing game then they will have to try different coverages, blitz packages, and other wrinkles because simply being better than everyone else is not working this year like it has in seasons past.

title: Is “at least he didn’t turn it over” the new standard for Colts football?
summary: Daniel Jones gave the ball to the Pittsburgh Steelers five times when they met back in 2025. He didn’t turn it over this year. Unfortunately, the result was still the same. Actually, the final score was somehow worse. Jones not turning the ball over is the silver lining some fans are clinging to in order […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 11: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts looks down field during the third quarter of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Daniel Jones gave the ball to the Pittsburgh Steelers five times when they met back in 2025. He didn’t turn it over this year. Unfortunately, the result was still the same. Actually, the final score was somehow worse. Jones not turning the ball over is the silver lining some fans are clinging to in order to feel better about another lackluster performance from the Indianapolis Colts. It marks a disappointing moment for this organization. Yes, a five turnover performance to the Steelers last year was awful. Zero turnovers last week was a vast improvement, but is that the new measuring stick? It doesn’t include fumbles, but Aaron Rodgers attempted 402 straight passes without an interception. That is a record and an outlier, but holding someone like Rodgers, especially in his prime, to a statement like, “well, at least he held onto the ball this time” would be unheard of. Before attacking, I am not saying Jones needs to have 402 pass attempts without an interception to be deemed great or even good. There is a lot of area in between Rodgers’ record-setting year and Jones’ five turnover game, last week’s performance being one of them. A zero turnover game should be more of the rule than the hoped and prayed for exception. Even thinking that shows how far this franchise has fallen since Manning and Luck. The Colts used to win. They used to win big. Now, we are seeing below average games and thinking “it could have been worse”. Daniel Jones isn’t the answer. Not in this league. Chris Ballard and the Colts put their faith in him, but Jones isn’t going to drag the Colts to greatness. Ever since that AFC Finalist banner was hung, the Colts have been too comfortable with “at least he didn’t turn it over” type of performances.

Jason Kelce will have a meet and greet with fans from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m. Tyreek Hill rumors: Do Chiefs even have room for WR after reworking record-breaking offense? | CBS Sports Most signs point toward this move. The Chiefs’ best home run threat, Tyquan Thornton, dislocated his ankle in Week 4, which puts the rest of his season in doubt. Plus, Mahomes’ connection with Xavier Worthy has never materialized. Mahomes is 8-for-37 targeting Worthy on deep balls, the worst completion rate (21.6%) among 38 duos with 25+ targets since 2024. An already thin WR room could take another hit at any moment, too, based on Rashee Rice’s track record. Mahomes led the NFL with 41 touchdown passes on deep balls from 2018-21. He had just SEVEN in four-plus seasons since. Aidan O’Connell has more in that span (eight) for crying out loud! That’s the Tyreek Hill effect. Three Ways Josh Simmons’ Eventual Return Can Help Chiefs Moving Forward | Sports Illustrated To this point, per TruMedia , Kansas City has the third-highest share of passes at or behind the line of scrimmage at 32.0%. It’s also in the bottom 10 in average yards to the sticks at -1.6, as well as in the top 10 in percentage of throws faster than 2.5 seconds (44.5%). A quick-game passing attack isn’t fun for anyone and, more importantly, it leaves infinitely less margin for error. Just ask the 2024 and 2025 Chiefs. Losing wide receiver Tyquan Thornton to an ankle injury hurts, surely, but the return of Simmons figures to potentially unleash the version of the Kansas City offense that was imagined during training camp. Could the Lions trade for Kristian Fulton? He still sees risk there. “All it takes is one bad play for that injury to flare up and for him to be out for a period of time, and then suddenly now you only have three good cornerbacks that you feel comfortable and confident with putting out there,” Goldman said. The Chiefs have reason to think twice. The old NFL saying is that you can never have too many cornerbacks, and that applies to Kansas City right now. His 4 yards per attempt were the fourth lowest in a game this season by any starting quarterback. In the “Thursday Night Football” postgame show on Amazon Prime, analyst and 17-year NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick had some strong words while assessing Nix’s performance. “I’m glad (the Broncos) scored the two touchdowns in the first half, but they were in four-minute mode when the second half started,” Fitzpatrick said. “It was really frustrating to watch. And part of it for me is Bo Nix is not playing competitively. It’s almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he’s playing football right now.” Texans RB Montgomery, S Pitre out for London affair vs. Jaguars | ESPN The Texans will travel to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars without at least a pair of starters. Houston (1-4) ruled running back David Montgomery (groin) and safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder) out for Sunday’s matchup against the Jaguars (4-1) at Wembley Stadium. Montgomery and Pitre, who suffered their respective injuries during last week’s 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans, have started every game this season for the Texans. New report links Greg Olsen to Monday Night Football in 2027 | Pro Football Talk It’s just a prediction, but Ourand wouldn’t throw something like that around unless he had good reason to believe it. Hovering over any of the top spots will be Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, who has the chops and the cachet to pick his spot and name his price. Olsen, who has won multiple Emmys (including the most recent one, from his spot on the Fox “B” team) seems destined to land with a No. 1 team, somewhere. Whether that’s ESPN, CBS, or Prime Video, it seems inevitable that Olsen, who was bumped to the bench because Fox wanted Tom Brady, will once again have a prime spot, somewhere. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Eric Bieniemy on Chiefs’ passionate moments: ‘It’s all about survival’ “Sometimes, you’re going to agree with things, and sometimes you’re going to disagree with things, but if there’s something that has taken place out on the field, they may have a better point of view than what we do off the field, so I want them to feel comfortable coming to share that stuff with me,” Bieniemy said. The short video made it clear that Bieniemy was listening to Mahomes and making an effort to hear him out. Chiefs Wide receiver Rashee Rice (Hamstring) did not participate in practice for the second consecutive day. He tweaked his hamstring during the first quarter of the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . Reid provided an update on Rice on Wednesday . Left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) was a limited participant in practice again, marking the 2025 first-round pick’s second time on the practice field since the team was in training camp. For more about Simmons, here are Reid’s comments from Wednesday . Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (Neck) was added to the injury report Thursday as a limited participant in practice. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (Knee) was a limited participant in practice. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. The following players were full participants in practice for the second consecutive day: Safety Chamarri Conner (Knee) Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (Knee) Chargers The Chargers listed 20 players on their initial injury report. Tackle Joe Alt (neck), guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Tre’ Harris (hamstring), cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring), and safety Derwin James (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday. Pass rusher Khalil Mack sat on Wednesday, but he returned from the rest day on Thursday. Outside linebacker Bud Dupree (NIR – Rest) did not practice on Thursday after limited participation on Wednesday due to a neck injury. Cornerback Rodney Shelley (Hamstring) did not practice on Thursday after limited participation on Wednesday. Alt, Awosika, Jackson and James all missed the Chargers’ Week 5 contest against the Denver Broncos . Harris left during the game with a hamstring injury and did not return. Defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell (knee), defensive tackle Justin Egoigbe (shoulder), linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee), wide receiver Quentin Johnston (chest), wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), wide receiver Ladd McConkey (foot), defensive back Elijah Molden (hamstring), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad), defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring) and safety Kendall Williamson (ankle) were limited on both days. Johnston and Thompson did not play against Denver. McConkey was nominally active on Sunday, but he did not enter the game against the Broncos. Lambert-Smith is on Los Angeles’ Reserve/Injured list but has been designated to return. Wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling was a full participant in practice on Thursday after limited participation on Wednesday. Tight end Charlie Kolar is listed as a full participant on Wednesday.
