title: Scouting Jets wide receiver Sterling Shepard
summary: The Jets recently signed former Giants and Bucs receiver Sterling Shepard to their practice squad. Shepard has already been active a few times for the Jets. Today, we break him down in detail. The 33-year old Shepard is listed at 5’10” and 194 pounds and was a second round pick out of Oklahoma in 2016. […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 27: Sterling Shepard #87 of the New York Jets scores a two-point conversion during the fourth quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on September 27, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets recently signed former Giants and Bucs receiver Sterling Shepard to their practice squad. Shepard has already been active a few times for the Jets. Today, we break him down in detail. The 33-year old Shepard is listed at 5’10” and 194 pounds and was a second round pick out of Oklahoma in 2016. He has had a productive NFL career with 440 receptions for almost 5,000 yards and 25 touchdowns and although most of that production came early in his career, he has been a useful contributor over the last few seasons. Background Shepard was a four-star high school recruit and headed to Oklahoma in 2012. As a true freshman, he posted a 100-yard game in his second appearance. Over the course of the season, he started four games and caught 45 passes for 621 yards and three scores. In 2013, he started 12 of 13 games and ramped up his production with 51 catches for over 600 yards and seven scores. 2014 saw him level up again, as he had over 900 receiving yards with a month of the season still remaining. However, injuries down the stretch limited him and he ended the year with 51 catches for 970 yards and five touchdowns. This was good enough for first team all-Big 12 recognition, though. In his final college season, he was a first-teamer again and was also named as an all-American as he had 1,288 receiving yards on 86 catches, with 11 touchdowns. The season was highlighted by an overtime win over Tennessee where Shepard caught the game-tying and game-winning touchdowns. Shepard was drafted by the New York Giants with the 40th overall pick in the 2016 draft and immediately made an impact with a touchdown in his first game and a 100-yard game the following week, leading to an all-rookie season. Over his first five years, he established himself as a reliable producer, catching at least 57 passes and having over 650 receiving yards each year. He had 20 touchdowns and his highest single-season output for yardage was 872 in 2018. During the next three seasons with the Giants, Shepard – who had signed a four-year extension ahead of the 2019 season – saw his career take a downturn due to injuries. After a productive start to the 2021 season, Shepard missed several games and then suffered a season ending Achilles tear in December. Then, in 2022, he made his comeback and was again off to a decent start only to tear his ACL in week three. He was back in 2023, but struggled to crack the rotation and ended up with just 10 catches for 57 yards as it looked like his career might be winding down. In 2024, he ended up on the Bucs’ practice squad, where he reunited with his college teammate Baker Mayfield. It wasn’t long before he was elevated to the active roster and he ended up starting five times and racking up 32 catches for 334 yards and a score in 14 appearances in a bounceback campaign. The Bucs re-signed him for 2025 and he was again a useful player with 39 catches for 371 yards and a touchdown in 13 games, despite only making two starts. Shepard was without a team this year until preseason when he signed with the Texans. However, he was released in final cuts eight days later. The Jets added him to their practice squad in September and he was elevated for two games due to some injuries, catching two passes including a two-point conversion. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Shepard brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Shepard lacks ideal size but has big hands and is strong. He posted 20 bench press reps at the scouting combine. He also posted an impressive 41-inch vertical at the scouting combine, although the rest of his numbers, including a 4.48 in the 40-yard dash, were about average for his size. This was also over a decade ago. Usage Shepard has played in the slot 60 percent of the time at the NFL level but can still produce on the outside. In college he played outside in 2014 but in the slot in 2015 to showcase his versatility. He’s also been an option on jet sweeps and end arounds with 17 carries for 109 yards and a touchdown in college and 36 carries for 274 yards and a touchdown in the NFL. He played both running back and wide receiver in high school, while also playing basketball and participating in track and field events. Deep threat Shepard has a reputation as a possession receiver but has made plenty of downfield plays over the years and even led the Big 12 in yards per catch in 2014. He hasn’t been as effective as a downfield threat in recent years as he was early in his career but has still made the occasional downfield plays here and there. Hands Shepard is regarded as a sure-handed receiver who has a 67 percent catch rate for his career. He dropped 20 passes in his first three seasons but has improved his efficiency dramatically since then as he has never had more than five drops in any season since that time and had just one drop on 53 targets last year. He has a good ability to adjust to the ball and make tough catches in traffic. Shepard is also adept at going up to get it in fade situations and staying inbounds on sideline catches. Routes Shepard is an excellent route runner who deploys foot quickness, deception and strength to generate short area separation. He can run a full route tree and is excellent at tracking and locating the ball early so he can compete for it. Red zone Shepard racked up 27 touchdowns in four years at the collegiate level but has been less of a red zone threat at the NFL level. He had eight touchdowns as a rookie and has 26 in his career, but hasn’t had more than one in a season since 2020. Of those scores, 18 came from inside the red zone with eight inside the three-yard line, although only one of those eight was after 2020. The Jets did use him in the red zone on this clutch game-tying two-point conversion, though. After the catch Shepard doesn’t break a ton of tackles but has the ability to turn upfield and dive for the marker or pylon, and can turn a short pass into a big play with his speed. He has been a solid option on screen passes throughout his career, averaging nine yards per screen pass while in Tampa Bay. He did not fumble in college but has four at the NFL level. Blocking Shepard has earned a reputation as a willing blocker who gives a great effort and takes pride in his technique. Former Giants general manger Dave Gettleman once said he was “a hell of a blocker”. That effort was on display here as he hustled downfield to knock Josh Norman off a downfield tackle. In the same game, he also sprang a long touchdown run with this excellent block. He was actually awarded a game ball for this performance despite just catching two passes for 17 yards. He hasn’t been called for holding in his career but was flagged for an illegal crackback block and a couple of illegal block in the back penalties. Physicality Aside from his blocking, Shepard also showcases tenaciousness when running routes, carrying the ball and making catches in traffic. He is also good at fighting off press coverage. He can take things a little too far at times, though, as he has six offensive pass interference penalties in his career, in addition to four for unsportsmanlike conduct or unnecessary roughness. Special Teams Shepard had some experience as a punt returner in college, as he fielded 30 punts and averaged 7.4 yards per return. This came in handy in 2023 as the Giants had to use him as an emergency punt returner but he had just 10 yards on three returns with two fair catches and a muff. He also fielded one kickoff in college and gained 27 yards on a kickoff return after a lateral at the NFL level. title: Tension is building about Landon Dickerson’s future with the Eagles
summary: The Eagles offensive line has undergone significant changes since the 2025 iteration, from coaches to starters, things look entirely different for the group heading into Week 6 of the 2026 season. While many of the moves were out of the Eagles control, including injuries and Lane Johnson’s retirement, the move that spoke the loudest was […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles offensive line has undergone significant changes since the 2025 iteration, from coaches to starters, things look entirely different for the group heading into Week 6 of the 2026 season. While many of the moves were out of the Eagles control, including injuries and Lane Johnson’s retirement , the move that spoke the loudest was the team trading Cam Jurgens to the Ravens . All that uncertainty has bled into the discussion about Landon Dickerson’s future in Philly as the All Pro left guard prepares to return from IR. Dickerson was put on IR after a disappointing Week 1 performance , which prompted the team to move Jurgens over to left guard rather than put someone else at the position. Several weeks after the decision to move their center, Dickerson admitted on his 94WIP show that it wasn’t fair to ask Jurgens to move over to a new position and expect him to perform at a high level. Jurgens was on his way out of Philly just a few weeks later, and the starting o-line for Week 5 was Markell Bell (rookie), Tyler Steen, Jake Majors (backup for Drew Kendall, who took over at center when Jurgens was moved to LG), Willie Lampkin, and Jordan Mailata. Eagles GM Howie Roseman said that they saw enough from Kendall in his two games to feel comfortable moving forward with him at center and trade Jurgens. Now that Dickerson is returning from IR , head coach Nick Sirianni is being a little non-committal about whether the Pro Bowl LG will get back in the starting lineup. SIRIANNI: “There’s just so much time before we have to make any of these decisions. I’m not going to discuss too much of that, but we love Landon [Dickerson]. I know that. He’s won a lot of football games here because where he’s been. The guys that are in right now are doing a good job and fighting their butts off, but Landon’s a special player, and we’ll see where we are.” This answer didn’t appear to be Sirianni’s typical competitive advantage answer, it seemed like one he didn’t want to address because it’s not a certainty they give the job back to Dickerson. With so many new faces, and a list of injuries on offense that makes sustained success a challenge, the team might opt to look toward the future and get their young lineman more reps. Dickerson was asked on Wednesday after practice whether the team still views him as the long-term left guard, his answer wasn’t filled with confidence. DICKERSON: “That’s a great question. Do they have a media day for Nick and Howie? You can ask them.” The Athletic’s senior reporter Zach Berman reported that there was some playful banter as part of Dickerson’s exchange, and some of he deflection is just the LG’s style of answering questions. Still, after watching Jurgens get sent elsewhere, Dickerson has legitimate cause for concern, and only time will tell how Howie Roseman and the team view the remainder of the 2026 season.

title: Jalen Hurts is “out indefinitely” … now what for the Eagles?
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are going to be without Jalen Hurts for at least one game and quite possibly more while the team’s starting quarterback is treated for a “small blood clot.” NFL insider Ian Rapoport said Hurts is “out indefinitely.” We’re all rooting for his health to improve. In the meantime, the Eagles have to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles throws the ball during an NFL preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are going to be without Jalen Hurts for at least one game and quite possibly more while the team’s starting quarterback is treated for a “ small blood clot .” NFL insider Ian Rapoport said Hurts is “ out indefinitely .” We’re all rooting for his health to improve. In the meantime, the Eagles have to navigate the rest of the 2026 season. So, what are they going do? Here are some thoughts. Tanner McKee is set to start against the Carolina Panthers despite a turbulent offseason. The 2026 offseason began with McKee coming off a less than inspiring Week 18 showing where the Eagles rested their starters ahead of the playoffs. There was thought McKee, who had previously flashed in limited preseason and regular season game action, might be able to beat the Washington Commanders in that regular season finale. But he wasn’t. He didn’t play very well, logging a 68.9 passer rating. In fairness, he did look better when DeVonta Smith was in the game early on to help put him over 1,000 receiving yards last season. And then a lot worse once Smith left. And even thought he was going up against a bad and injured Washington team, they still had actual NFL starters playing while the Eagles mostly did not. This less than stellar performance seemingly shook the Eagles’ confidence in McKee because the team decided to trade for Andy Dalton. At first, it was thought Dalton was brought in just to be the Eagles’ third quarterback (even the team back-channeled as much to reporters). But then OTAs began and Dalton was taking the bulk of second-team QB reps. At the time, the Eagles insisted they were rotating QB2 reps between Dalton and McKee. And that’s what we saw take place during training camp and the preseason games. The problem: there was never a clear-cut winner by the time the regular season rolled around. Both players struggled to play well, perhaps in part because they rotated reps instead of being able to enjoy more consistency. Leading into Week 1, the Eagles were still splitting QB2 reps. But then it was made clear that Dalton was Hurts’ backup with the Eagles designating McKee as the emergency third quarterback. Dalton was thrust into action during the Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears. The Eagles shouldn’t have asked him to throw the ball in a goal-to-go situation but they did and his sole pass in the game was picked off by a rookie safety. Makai Lemon reportedly ran the wrong route on the play but it was still a terrible decision by a veteran quarterback turning 39 in late October. Makai Lemon ran the wrong route on Andy Dalton’s Week 3 interception, according to Jeff McLane on his unCovering the Birds podcast: https://t.co/GmU5D9tN5v pic.twitter.com/JzW0TNWeLE — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 5, 2026 Following Week 3, the Eagles decided to switch things up and make McKee QB2 again, as he always should have been. While McKee did not do enough to clear outplay Dalton in the offseason, he did show promise in the past and Dalton mostly stunk it up since joining the Eagles. Nor was he any good for the Carolina Panthers in 2025. It’s not easy to imagine McKee will thrive this Sunday. The Eagles’ offense wasn’t looking great prior to injury issues but those problems have certainly not helped spark a turnaround. It’s looking like McKee could be without DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley. He’s also going to be playing behind an offensive line that looks something like this: LT Jordan Mailata LG Willie Lampkin? Landon Dickerson? C Jake Majors? RG Tyler Steen RT Markel Bell It’ll be interesting to see if there are any notable stylistic differences between Sean Mannion calling the game for Hurts versus McKee. But, again, I’m not expecting the results to suddenly be pretty. Though, if you’re looking for reason for optimism, the Panthers’ defense might be fairly gettable. They’re banged up at cornerback with starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson both on injured reserve. Cole Payton could eventually warrant some playing time. Honestly, there’s a strong case to be made the Eagles should just be starting Payton now. They probably won’t do that. Although it’s not like McKee has a ton of experience (just two career starts), he is the more proven option than a Day 3 rookie from the 2026 NFL Draft. But McKee is also going to be a free agent after this season. Maybe the Eagles feel like they can showcase him a little bit before trading him ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Or maybe they feel like McKee can factor into their compensatory pick formula by signing with a new team in 2027 NFL free agency. But maybe McKee just isn’t that good and there really isn’t much to be learned by playing a subpar quarterback on the final year of his contract. By contrast, Payton could be a long-term factor for this team, whether that’s as a backup or a starter (more likely the former than the latter). Payton offered some intrigue in offseason practices and limited preseason action. He has a penchant for being overly aggressive, so, there might be a lot of turnovers and growing pains. But there’s some level of admiration to be had for how fearless he is. Plus, he can at least run around a bit. If the Eagles are going to concede that 2026 just isn’t their season, they should play Payton. At the very least, they should have Payton be their backup behind McKee. Reporting suggest the Eagles might bring Andy Dalton back. There’s really no good reason to do that. The case would be that he gives the Eagles a better chance to win now than Payton does. The problem is that’s not even necessarily true. And there’s just nothing to be learned from Dalton playing if the season is truly lost. I imagine the Eagles and a lot of fans aren’t willing to throw in the towel just yet. But, for the betterment of the team moving forward, it’s most helpful for them to be honest about their 2026 outlook and focus on the future. Which brings us to our next point … The Eagles should shift their focus beyond the 2026 season. BGN alumnus Jimmy Kempski recently made what I find to be a very compelling case for the Eagles to punt on the 2026 season . To be clear, no one is reasonably suggesting that the Eagles should ACTIVELY try to lose games. This isn’t about tanking. It’s about not making decisions that only focus on maximizing wins in 2026. It’s about taking a long-term view and being willing to sell players ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline if there are strong offers to be accepted. It’s also about finding playing time for players who could be long-term contributors … as opposed to any overreliance on stop-gap veterans who won’t be here after this season. The Eagles being bad this year doesn’t have to be a bad thing for them in 2027, especially if they play their cards right in this stretch. Yes, the Eagles are only a couple plays away from being 4-1. But they just haven’t played well this season: It's not technically false that the #Eagles are "two plays away from being 4-1" but they would have been one of the worst 4-1 teams ever. Through 5 weeks they are 30th in net EPA/drive (ahead of only Arizona and Miami) and rather fortunate to be 2-3. pic.twitter.com/lRA0k8aMeH — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 15, 2026 The NFC East might be bad enough for the Eagles to win a lousy division, even with Hurts missing time. But merely making the playoffs shouldn’t the goal for this team. They should (and normally do) strive for legitimate championship contention. I’m sorry but they’re just not winning the Super Bowl this year.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Jalen Hurts will miss Eagles-Panthers game due to “superficial blood clot”
summary: Here’s a pretty massive and unexpected Philadelphia Eagles development: Jalen Hurts has been ruled OUT of the team’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers due to a “superficial blood clot.” The following statement by the Eagles comes via NFL insider Ian Rapoport: On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - FEBRUARY 09: (L-R) Tanner McKee and Jalen Hurts practice during the Super Bowl LIX Pregame at Caesars Superdome on February 09, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Roc Nation) | Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Roc Here’s a pretty massive and unexpected Philadelphia Eagles development: Jalen Hurts has been ruled OUT of the team’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers due to a “superficial blood clot.” The following statement by the Eagles comes via NFL insider Ian Rapoport : On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report. Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team’s flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia. Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter. On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority. Well, this is pretty wild. Some thoughts that immediately jump to mind: We all hope Hurts is OK. It’s currently unclear how long Hurts will be out. Seems like it’ll be more than a one-game absence. But we’ll see. Tanner McKee is now in line to start at quarterback this weekend. Cole Payton figures to be his backup, unless the Eagles re-sign Andy Dalton. This is probably not the development the Eagles needed to try to turn their season around after 2-3 start! The line for this game has predictably shifted again. After originally opening as 1.5-point home favorites, the Eagles are now 3.5-point home underdogs. Hurts is just one of many key players likely to be absent on Sunday . McKee seemingly won’t have the likes of Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith to work with as he also plays behind a patch-work offensive line. 2026 has had a “season from hell” feel and this Hurts development is only the latest contribution to that sentiment.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Eagles sign running back to practice squad
summary: About one hour after the Philadelphia Eagles announced Jalen Hurts is going to miss Sunday’s game due to a blood clot, the team made a transaction that has nothing to do with their quarterback situation. The Eagles signed free agent running back Ian Wheeler to their practice squad. Wheeler, who turned 25 in September, played […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Ian Wheeler #27 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball to the one-yard line during the fourth quarter of a preseason game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images About one hour after the Philadelphia Eagles announced Jalen Hurts is going to miss Sunday’s game due to a blood clot , the team made a transaction that has nothing to do with their quarterback situation. The Eagles signed free agent running back Ian Wheeler to their practice squad. Wheeler, who turned 25 in September, played college football at Howard before going unpicked in the 2024 NFL Draft. He had stints with the Chicago Bears, New Orleans Saints, Louisville Kings (UFL), and most recently the Buffalo Bills, who cut him in late August. Wheeler earned his shot with the Bills through his United Football League success : Wheeler played an important role for the 2026 UFL Champion Louisville Kings, being named the 2026 UFL United Bowl MVP after helping his team to a 27-20 victory over the DC Defenders. In nine regular season games, Wheeler finished fourth in the UFL in rushing yards with 370 on 68 carries, and second in rushing touchdowns with 6. He also added 13 kick returns for 370 yards and a 28.5 yards per return average. His 776 all purpose yards were good for fifth in the league. The Eagles are currently expected to be missing their top three running backs in Week 6. Saquon Barkley is still dealing with a hamstring injury, Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve, and Will Shipley is expected to miss multiple games due to a foot issue. The Eagles currently have Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as their only backfield options on the roster. Wheeler joins former Dallas Cowboys draft pick Jaydon Blue as more running back depth on the practice squad. (Note: The Eagles brought in Ja’Quinden Jackson for a free agent visit earlier this week and were reportedly set to sign him but the team never announced that move. Perhaps something changed and they decided to go with Wheeler instead.) title: Eagles News: Jalen Hurts is running less than ever
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! We can’t praise Jalen Hurts for his impact on the run game when it’s been good in the past (which he absolutely deserves credit for!) and then also say it doesn’t matter if he’s not running now. It absolutely does matter. […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 11: Jalen Hurts of Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! We can’t praise Jalen Hurts for his impact on the run game when it’s been good in the past (which he absolutely deserves credit for!) and then also say it doesn’t matter if he’s not running now. It absolutely does matter. One would imagine his calf injury isn’t helping matters at the moment. But, dating back to last year, there’s been plenty of reporting about how Hurts doesn’t want to run as much as he did in the past and the Eagles seem to be on board with that approach. There’s certainly a balance to be had because it’s not good if Hurts recklessly runs around too much. But we’ve reached a point where it’s not enough, especially at a time where the offense is in desperate search of answers to get going. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Why doesn’t Jalen Hurts run anymore? – NBCSP After twice averaging over 50 rushing yards per game early in his career, he’s at a career-low 21.4 yards per game this year, which ranks 9th among quarterbacks. After running for 49 yards in the opener vs. Washington, he’s averaged just 15 yards per game since Week 2. His 61 rushing yards the last four weeks is 2rd-fewest in a four game stretch since he became a full-time starter in 2021. It’s his fewest – by 75 yards – through five games of a season. His two rushing yards Sunday were 2nd-fewest of his 89 career starts. He had minus-10 rushing yards in the win over the Vikings last year at U.S. Bank Stadium. He had two five-yard losses, one of them a kneeldown, in the final 47 seconds of that game. Hurts is still effective when he does run. His 4.7 average is his highest since 2021, and his two runs of 20 yards or more match his total from all of last year. He just does it less than ever. Why? I asked him that on Wednesday. Jalen Hurts won’t say much about “very unique” calf injury that was disclosed last Friday – PFT When the question came up during his midweek press conference, here’s what Hurts said: “It was a very unique experience, to say the least. I don’t want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game.” There’s a lot there, in not that many words. What would be “very unique” about a calf injury that didn’t impact his practice reps? And why would it be a big secret? The complicating factor is that the Eagles flew to London on Friday. Did he require medical care in London? Would it be something that the team doctors were able to provide? Did he have to visit a local hospital for it? Nick Sirianni’s Eagles career is at a crossroads – BGN And make no mistake, Sirianni will attempt on Sunday to do something no NFL team has ever successfully done — win a game in which a team is coming off an international game and has to play a team coming off a bye week. It’s only happened four times before, and teams in the Birds’ position are 0-4. This was the Eagles’ choice, by the way. They could have scheduled their bye week coming back from London, but chose to push it later in the season. Nevertheless, it would be a remarkable thing if Sirianni has this team up and running at full capacity on Sunday afternoon against a team coming off a two-week break. It’s fair to wonder if Sirianni lost the locker room last Sunday, even if his decision to allow a return was defensible. He has taken full responsibility for last week’s debacle, a noble act. And while that is certainly appreciated by his players, and while his players all want to do well for him, how will they respond to that? Do they see their boss taking ownership of a questionable decision and continue to rally behind him? Or do they see him as a good guy that lacks answers on how to fix a lackluster offense and has had an uneven track record of making in-game decisions? Panthers vs Eagles: Matchups to watch – Cat Scratch Reader Robert Hunt vs Jalen Carter. The Eagles defense has been keeping them in games while their offense stumbles around. Jalen Carter is a big part of that. He leads the team with three sacks in five games, which is a very high number for an interior lineman. He’s coming off a dominant performance against the Jaguars in which he was credited with two of those sacks and 1.5 run stuffs. All of the Panthers interior linemen will be responsible for keeping Carter in check, but it’s likely going to be Robert Hunt that handles the bulk of that assignment. Hunt has been a little shaky this season. He’ll need to regain his form from past seasons to limit Carter. Analyzing trade values of potential Eagles sell candidates – PhillyVoice RB Saquon Barkley (29). Why should the Eagles trade him? Trading Barkley would be a tough pill to swallow because of his contributions to the 2024 Super Bowl team, but he turns 30 in February and he has an expensive contract. (Caveat: The team kind of has to be inarguably “done-done” to trade Barkley.) Why should other teams trade for him? Barkley still has juice, and there are a bunch of teams that he could help make dangerous. Trade value: Second-round pick. Logical trade partners: Broncos, Texans, Seahawks, Vikings, Packers. Game Review – JAX 19, PHI 17 – Iggles Blitz Willie Lampkin made his first career start and got most of the attention. He struggled early on before settling in. He gave up the most pressures of any of the linemen. I think his biggest issue was getting his hands on defenders too slowly at times. He will need to be more aggressive moving forward. He did have some good blocks and showed some promise. His lack of size was an issue at times. I hope we get to see a few more starts so we can get a better feel for what his ceiling is. 15 NFL players, coaches on the hot seat entering Week 6: Quinn, McDaniel, others – ESPN And as I wrote about last year, Sirianni’s lack of clear ownership over any one particular piece of the operation makes him more likely to receive blame for what goes wrong than credit for what goes right. Sirianni’s résumé through five-plus years as Eagles head coach is as good as anybody’s in NFL history, but for various reasons, there’s a clear perception that Sirianni isn’t the one driving much of that success. And while Sirianni has racked up a gaudy win-loss record during his time in Philadelphia, the Eagles are 5-7 over their past 12 games, including a three-game losing streak. Three of their next four games are at home against the Panthers, Cowboys and Giants, all games we would expect Sirianni’s team to win. If the Eagles win games, even in ugly fashion, fans will tolerate the struggles. But if the losing streak continues, well, the sudden end to Doug Pederson’s tenure with the team in 2020 should tell you just how quickly an otherwise successful run can come to a sudden close in Philadelphia. NFL QB rankings, Week 6: Josh Allen reclaims No. 1 spot; Jordan Love makes biggest jump – NFL.com 26) Jalen Hurts gave his best effort, hit a big touchdown pass to Darius Cooper and moved the Eagles into a winning position before it all fell apart. It’s tough to pin too much of the Eagles’ struggles on Hurts right now. He’s playing behind a makeshift offensive line, doesn’t have his top running back or receiver, and is being asked to make the best of it. Struggling Eagles first-round pick reacts to reduced role: ‘Ain’t a weird situation at all’ – NJ.com “Nah, it ain’t a weird situation at all,” Campbell said on Wednesday about having to split time with Trotter Jr. “It’s a great bond. Like whatever people think or whatever the case may be, it’s not that at the end of the day. … Football is about competition. So I think in our room, we all understand our goals…

title: Vic Fangio talks “dangerous” Panthers offense
summary: The Eagles defense has started to find their footing, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio spoke to reporters this week about how challenging Sunday’s game will be against the Carolina Panthers. He also talked about how injuries are affecting various areas, and why Jordan Davis hasn’t played as much the past two weeks. Here’s what the […]
full_text: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles defense has started to find their footing, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio spoke to reporters this week about how challenging Sunday’s game will be against the Carolina Panthers. He also talked about how injuries are affecting various areas, and why Jordan Davis hasn’t played as much the past two weeks. Here’s what the DC had to say: On the LB plan Fangio confirmed that they were going to play Jeremiah Trotter Jr. more in London, before he got ejected, and that the plan was to rotate him with Jihaad Campbell. The DC did, however, shoot down the notion that Trotter was going to be the starter. “Well, Trot played good in the start that he had when Zach [Baun] was out and it was close. I just think he deserves playing time.” He explained that moving forward the rotation will be by series more than situational. Fangio also said not to draw any comparisons to similar situations the past couple years. He also said that he doesn’t think playing Trotter more would affect Campbell’s development. The DC didn’t exactly have a rave review of Campbell after Sunday’s game, saying only that he, “Played okay.” On the edge rush group “I think it’ll be pretty miraculous for Jalyx [Hunt] to play this week, but he’s the kind of guy, he’s going to be pushing the envelope and making the medical people clear him. He’s not going to be one of those guys that’s going to be hesitant to come back.” Fangio also noted that hopefully Jonathan Greenard will be ready to go this week, but stopped short of confirming his availability. On Kenny Moore at safety “I think when you consider the lack of background, both [Kenny Moore]’s never played safety in his career, gets here after training camp, limited reps with our defense, he’s getting some in scout team. I thought he did a pretty damn good job considering the circumstances.” On Jalen Carter Fangio said that Carter’s case may have been smaller last week, and should be much smaller this week — later on, he explained that medically, he needed the cast on for four weeks. He also talked about what the DT can do to be more consistently dominant. “I just think as he progresses as a player, understands what’s important from a technique standpoint and how to play, we’ll get more of that. But it’s not like he’s been not playing good since he’s been here. It’s just he obviously made a couple big plays the other night and hopefully that will continue and it’s hopefully his wrist [is] getting better.” He also acknowledged that Carter may have been getting double teamed a lot in the second half against the Jaguars. On Jordan Davis’ workload Davis played a little more this week than he had the week prior, but Fangio revealed that the Eagles defense was in nickel a lot more than base, which affected that number, too. “Well, one of the things that happens is it became a pretty big nickel game, not much base, which only two of those guys play. So it kind of becomes three for two with him, [Moro] Ojomo and Jalen [Carter]. So those three, and then when you add the other two guys, it’s going to spread it out some.” On preparing for the Panthers Fangio talked about how QB Bryce Young has really progressed the past few years, and gave kudos to him and the coaches to get him there. He noted that Young is a really good processor, makes quick decisions, and knows where to go with the ball. “[Bryce Young]’s elusive, he’s a scrambler, really good anticipation. Very, very impressed by him.” The DC also admitted that the offense is dangerous with players likeWR Tetairoa McMillan and WR Jalen Coker, pointing out that the Panthers are third in the league in yards. “They’re dangerous. I think they’re third in the league in yards. It’s only a five game season up to this point, but fifth in points, something like that, or fourth in first downs. They’re balanced. They run it good. [Chuba] Hubbard’s really a good back, runs hard. They block good. They’re a good offense, and it’s not tilted one way or the other. It’s [not] all pass. They’re really good running and throwing and the run game and the pass game compliment each other in the early downs. They got it going right now.” He said that during their first day of preparing for the Panthers, they talked about how their kicker has made a 70-yarder before, and how they’ll have to plan accordingly. Other notables Fangio confirmed that head coach Nick Sirianni stresses situational awareness, and said he knows that the head coach spends a lot of time research it every week and is something he takes a lot of pride in. He admitted that having LB Zack Baun out on the field makes a big difference, and Baun has been a really good player for the Eagles since he got to Philly. He noted that Baun is one of the top linebackers in the league, and when he’s out on the field, they expect him to step up in big moments. The DC also acknowledged that the depth at safety is “challenged” with Marcus Epps being out with an injury and then losing his replacement Michael Carter the next game.

title: Nick Sirianni’s Eagles career is at a crossroads
summary: As the days have passed following last Sunday’s nightmare-fueled loss to Jacksonville in London, and all angles of Nick Sirianni’s last minute decision to allow the Jaguars an opportunity to return the final kickoff have been dissected to within an inch of its life (including by me), I think it’s fair to say this week’s […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Chief Security Officer Dom "Big Dom" DiSandro of the Philadelphia Eagles smiles with head Coach Nick Sirianni prior to an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the days have passed following last Sunday’s nightmare-fueled loss to Jacksonville in London, and all angles of Nick Sirianni’s last minute decision to allow the Jaguars an opportunity to return the final kickoff have been dissected to within an inch of its life ( including by me ), I think it’s fair to say this week’s home game against the Carolina Panthers is a crossroads for the embattled head coach. Upon further reflection, I can agree that his kickoff decision last week can be argued both ways. There were sound reasons to kick it through the end zone (still is the right call in my opinion) and to allow a return. There are other aspects of those final moments that deserve scrutiny, specifically whether Jalen Hurts, Makai Lemon, and Sean Mannion executed those final seconds correctly. But in the end, it was virtually impossible for the Jaguars to win a game with eight seconds left, no timeouts and about to receive a kickoff. In 999 times out of 1000, the Eagles win with no issues and none of those decisions are discussed. Ever. Perhaps the greater point of emphasis on the job Sirianni did last Sunday should be on the team’s overall performance. Coming off back-to-back losses and fielding a wildly undermanned roster, Sirianni had his team up for that game in London. They flew across the ocean, knowing they had less talent on the field than their opponent, and should have won a game in which they were massive underdogs. That Sirianni was able to coax that kind of effort out of a pedestrian roster last Sunday is a testament to his ability to get his players to play hard for him. That’s why Sunday’s game against Carolina is such an important one for him, and the organization. We’ve seen the head coaching life cycle under Jeffrey Lurie. When things start to go bad, the front office doesn’t let situations linger. They make quick decisions. Andy Reid was dismissed after a 4-12 season in 2012 that was preceded by an 8-8 season the year before. Doug Pederson was let go after just one losing season, a 4-11-1 campaign during the COVID year of 2020. When Lurie and Howie Roseman feel a coach’s life cycle has come and gone, they act quickly. The 2012 and ‘20 seasons spun wildly out of control on both coaches to the point a change became inevitable. A win on Sunday stops the bleeding and at least signals this year may not spiral out of control. It’s similar to Week 6 of the 2024 Super Bowl season. Coming off a ‘23 campaign in which the team fell apart and collapsed in spectacular fashion, the Eagles started 2-2 and coming off a humiliating loss to the Bucs in Tampa. There was a very real feeling that if Sirianni didn’t take care of business coming out of that bye week, he might be fired in-season. It wasn’t pretty, but with a new run-first, no-turnover offensive philosophy and a defense that was finding its legs, the Eagles edged the Browns 20-16 in an ugly home win. But, it was a victory that launched a 10-game winning streak. They would lose just one more time the entire season before winning it all. That won’t happen this time. There won’t be any 10-game winning streaks, and the likelihood of this team winning a Super Bowl at this moment is exceedingly remote. No one is expecting that right now, but a loss and, more to the point, a lackluster effort at the Linc, could spell doom for the future of Sirianni as head coach of the Eagles. There is no chance anyone is fired in the middle of the season, but how this team plays down the stretch will determine whether Sirianni has a long-term future in Philadelphia. And make no mistake, Sirianni will attempt on Sunday to do something no NFL team has ever successfully done — win a game in which a team is coming off an international game and has to play a team coming off a bye week. It’s only happened four times before, and teams in the Birds’ position are 0-4. This was the Eagles’ choice, by the way. They could have scheduled their bye week coming back from London, but chose to push it later in the season. Nevertheless, it would be a remarkable thing if Sirianni has this team up and running at full capacity on Sunday afternoon against a team coming off a two-week break. It’s fair to wonder if Sirianni lost the locker room last Sunday, even if his decision to allow a return was defensible. He has taken full responsibility for last week’s debacle, a noble act. And while that is certainly appreciated by his players, and while his players all want to do well for him, how will they respond to that? Do they see their boss taking ownership of a questionable decision and continue to rally behind him? Or do they see him as a good guy that lacks answers on how to fix a lackluster offense and has had an uneven track record of making in-game decisions? In short, do the players trust him? If they do, you will see an Eagles team come out of the locker room on Sunday ready, once again, to play hard. Despite being the home team, it is essentially a pick ‘em game, meaning most oddsmakers believe Carolina is the better team. But it was clear last week that Jacksonville was the better team by a significant margin, and the Birds almost shocked the world by stealing a game in which they were touchdown-underdogs. Sirianni and the Eagles are paying the price for winning a Super Bowl two seasons ago. Two of their offensive linemen essentially broke themselves doing it, and they’ve never recovered. Their veteran offensive coordinator left to take another job, and they’ve struggled to replace him ever since. Their star wide receiver revealed team goals weren’t as important to him following the Super Bowl and played his way out of town in pursuit of singular glory. And the litany of injuries they’ve suffered, along with the sudden retirement of Lane Johnson, has almost forced the ushering of a new era upon the franchise before they were ready for it. About the only thing that hasn’t happened is an injury to their star quarterback, which I hope I haven’t now spoken into existence. And let’s not pretend there isn’t uncertainty over whether Jalen Hurts can truly ever be successful in an offense that asks him to play a style of football he never has before and has never appeared comfortable playing. It’s almost impossible to quickly return to a Super Bowl without a ton of luck on your side, and the Eagles have had none of it this year. That’s OK. That happens. This has been an unbelievable run, and Sirianni has had remarkable injury luck over his first five seasons. But that bill is coming due now. The Eagles may finish with a record under .500. Coaches can survive that as long as progress can be seen on the field and the product is not embarrassing. Good coaches help less talented teams play over their heads and improve as the season moves along. There are not a ton of healthy Pro Bowlers left on the roster, so every player on the team needs to be coached up even more now. It is imperative this coaching staff, specifically on the offensive side of the ball, gives this team an edge. The Eagles must play smarter football than the guys lined up against them. They cannot rely on their talent to paper over execution problems and mistakes. They cannot be a heavily-penalized team. They cannot make bad decisions. Virtually every in-game decision has to have the correct process, even if the results don’t go their way. If they play smart, competent football, Sirianni should keep his job, no matter the record. He’s a CEO head coach, and must be the very best version of that for this project to work. This Sunday begins an opportunity to show he can get the most out of his talent and defy the critics who believe his…
author: John Stolnis

Who are you rooting for? What are you watching for? Who do you have in fantasy football? Join the comment section and enjoy […]

Also on the Steelers’ injury report, cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton (ankle) improved from non-participants on Wednesday to limited participants on Thursday. Watt and Cam Heyward, who had rest designations on Wednesday, were both full participants Thursday as expected. title: DK Metcalf is quietly making plays for the Steelers
summary: It’s been a rough go of things for Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf. In five games, he has just 19 receptions for 225 yards, putting him on pace for 65 catches, 762 yards, and three touchdowns. And while those numbers are far from horrible, they certainly shouldn’t reflect that of a wide receiver making […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a rough go of things for Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf. In five games, he has just 19 receptions for 225 yards, putting him on pace for 65 catches, 762 yards, and three touchdowns. And while those numbers are far from horrible, they certainly shouldn’t reflect that of a wide receiver making $33 million per year. Metcalf has received a lot of well-placed criticism for his production, or lack thereof, in relation to his pay. However, in Pittsburgh’s last two wins, he’s made plays that haven’t shown up on the stat sheet that prove he’s willing to do the dirty work. On Jaylen Warren’s 80-yard touchdown catch and run, Metcalf threw two key blocks that sprung Warren down the sideline. DK Metcalf sprung the 80 yard Jaylen Warren TD with a pair of key blocks. Very T.O. Garrison Hearst esc pic.twitter.com/2WxJFDKHdf — Jarrett Bailey (@JBaileyNFL) October 15, 2026 This isn’t a one-off from Metcalf, either. On the first play from scrimmage for Pittsburgh’s offense against the Bengals in Week 3, Aaron Rodgers hit Warren out of the backfield. Metcalf immediately found a body to get his hands on, and he turned what would have been an eight-yard gain to a 30-yard gain. Metcalf has had a willingness to block. First play against the Bengals, immediately turns and finds a body to lock up with and leads Warren to get another chunk of yards. pic.twitter.com/bU04lWftJ0 — Jarrett Bailey (@JBaileyNFL) October 15, 2026 And even when balls aren’t thrown Metcalf’s way, he is drawing double coverage from opposing defenses, which is opening up opportunities for others to make plays. For instance, the Bengals shade a safety over the top of Metcalf, which opened up things across the middle for Roman Wilson to pick up 18 yards. And even when the ball doesn’t go to DK, he’s drawing the attention of multiple DBs. The Bengals shade the safety overtop of him here, and the middle is open for Roman Wilson to find a hole and pick up 18. pic.twitter.com/qKvX9oz6UH — Jarrett Bailey (@JBaileyNFL) October 15, 2026 We all want to see Metcalf have bigger performances in the box score and have larger impacts on wins with big catches. But the silver lining in his sub-par stats is that he’s making a difference by blocking hard, taking up attention from defenses, and doing gritty work that many stars shy away from. And as those other opportunities for others like Wilson and Germie Bernard open up, defenses will have to take away their extensive coverage on Metcalf if Pittsburgh’s other play-makers carve them up. This is a deeper group of weapons for Pittsburgh than it was a season ago. As the season progresses, Metcalf will naturally see more balls come his way. It then becomes up to him to make the most of those chances. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Which young Steelers are worth building around?
summary: The Steelers are a team straddling two timelines this season. In one lane, they are a team tied for the oldest average age of players (27.1) in the NFL. In the other lane, they are a roster that features 29 players aged 26 years old or younger. That total includes a handful of players currently […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers are a team straddling two timelines this season. In one lane, they are a team tied for the oldest average age of players (27.1) in the NFL. In the other lane, they are a roster that features 29 players aged 26 years old or younger. That total includes a handful of players currently on injured lists, but not the practice squad, save for running back Lew Nichols, who was on the active roster this past week. Considering that rosters have just 53 spots, and only 48 can be active on game day, that’s a lot of youth for a team whose average age is spiked by featuring players like Aaron Rodgers (42), Cam Heyward (37), Chris Boswell (35), and Cameron Johnston (34), not to mention guys like T.J. Watt (32) and Jalen Ramsey (31). Heading into the season, both members of Read & React predicted the Steelers would be the AFC’s seventh seed, with the expectation of a similar win total to what they accomplished in 2025. Pittsburgh is currently 3-2 and would miss the playoffs as the ninth seed if the season were to end today. While it thankfully does not, the chances of this team putting fans through a rollercoaster of a year remains fairly high. Following last week’s victory over the Colts, Steelers fans are currently riding one of the upswings in that metaphorical coaster. As such, Read & React thought this would be a good time to take a longer view and take stock of the Steelers’ young players. We will be sorting the players 26 and under on the roster into tiers: Franchise cornerstones — these are the players we believe are most important to this franchise. While we mostly believe these players are those who’ve already proven they are good to some degree, we aren’t fitting them for gold jackets and the Ring of Honor just yet either. Most of them still have plenty to prove, and we acknowledge that career trajectories for young players can take sudden and unexpected turns. That said, if the Steelers want to get back to championship contention, this group of players will need to be instrumental and team leaders in that effort. Quality starters and role players — Not every player can be a franchise cornerstone. But while great teams have a fair share of superstars, they also tend to have a quality collection of guys willing to do the dirty work and take less of the credit while serving the great goal of the team. These players are ones who might not ever be superstars, but are players we think can contribute to the next chapter of the Steelers in a positive way. Need to see more (but trending positive) — Players in this tier have only seen limited playing time, but have left a decent enough impression to have reason to hope they can develop into contributors. Need to see more (or hasn’t played) — Pretty self-explanatory. These players haven’t played, and thus make it hard to give a real assessment. Never say never, but… — Anything is possible, and we don’t want to write anyone off. But these are players where it’s reasonable to question their impact or spot on the roster beyond 2026. Now you may be asking, “Why 26?” The answer is relatively straightforward. Players are often considered to be entering their athletic primes between the ages of 27-29. That’s roughly the age group where they’ve spent their rookie contract in the league and have earned a second contract. There are several 26-year-olds on Pittsburgh’s roster who are still working towards a second contract, while a handful of younger players were handed extensions this summer, for example. We’ll break it all down for you. Franchise cornerstones Zach Frazier, C RB: While this list is a very loose “ranking,” Frazier was an obvious No. 1 choice. He’s established himself as one of the league’s top centers with outstanding strength, toughness and recovery/anchor. He’ll be an expensive name to keep around as contract negotiations loom in 2027, but that’s a good problem to have as Frazier has developed into the quite literal centerpiece of the Steelers’ offensive line rebuild in recent seasons. He’s undoubtedly a long-term starter, and his mobility remains an underrated aspect of his game. Zach Frazier is very good pic.twitter.com/dvD9L8V6os — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 7, 2026 Max Iheanachor, OT RP : His career is still very young, but even at just 22 years old, there’s an argument that could be made that Iheanachor is already the most talented of Pittsburgh’s starting tackles. That’s no knock against another Steeler who will soon be joining this list; that just speaks to the potential the rookie out of Arizona State is already beginning to realize. Sure, the Cleveland game had a few warts, but overall Iheanachor has been a shot in the arm for an offensive line that was struggling mightily the first two weeks without him in the lineup. He allowed zero pressures last week against the Colts, and he’s shown he can be an asset in the running game. It’s no coincidence that the Steelers running game took off once he was inserted into the lineup. If the Steelers are going to return to the upper echelon of the AFC, Iheanachor’s continued development will play a huge part in that. Max Iheanachor pic.twitter.com/sn4LhHQ40S — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) October 15, 2026 Troy Fautanu, OT RB: A college left tackle turned right tackle turned left tackle again, Fautanu’s NFL career hasn’t been without its rough points after injury prevented him from playing most of his rookie season. But aside from still-occasional lapses in technique and when dealing with power rushes, Fautanu has overwhelmingly looked the part of an ascending long-term starter. He has a powerful punch, a mobile base in pass protection and plays with more violence than he’s typically given credit for. #Steelers T Troy Fautanu vs. Browns EDGE Jared Verse: 18 pass-rushing matchups 1 pressure allowed Another generally impressive outing for Fautanu. Handled the power and quickness of Verse very well, leveraging quick + active hands and shrewd parries pic.twitter.com/cKTBzVoDY2 — Bradley Locker (@Bradley_Locker) October 2, 2026 Nick Herbig, OLB RB: The Steelers’ increased usage of Herbig as an inside linebacker this season has diminished his once-elite efficiency as a pass rusher, but I’m not too worried about his long-term fit in the Pittsburgh defense. Only 108 of Herbig’s 158 snaps this season have come at an edge alignment per NFL Pro, and his quarterback pressure rate has dropped below double digits for the first time of his career at 6.3% so far this season, with no sacks through five games. Still, his signature quickness hasn’t diminished — defensive coordinator Patrick Graham just needs to find better ways to use Herbig’s skill set, which should come down the road when he’s not the team’s No. 3 outside linebacker anymore. It’s also worth noting that Herbig has a bit more power and run-stopping ability than his speed-rushing profile might indicate. Watch Nick Herbig long-arm eject this extra OL into the path of the puller to blow up the play. pic.twitter.com/GyZnzwazVv — Derrick (@Steelers_DB) October 12, 2026 Darnell Washington, TE RP : The Steelers have already handed Washington a second contract, and it’s not hard to see why. There just isn’t another playmaker in the NFL who combines his size, fluid movement, contact balance, and desire to put opponents in the dirt quite like Washington. Widely regarded as one of the best blocking tight ends in the league, that alone would be enough to cement Mount Washington as a franchise cornerstone. But add on his increasingly growing involvement as a pass catcher and his ability to turn plays into explosive gains simply by refusing to be tackled, and the Steelers have found themselves one of the NFL’s true unicorns. Darnell Washington blocked one guy, then blocked a second guy, then blocked a third guy WITH the second guy. pic.twitter.com/4Ely7yQYhT — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) October 11, 2026 Quality starters and role players Mason…

title: Four wide receiver trades the Steelers should make
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers enter Week 6 without three of their wide receivers. Michael Pittman is on IR with a foot injury, and both Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek suffered injuries in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts that will leave them unable to play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That leaves DK Metcalf, […]
full_text: (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers enter Week 6 without three of their wide receivers. Michael Pittman is on IR with a foot injury, and both Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek suffered injuries in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts that will leave them unable to play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That leaves DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard, and Kaden Wetjen as the only receivers who made the initial 53-man roster that are healthy. Brandon Smith was called up on Sunday, and may get a roster spot in Week 6. Should the Steelers want to make a splash, though, and add a proven playmaker, there are multiple names to look at via trade. Vikings WR Jauan Jennings Jennings signed with the Vikings this past offseason after five seasons with the San Francisco 49ers. He put up solid numbers over his last two seasons, with 55 receptions in 2025 and 77 catches in 2024. Thus far with Minnesota, he has just two receptions for nine yards. Considering his proven ability to do the underneath nitty-gritty stuff, including hard run blocking and catching passes through contract, he fits what Pittsburgh wants to do offensively. A 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for his services would be a good move for Pittsburgh to make. Titans WR Calvin Ridley Ridley is in his ninth NFL season, and his current role with the Tennessee Titans is a small one. He has only caught five passes on eight targets thus far in 2026. Ridley isn’t far removed from a pair of 1,000-yard seasons in 2023 and 2024, and perhaps playing in a better offense with a quarterback like Aaron Rodgers would bring out a bit of the player we saw a few seasons ago. He’ll be 32 before the season ends. With that in mind, A 2028 sixth-round pick would be fair compensation for the former Second-Team All-Pro. Browns WR Jerry Jeudy Do I think the Browns will trade Jeudy to the Steelers while both are very much alive in a playoff race? No. But if we only wrote about things we think will happen, not a lot of work would get done. It’s far from unprecedented to see players dealt within the division. The Browns traded quarterback Joe Flacco to the Bengals last season, and Mike Tomlin was infamously really, really fine with it. Jeudy caught 50 passes a season ago, but only has eight catches on 15 targets in 2026. Shipping a fifth-rounder to Cleveland for the 27 year-old wouldn’t be the worst idea. Jaguars WR Brian Thomas We saw Marvin Harrison Jr get dealt to the Houston Texans in a splash move, which leaves Thomas as the biggest name being centered around trade rumors at the position. The 2024 Pro Bowler has gotten lost in the pecking order due to Parker Washington emerging as a budding star, as well as Jakobi Meyers and Brenton Strange being the second and third options in the Jaguars’ offense. After nearly 1,300 yards in 2024, injuries saw that number dip to just over 700 in 2025. Through five games, he has nine catches for 105 yards. A third-round pick may be enough to secure a deal for Thomas, who would instantly become the best receiver on the team. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald doesn’t sugarcoat Sam Darnold’s performance vs. Broncos
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are in crisis mode following another error-filled Sam Darnold performance in defeat. Darnold is 1-3 as a starter since returning from his opening day glute injury, and the context of his interceptions are impossible to ignore and consistently game-damaging. His two interceptions in Seattle’s 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos were […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are in crisis mode following another error-filled Sam Darnold performance in defeat. Darnold is 1-3 as a starter since returning from his opening day glute injury, and the context of his interceptions are impossible to ignore and consistently game-damaging. His two interceptions in Seattle’s 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos were disastrous; the first pick was in game-tying field goal range, while the second pick led to Denver’s 8-yard game-winning field goal drive. Darnold has thrown seven interceptions in four games, which would be fine if he was throwing 16 touchdown passes, but alas he’s only thrown seven TDs. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is normally not one to be overtly critical of his players, especially not his starting quarterback. This was one of those rare times where that didn’t happen. “It wasn’t a performance that was good enough to win the game,” Macdonald said, “you know, by our team, but the quarterback leads the team and I bet you Sam will be the first one to tell you that. We love him. It’s just that’s what it is. “We have to take care of the ball. Sam knows that, he told the team that. We’ve got to take care of the ball,” Macdonald also said in the post-game press conference. “Just got greedy,” Darnold said of his second interception. “That play specifically, I should have just gotten it down to [Cooper Kupp]. Coop ran a really good route right under the sticks, and I feel like he would have caught it and got the first down. I’ve just got to continue to go through my progressions and trust it. “It’s B.S. for me to keep turning the ball over,” Darnold also added. “It’s not fair for our defense. It’s not fair for our special teams. It’s not far, really, to our entire team. Indeed, Sam. Indeed. The offense as a whole has been bad, but Darnold’s play has not been good enough and it does start with him. Even winning a Super Bowl isn’t enough to earn this much grace when the mistakes are ruinous.
author: Mookie Alexander

title: Winners and Losers from Seahawks vs. Broncos: Benching Sam Darnold must be considered
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have a great defense and a mediocre football team right now. After an ugly 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos, Seattle sits at 3-3 and are almost certainly going to be only competing for a Wild Card berth. At this rate, missing the playoffs seems distinctly possible if not probable. An […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have a great defense and a mediocre football team right now. After an ugly 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos , Seattle sits at 3-3 and are almost certainly going to be only competing for a Wild Card berth. At this rate, missing the playoffs seems distinctly possible if not probable. An offense this bad can sink a season just as much as a great offense can be undone when a defense is rancid. This is about as clear-cut as a Winners and Losers as you’re going to get, so sit tight. Seattle Seahawks Winners Jaxon Smith-Njigba is playing through pain and playing his ass off Another 12 catches for 134 yards for the NFL’s premier receiver. Without him, Seattle’s offense may be threatening 1992 levels of ineptitude. JSN is not 100 percent and took some huge hits all night, making me wonder if he was going to make it through the game. His toughness is criminally underrated and his strength at the catch point is terrific. Seattle’s defense didn’t deserve that loss Okay, the second quarter was bad. Screen passes and short throws and that Devon Witherspoon DPI resulted in two touchdowns allowed back-to-back. Tell me what more the defense could’ve done. Get a turnover? Didn’t have one but they limited Denver to 168 yards of offense and basically nothing after halftime. I thought Tyrice Knight in particular did a great job filling in for Drake Thomas, while Nick Emmanwori continues to look more like himself after his ankle surgery. There’s very little to complain about outside of (again) the continued lack of consistent pressure from the edge group. The Broncos offense had two good drives out of 11 real attempts to score and it’s unreasonable to expect a defense to play much better than that. If your offense can’t score 15 points minimum to win a game in regulation then that’s on the offense. George Holani redeems himself for a couple of plays Hey, he didn’t fumble and got a career-long 13-yard run which set up an angry run touchdown on the next play. After last week’s disaster at least he did something positive and got Seattle’s only TD of the night. Irv Charles showed more on one kickoff coverage rep Yes, Denver scored a touchdown anyway, but to see Irv immediately wrap up a returner at the 25 was a breath of fresh air after repeatedly seeing kickoffs go beyond the 30. More Irv! This is what you do! Seattle Seahawks Losers Sam Darnold is playing bench-worthy football, there I said it I defended Darnold from the idea of getting benched last week but left the door open a little bit if it persisted. I’ll preface this by saying that Drew Lock not throwing any picks in his two games is not indicative of a QB who is suddenly not turnover prone anymore. Lock has had plenty of games where he’s looked like a very good starter and then the following week looks like a mess. Playing an awful Arizona Cardinals defense (in which Seattle actually had a good running game to lean on) doesn’t tell me much about how he’d do against way better teams. But Drew Lock as a backup seemingly has it ingrained in his head not to be reckless with the ball. Sam Darnold is reverting to every bad habit he’s ever had in college and in the NFL, except there is no great payoff like we’ve seen over the past two seasons. Darnold’s NFC Championship Game performance is the single greatest performance by any Seahawks QB in the playoffs and I’ll say that with confidence… but he’s also vying to be a long-term starter and not a mid-level contract guy. You can’t pay him top-level money so that’s out the window, but can you even start him at this rate? Not everything falls on Sam. This offensive line is not playing well, the running game is mediocre, and Brian Fleury’s pure progression concepts are causing way too many route spacing issues. But Fleury isn’t making Sam not trust his reads, double and triple hitch in the pocket, and toggle from risk averse to greedy at any given moment. I don’t think Seattle will bench Darnold next week unless they make up an injury and put him on IR to heal (four games + bye week). But he’s on as short a leash as any Seahawks QB has been in a long time. Respect what Darnold did to help Seattle win a Super Bowl, but acknowledge that the context of his play and a looming extension makes his future murky. These turnovers are unacceptable. Abe Lucas is struggling, and Josh Jones might have to start playing This isn’t a one-off with Abe, I’m afraid. He’s been struggling badly throughout the season with pass-pro and run blocking, and Thursday night was his worst game of the season. Nik Bonitto spun him like cotton candy for one of the many sacks on Sam Darnold. He is whiffing on screens, blitzes on his side are not being picked up, and he physically looks lesser than his 2025 self. If we’re going to talk about benching players (namely Sam Darnold), I believe changing in Josh Jones at right tackle next week should be in strong consideration. Abe is better than this and right now he’s not anywhere close to his best. The offensive line continues to struggle If the Seahawks aren’t going to max protect under Brian Fleury then this offensive line doesn’t have a chance. They just don’t. I am very disappointed that the OL is this underwhelming against any competent defensive line. Lucas’ struggles have already been documented, but Grey Zabel is having a second-year slump, Jalen Sundell has had his own problems in pass pro and getting bullied, and the right guard rotation continues to be an annoyance. I cannot wait until Anthony Bradford is back, a sentence I’d never thought I would type. Klint Kubiak seemingly hid the weaknesses of this offensive line for the most part. Brian Fleury’s decreased use of max protect calls ( shoutout Hawkblogger for taking Fleury to task on this ) reduces help for the line and it is exposing them as not being as good as we thought they were. Brian Fleury might be a one-and-done coordinator but in a different way I don’t fault Fleury for the running game not being effective with below-average running backs. I fault him when Emanuel Wilson is getting short-side tosses to the weaker side of the line. Know your damn personnel. Seattle’s passing game is disjointed for reasons that are not Darnold exclusive. How many times are receivers running routes to the same area? Why are the route combinations condensing the field and adding defenders into the mix instead of spreading them out? Why is 3rd and 1 WITH TIME ON YOUR SIDE an under-center straight dropback (which was an interception)? Why is it always taking so long to get the play call in? First-time OC, first-time playcaller, it’s an unenviable task to succeed Klint Kubiak. Some of the cracks the offense showed last season are now canyon-sized holes this season, so it’s not like some of these issues are new. That they’ve gotten worse under Fleury is not favorable for him. I’m not in “Fire Fleury” mode but I think there’s been enough dysfunction to suggest he needs to turn it around just as much as anybody. The Rashid Shaheed contract looks like a disaster Shaheed was a good player for the New Orleans Saints and a valuable part of Seattle’s Super Bowl run last year, albeit primarily through special teams. He does not fit this offense and possibly not this quarterback. The 5-catch showing flatters him, and if nothing else I think his two-point conversion catch was his best play all night. But he also lost a fumble and then had a pretty important dropped kickoff to start overtime that, combined with a Tyrice Knight holding penalty, backed Seattle up at its 11. I’ve way over-estimated Seattle’s wide receiver group outside of JSN. The 2026 version of Cooper Kupp is still capable but can’t be your WR2. Tory Horton has not justified a high target share and I think he has some culpability on the first interception.
