title: Seahawks-Broncos score: Sam Darnold has another disaster in overtime loss
summary: The Seattle Seahawks (3-3) officially have a quarterback problem. Sam Darnold threw two more dreadful interceptions, one of which was in field goal range toward the end of regulation, another of which gifted the Denver Broncos (4-2) the game-winning field goal in overtime. Seattle was down 14-3 throughout the second half, finally found some offense […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks (3-3) officially have a quarterback problem. Sam Darnold threw two more dreadful interceptions, one of which was in field goal range toward the end of regulation, another of which gifted the Denver Broncos (4-2) the game-winning field goal in overtime. Seattle was down 14-3 throughout the second half, finally found some offense late, but ultimately lost 17-14 despite the defense putting in a heroic second half and overtime display. Denver’s offense put up 168 yards and won. There’s nothing more to say. I’ve defended Darnold’s struggles, thank him forever for the Super Bowl ring, and his NFC Championship performance is one of the great showings in Seahawks history. But this version of Darnold is Jets Darnold and the Seahawks are not going to be back in the playoffs this year if he keeps playing like this. Something has to change. This was abysmal. It’s not all on Darnold given the shambolic offensive line performance and the mediocre rushing attack and questionable play-calling, but Darnold is killing any semblance of a smooth offense at the moment and directly costing Seattle games. Seahawks-Broncos 1st half recap Seattle started on offense and went heavy on shotgun plays. Sam Darnold completed his first four passes to get into Broncos territory, only for consecutive sacks to completely derail the drive and prompt a punt. Denver was backed up inside its own 10, gained very little on consecutive running plays and then Bo Nix was lucky that his pass to Jaylen Waddle was too inaccurate to either be caught by Waddle or pick-6’d by Julian Love. The Seahawks had a short-ish field and got on the board first with a field goal. They picked up 13 yards on the ground, with Velus Jones Jr getting some run over George Holani. Neither pass by Sam Darnold was completed, and Myers came on for a 55-yarder. 3-0 Seahawks. The Broncos’ first points came on an eight-minute drive that extended into the second quarter. Denver converted on multiple third downs and a 4th-and-3 near midfield. The Seahawks didn’t concede a lot of big plays, but they were dinked and dunked through small runs and screen passes. JK Dobbins waltzed into the end zone to cap off a long touchdown drive. 7-3 Broncos. Direct snap to RJ Harvey and he takes it in for his first TD of the season! SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cuwTIyAeJk — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) October 16, 2026 A big kick return by Rashid Shaheed was wasted by Seattle, which ended up punting the ball back to Denver in swift order. Darnold was nearly picked on a blitz looking for Jaxon Smith-Njigba. That kind of game and that kind of season. Denver went on a 9-play, 79-yard drive that was aided heavily by a pass interference in the end zone by Devon Witherspoon on Courtland Sutton. Automatic first-and-goal at the 1 and a direct snap touchdown to RJ Harvey for another score. 14-3 Broncos. Wildcat TD 🤩 📺: #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/GDO1RDJ9su — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 16, 2026 A kickoff out of bounds gave the Seahawks another short field. Well, what would they do this time? Fumble, of course. Rashid Shaheed took an end-around and as he was upended, the ball was jarred loose by a knee and the Broncos recovered. To make it worse, the effort by Elijah Arroyo to recover the fumble cost him his shoulder and ultimately the rest of the game. Defense making plays 😤 📺: #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/XXiA3RAyYf — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 16, 2026 No other scoring happened heading into the break. Seattle’s offense was thoroughly disjointed. Seahawks-Broncos 2nd half recap Denver’s offense didn’t manage much offense throughout the third quarter, so Seattle’s defense tightened up. The offense wasted opportunities time and time again. Bad sacks by Sam Darnold, a lack of blocking by Abe Lucas, and even when good things happened there were bad things to override the good. Rashid Shaheed caught a 42-yard long ball to finally make a major contribution in the passing game. Darnold was sacked on a third down, setting up a longer but still makeable field goal for Jason Myers… DOINK. I wish I had a more thorough recap but the game was just dull. Plain dull. Few explosive plays, a lot of negative Seahawks plays, just no scoring. Sam Darnold took a dismal fifth sack while in field goal range. Just a messy, messy showing. It’s the fourth quarter and time is ticking away. HANG ON! We have excitement! We have an 11-play, 67-yard drive from the Seahawks that felt like pulling teeth but actually ended in points! Sam Darnold converted a 4th and short to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who took a shot but not the full brunt of it. Darnold scrambled for 18 yards for another critical conversion. George Holani, rebounding from a horrible game last week, had a strong 13-yard rush with the help of his offensive linemen and Eric Saubert. He dragged tacklers to the 1, then muscled his way into the end zone on the next snap. A two-point conversion desperation throw to Rashid Shaheed was tipped in the air and CAUGHT! 14-11 Broncos . George Holani just kept on running! SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Dz0iHQxhDo — NFL (@NFL) October 16, 2026 6️⃣ for 3️⃣6️⃣ 📺: @NFLonPRIME pic.twitter.com/JoSyOCNEqV — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 16, 2026 ONE OF THOSE CATCHES 🤯 @RashidShaheed +2 📺: @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/2krgXf9Hh2 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 16, 2026 The Broncos offense, which was stuck in mud all half, went three-and-out again after Bo Nix took two really bad sacks. Nick Emmanwori devoured him with a sack as a spy on 3rd and long. Punt time! NICK GOT HOME 💪 -10 yards on the sack. 📺: @NFLonPRIME pic.twitter.com/ClL7DlQ0Fm — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 16, 2026 Sam Darnold lofted a beauty to JSN for 30 yards to set the Seahawks up near midfield! On 3rd and 1 inside Denver’s 40… Sam gets picked by Kris Abrams-Draine on a throw intended for Tory Horton. Dear oh dear oh dear. Seattle had all of its timeouts but only took two because Nix threw an incomplete pass on 3rd down. Uchenna Nwosu nearly got a pick and instead had a PBU. Rashid Shaheed had a big punt return to the 45. Cooper Kupp with a drop. Brutal. Darnold gets LEVELED and he’s hurt, but so is a Broncos player on a short throw to AJ Barner. It’s 3rd and 6 and he converts to Shaheed! Spike with under 30 seconds left. Now a throw over the middle to Kupp to the 23! Another spike! Quick throw to JSN to the 16 with 7 ticks. Jason Myers from 34 for the tie… GOOD! 14-14 and we go to overtime! RIGHT DOWN THE MIDDLE. @JayMy_31 +3 🔥 📺: @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/mNlWahYyBz — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 16, 2026 Seahawks vs. Broncos overtime recap The Seahawks started overtime on offense by fumbling the kickoff. Rashid Shaheed dropped it and then only returned it to the 23, and a holding penalty backed Seattle up half the distance to the goal. Two runs with Emanuel Wilson only gained seven yards, setting up a dreaded 3rd and 3. A quick throw to JSN converts for the first. Darnold has a second down pass batted down, then a third down pass picked off by Ja’Quan McMillian. Denver already on the cusp of field goal range. J-Mac coming up clutch 💪 📺: #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/iu9Hck8qGA — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 16, 2026 Two runs gained 8 yards, setting up 3rd and short for Denver. Bo Nix stifled by Tyrice Knight, but it’s still a makeable 52-yard field goal for Wil Lutz. He got it. 17-14 Broncos OT. Seahawks-Broncos full box score Seahawks injury report TE Elijah Arroyo left the game in the second quarter with a shoulder injury and did not return. Next week’s opponent The Seahawks return home for a daunting Sunday Night Football showdown with Kenneth Walker III and the Kansas City Chiefs (4-0). NBC and Peacock have the broadcast at 5:15 pm PT on Oct. 25.

title: Seahawks Reacts results: Fans lean toward playoffs again, but no NFC West title
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. How’s everybody feeling? Two losses in three games isn’t a comfortable place to sit, as a […]
full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. How’s everybody feeling? Two losses in three games isn’t a comfortable place to sit, as a fan of a team who is the defending champs and have aspirations for an attempt at a repeat. The Seattle Seahawks lost in Week 5, to possibly the biggest threat in the NFC to another long playoff run for the Seahawks. A team that had to have taken it personally that their bitter rivals had cigars in their teeth and damaged their locker room from celebrating a Lombardi Trophy win . Are moral victories a thing? Depends on your perspective. Seattle fumbled three times and was intercepted twice and still had a chance to win that thing. Last year, Sam Darnold only had three games where he threw multiple interceptions, and two were the Rams. The game against the San Francisco 49ers was a total meltdown but was still a tight game down to the very end. Having that been said, how are Seahawk fans feeling about the franchise’s chances moving forward? Well, 93% still believe that this team is making the playoffs, although that comes with a caveat. After topping some power rankings to begin the year, Seattle fans overwhelmingly (70% of those polled) see them as a wild card team. While there is a lot of season left, with less than 1/3 of the regular season games having been decided, this is somewhat understandable, as the Seattle Seahawks currently sit outside of the playoff picture. In the NFL’s playoff format, a team needs to either win their division (seeds 1-4) or earn a 5, 6 or 7-seed as a wild card team. In the 2025 Super Bowl-winning season last year, Seattle was the #1 seed in the NFC, won during a dramatic last-second win against the Los Angeles Rams. Both the Rams (5) and the San Francisco 49ers (6) entered the tournament last season as wild card teams. The Hawks are currently in a logjam of records, tied with 10 other teams at 3-2 with the 4th-best win percentage thus far (0.600). It might be tough for the Seahawks to catch the Niners (5-0), who join the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings as the triumvirate of undefeated teams in the league headed into Week 6. The NFC north trio of the Bears, Lions and Packers also have 3-2 records and currently squeeze Seattle out of the picture. Despite the current climate, a majority of 12’s seem to believe this is heading in a better direction. It’s a 59/41 split between those who are confident the Seattle Seahawks are headed in the right direction and those who don’t. The Seahawks still look forward to the returns of Anthony Bradford, Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price, as well as the continued health and re-acclimation of Tory Horton, Trevon Diggs, Sam Darnold and Ty Okada. Needless to say, a Thursday primetime game against the similarly 3-2 Denver Broncos is a chance to make a statement, after an absolute street fight against a contender last week. title: Seahawks elevate pair of special teams players for Broncos game
summary: Through the first month of the season, the Seattle Seahawks struggled with kickoff coverage and rank near the bottom of the league in yards allowed per return, but they’re set to gain a key special teams asset ahead of a crucial Week 6 road matchup against the Denver Broncos. The team announced they’ve elevated wide […]
full_text: Through the first month of the season, the Seattle Seahawks struggled with kickoff coverage and rank near the bottom of the league in yards allowed per return, but they’re set to gain a key special teams asset ahead of a crucial Week 6 road matchup against the Denver Broncos. The team announced they’ve elevated wide receiver and special teams gunner Irv Charles, as well as linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo from the practice squad. Both will make their team debuts. Acquired from the New York Jets in May , Charles missed the first five games while on injured reserve with a knee issue but was designated to return to practice on October 7. Seattle activated him to the active roster on Tuesday , although, he was released a day later to make room for running back Velus Jones Jr . As a vested veteran, Charles wasn’t subject to waivers and rerouted to the practice squad. Upon his return, Charles is expected to play a key role on kick and punt returns—areas where he’s highly regarded. On the defensive side, Ciarlo’s elevation was expected given the Seahawks will be without starting linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (chest), leaving a thin group even thinner. The third year linebacker went undrafted out of Army in 2024 before signing with the Jets, but missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury. He was released in May, 2025 and spent time with the Buffalo Bills, Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans prior to signing with the Seahawks on September 30.

Seattle is coming off a frustrating 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, while Denver enters the game after a 23-17 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Both teams are 3-2, but their paths to victory look different: Seattle needs to protect the football and keep its passing game productive, while Denver must find ways to pressure Sam Darnold and make life difficult for the Seahawks’ offense. Here are three predictions worth considering for Thursday night. 1. Jaxon Smith-Njigba Over 91.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Jaxon Smith-Njigba has been one of the NFL’s most productive receivers through the first five weeks, and his role in Seattle’s offense makes this one of the most appealing player props on the board. Smith-Njigba has recorded 583 receiving yards on 37 catches and 50 targets, averaging 116.6 yards per game. He has exceeded 91.5 yards in four of Seattle’s five games, giving him a strong track record against this number. Denver’s defense is a challenging matchup, but the absence of cornerback Pat Surtain II makes the assignment more favorable. Seattle should continue to feature Smith-Njigba as its primary receiving option, particularly when the offense needs to move the chains on third down. The main concern is Denver’s ability to disrupt the timing of Seattle’s passing game. Still, Smith-Njigba’s target share and production make the over worth considering at this number. The pick: JSN over 91.5 receiving yards. 2. AJ Barner Anytime Touchdown Scorer (+380) AJ Barner is an intriguing touchdown candidate because of his role in Seattle’s passing game and the potential matchup against Denver’s linebackers. Alex Singleton is a player worth targeting in coverage, particularly when offenses use tight ends to attack the middle of the field. Barner can give Seattle another option in that area, and his red-zone with Barnyard involvement makes the anytime touchdown market more appealing than a simple bet on receiving yards. Barner has caught 12 passes for 122 yards through five games, averaging 24.4 receiving yards per contest. His season totals don’t make him a high-volume receiver, but touchdown bets are about opportunities in scoring situations as much as overall production. Seattle can use motion, play-action and formations that force Denver’s linebackers to make difficult decisions. If the Seahawks can create a favorable matchup for Barner near the goal line, he has a realistic path to finding the end zone. The pick: AJ Barner anytime touchdown scorer. 3. Over 41.5 Total Points (-105) The game total offers another angle on Thursday night’s matchup. FanDuel listed the total at 41.5 points, with the over priced at -105. Check the live board before placing a wager, since both the number and the price can change. Seattle enters the game averaging 26.8 points per contest, while Denver has scored 19.4 points per game. Those numbers suggest that the Seahawks could do much of the scoring work, but the over doesn’t necessarily require both offenses to produce at their season averages. Smith-Njigba’s production gives Seattle a clear path to moving the ball through the air. If the Seahawks can turn those drives into touchdowns rather than settling for field goals, they could put significant pressure on Denver’s offense to respond. The Broncos, meanwhile, have enough talent to capitalize on short fields or create scoring opportunities when Bo Nix can avoid negative plays. A couple of explosive gains or turnovers could help push the game beyond the number. There are reasons to be cautious. Seattle’s defense has been strong, Denver’s offense has struggled to produce consistently, and the market has moved toward a lower total. The over depends on Seattle sustaining its offensive production and Denver contributing enough to keep the scoreboard moving. The pick: Over 41.5 total points (-105). 4. Emanuel Wilson Under 66.5 Rushing Yards (-118) Emanuel Wilson’s rushing yardage line looks a little too high given Seattle’s struggles to establish a consistent ground game. Wilson finished with 61 rushing yards on 20 carries against San Francisco, falling short of this number despite receiving a substantial workload. Wilson is averaging 50.2 rushing yards per game this season, well below the 66.5-yard threshold. He has also been inconsistent from week to week, recording 14 yards against Washington and 3 against New England before producing bigger performances against Arizona and the Chargers. Seattle’s offensive line has had difficulty creating consistent running lanes, and the Seahawks may need to lean more heavily on Sam Darnold and the passing game to move the ball. Wilson’s workload gives him a chance to clear this number, but he needs both volume and efficiency to get there. Given his season average and Seattle’s inconsistency on the ground, the under is worth considering. title: Seahawks vs. Broncos game preview: Can Seattle get back on track in Denver?
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are looking to bounce back from a painful loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but a short week leaves little time to regroup. Seattle heads to Denver on Thursday to face the Broncos, with both teams sitting at 3-2. For the Seahawks, this is an opportunity to correct course before their divisional […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 08: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos looks for a pass during the third quarter of the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 08, 2024 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks are looking to bounce back from a painful loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but a short week leaves little time to regroup. Seattle heads to Denver on Thursday to face the Broncos, with both teams sitting at 3-2. For the Seahawks, this is an opportunity to correct course before their divisional loss creates bigger problems in the NFC West race. These teams have plenty of history. Seattle and Denver shared the AFC West until the Seahawks moved to the NFC West in 2002, and their rivalry produced one of the most memorable games in franchise history: Seattle’s 43-8 demolition of the Broncos in Super Bowl 48. The Seahawks have also won the two most recent meetings, beating Denver 17-16 in the 2022 season opener and 26-20 in Mike Macdonald’s head-coaching debut in 2024. The Russell Wilson trade and the occasional friction between Sean Payton and Macdonald have added another layer to the matchup. Both teams need a win, but Seattle has more immediate problems to solve. Here are the matchups that could decide Thursday night’s game—and what the Seahawks need to do to leave Denver with a victory. Turnovers: Seattle’s biggest problem Seattle has plenty to fix, but nothing is more urgent than protecting the football. The Seahawks have committed nine turnovers this season. Opponents have scored 44 points off those turnovers over that span. This is no longer an occasional mistake; it is undermining the entire operation. The problems start with an offense struggling to find a rhythm. The offensive line has had trouble protecting Sam Darnold and creating running lanes, leaving the quarterback in increasingly difficult situations. Darnold has also alternated between passing up opportunities and forcing reads that lead to costly mistakes. Against San Francisco, Seattle turned the ball over four times, including two interceptions and two lost fumble. Those giveaways affect the entire team. They give opponents shorter fields, put the defense under immediate pressure, and increase the workload on a unit already trying to keep the game under control. The resulting cycle is difficult to break, especially when the offense cannot sustain drives. A short week offers little time for major corrections. Seattle does not need to reinvent its offense by Thursday, but it does need to simplify where necessary, make better decisions, and take care of the ball. On the road against a capable defense, another turnover-heavy performance could be decisive. The offensive line faces a serious test Denver has the personnel to pressure Darnold from both the edge and the interior. Nik Bonitto is a major threat off the edge, while Zach Allen can disrupt the pocket from inside. Seattle’s offensive line will have to account for multiple rush threats rather than concentrating on one defender. The concern goes beyond sacks. Inconsistent protection disrupts the timing of the offense, while an ineffective running game makes Seattle easier to diagnose. If Denver can anticipate pass situations, the Seahawks risk putting Darnold in exactly the kind of high-pressure environment that has contributed to their recent turnovers. Seattle’s running back situation makes the challenge harder. With Zach Charbonnet out and Jadarian Price on IR, the options are limited, and the ground game has struggled to produce consistently. Blocking, vision, and play design all need to improve. The Seahawks may not be able to establish a dominant rushing attack, but they need enough credible production to keep Denver from teeing off on obvious passing downs. Seattle needs options beyond Jaxon Smith-Njigba Jaxon Smith-Njigba is Seattle’s best offensive player right now, and building the passing game around him makes sense. The problem is when he becomes the only dependable option. Against Denver, the Seahawks have an opportunity to spread the ball around and take advantage of a depleted secondary. The Broncos will be without cornerback Patrick Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga. Riley Moss is questionable after missing the previous game against the Chargers. If Moss cannot play, Denver will have to lean further on its depth in the secondary. Seattle should not respond by simply forcing more targets to Smith-Njigba. JSN has also been listed with an ankle issue. He will play, but the Seahawks need a plan that can function if their top receiver is limited. The production from the other pass catchers suggests there is room for a more balanced approach. Tory Horton has seen limited opportunities, Cooper Kupp needs a larger role, and Rashid Shaheed has not been heavily involved in the passing game. Tight end A.J. Barner and the running backs can also provide useful outlets. One matchup deserves particular attention: linebacker Alex Singleton. According to the Next Gen Stats figures cited for this game, Singleton has been targeted 27 times this season, the most among NFL linebackers. He has allowed 21 receptions for 248 yards, the second-highest total at the position. Seattle should test that weakness with crossing routes, digs, slants, and tight end combinations that force Singleton to cover in space. These concepts can create windows between the linebackers and safeties while giving Darnold quick answers against pressure. Running backs can add another layer with short receptions, especially if Denver’s linebackers retreat to protect the middle. The goal is not to reduce Smith-Njigba’s role. It is to make Denver defend the entire field. If Kupp, Shaheed, Horton, Barner, and the backs become credible options, the Broncos will have a harder time devoting extra attention to JSN. Checkdowns have their place, but Seattle needs more than one reliable answer in the passing game. Josh Jobe has become a target—and Denver knows it The loss to San Francisco highlighted a recurring concern: Josh Jobe has become a vulnerable spot in Seattle’s secondary. Opponents have reason to test him with their best receiving options, looking for openings in coverage or opportunities to draw penalties. Mike Evans was the most notable example against the 49ers, finishing with seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. His performance highlighted the difficulty Seattle had containing that matchup. Denver could take a similar approach, targeting Jobe and forcing the Seahawks to show they can protect him. If the matchup keeps producing, the Broncos have little reason to move away from it. Macdonald and the defensive staff need a counter. One option is to provide safety help over the top when Denver aligns a dangerous receiver against Jobe. That does not mean permanently dedicating a safety to his side and leaving other areas exposed; it means identifying the situations where the risk is greatest and adjusting accordingly. Seattle can also vary its man and zone looks, use leverage that provides help inside or over the top, and change the matchups on third down. When the formation allows it, Witherspoon could take on more difficult assignments. The key is to avoid leaving Jobe isolated against Denver’s best options without a clear plan for support. Pritchett played just four snaps against San Francisco, and Seattle should be willing to consider alternatives when the current approach is struggling. More playing time would not guarantee better results, but it would give the coaching staff another option to evaluate. This is not about declaring Pritchett the answer. It is about recognizing that the current matchup needs a response. If Denver identifies the same weakness and Seattle makes no adjustments, the secondary could be in for another long night. Getting pressure on Bo Nix is essential Seattle’s pass rush needs more consistent production off the edge. Macdonald’s scheme uses…

summary: A big development in the AI space is that neurons are now legible. full_text: A big development in the AI space is that neurons are now legible . With all these advancements in science and technology, we might finally come closer to understand what the hell is going on in Kyle Shanahan’s brain. I’m so grateful we have the football version of Leonardo Da Vinci coaching my favorite football team. I’m even more grateful that the Denver Broncos beat the Seattle Seahawks. 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey is working less. His thoughts? It’s complicated (paywall) “I want to win — whatever it takes to win games,” McCaffrey said. “I think what I love about this team is you’ve got a bunch of selfish, unselfish guys. Obviously, people want the ball every play, but not at the expense of the team. … “I think we’ve got to do whatever it takes to win and when you have a roster like ours where the ball can get spread around so much, you should probably not get as many touches, either. It’s never my job to count them, but to make them count.” Why is Shanahan finally taking better care of McCaffrey this season? It’s not about extending his career. It’s about reinvigorating his rushing attack.” Mike Evans broke ribs and got even better: How the 49ers WR’s history made him who he is (paywall) “But over time, his skills sharpened, and he became a sort of point forward — someone who could bring the ball up the court, guard the opponent’s tallest player and finish with 16 rebounds. He plays wide receiver like a rebounder, using his tremendous length — the 6-foot-5 Evans has a nearly 7-foot wingspan — to box out defensive backs when the ball is in the air. The quarterback’s rule when targeting Evans: Even when he’s not open, he’s open. “It’s feel, and it’s years of repetition,” Evans said of knowing where a defender is even when he’s behind him. “That helps a lot.” Terry Petteway also learned how to tap into his pupil’s hypercompetitiveness. He’d point to the biggest kid on the other squad and tell Mike he couldn’t guard him. “He’d look over and say, ‘What? That guy?’” Terry recalled. “Then he’d go and tear the guy’s head off. All you needed to do to motivate Mike was tell him he couldn’t do something.” Asked whether Evans ever got into fights on the court or football field, Terry laughed. “That’s not a fair question!” he protested. “I’m gonna put it this way: Mike was never, ever going to back down from anybody. And he’s still like that today.” Christian Kirk getting closer to making a difference for injury-riddled 49ers “I believe I have a lot of really good football left,” Kirk said on Thursday. “In no way, shape or form, I thought about anything other than that. It’s just all about working to get my body back to feeling great, to be able to go out and play.” Kawakami: John Lynch’s near-perfect offseason has relaunched this 49ers era (paywall) “I’ve already said that Odighizuwa is better than Hargrave. Let’s go bigger than that with this rookie: Halton’s Seahawks-wrecking performance last Sunday was the 49ers’ best game by a defensive tackle since DeForest Buckner in his prime. And Halton is only 22. It’s early. But Halton, the 107th pick in this draft, looks like he’s everything the 49ers hoped to get when they signed Hargrave or took Alfred Collins 43rd in 2025 and Javon Kinlaw 14th in 2020. The minor complication is that Halton looks like a natural three-technique DT. And you usually play only one of those at a time, with a nose-tackle type next to him on early downs. But lining up two explosive three-technique types together, with Odighizuwa and Halton, makes for a very dynamic interior DL.” Kyle Shanahan shares updates ahead of 49ers-Commanders game “San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan spoke with reporters ahead of Thursday’s practice as the team prepares for its Week 6 matchup against the Washington Commanders.” 49ers injury updates: Christian Kirk returns; Mike Evans is dealing with a new injury “As for Bosa’s availability for Monday night, Shanahan said, “Hoping he can go, but not going to practice today.” He believes it won’t be an injury that lingers for the rest of the season. Linebacker Nick Martin won’t return this week. There was speculation about Martin returning with Greenlaw and Wallow out, but Shanahan said, “He’s not getting up this week.” Deebo Samuel could head to the injured reserve. Shanahan said, “I think if we didn’t have that bye week, it’d be around that area. But gaining that week where we don’t play is still why we’re trying to wait on that right now. And hope we don’t have to do it.” Wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling is “a ways away,” but Shanahan thinks he’s on track. There’s an “outside chance” Demarcus Robinson returns before the bye week. Shanahan said they’re hoping to have him back after the bye, which is his way of saying that’s the expectation.

title: Seattle Seahawks vs. Denver Broncos Game Thread: We in for a snooze fest?
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are taking on the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football in a game between the San Francisco 49ers’ last two opponents. The Seahawks are 3-2 after their loss to the 49ers on Sunday, while the Broncos are 3-2 after another uninspiring win, this time on the road over the 0-5 Los Angeles […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - OCTOBER 11: Quarterback Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks signals a play in action during a game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks are taking on the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football in a game between the San Francisco 49ers’ last two opponents. The Seahawks are 3-2 after their loss to the 49ers on Sunday, while the Broncos are 3-2 after another uninspiring win, this time on the road over the 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers. Both offenses have struggled so far compared to their 2025 levels, while the defenses have been good on both sides. Seattle’s defense ranks second in EPA allowed per play, while Denver’s ranks 8th. Denver will be without Patrick Surtain and Talanoa Hufanga, however, and their defense has been susceptible to the run at times this season, ranking 28th in EPA allowed per rush. Seattle, however, has had one of the most inefficient rushing attacks in the NFL, which is why we could be in for a physical, low-scoring game on Thursday. Overall, the Broncos are 24th in EPA per play, while the Seahawks are 26th (and 30th in EPA per rush). For the Seahawks, the offense has instead been funneled through Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who has 49 catches for 583 yards and seven touchdowns through four games. Denver hasn’t really gotten going in the air, with quarterback Bo Nix really struggling to start the season. Perhaps the Broncos can get reignited with Sean Payton at the helm as the playcaller, although that wasn’t the case in his first week at the helm on Sunday. Urgency will fall more on the loser of this one, as they’d fall to 3-3 two weeks out of the trade deadline.

full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers promoted Ogbo Okoronkwo to the active roster and signed linebacker Eugene Asante to the practice squad. Asante will likely be elevated for Monday Night Football with Dre Greenlaw suspended and Garret Wallow dealing with a hamstring injury. Asante ran a 4.48 40-yard dash and had a 10-yard split in the 96th percentile. He’s on the roster to cover kicks. Asante was an undrafted free agent out of Auburn in 2025. Asante spent time on the practice squads of the Dolphins, Browns, Falcons, and Cardinals. Raheem Morris should be able to vouch for the type of player Asante is. Arizona released him from its practice squad on October 13. The big news is the 49ers opening the practice window for wide receiver Christian Kirk. He’s been dealing with a calf injury since the first day of training camp. It’s been three and a half months since Kirk played football. The 49ers have two games before their bye. It’s reasonable to think the Niners will give Kirk a few weeks to get back up to speed and in football shape; that way, he can hit the ground running when they return from the bye. Kyle Shanahan said Kirk has had setbacks since he hurt his hamstring on the first day of training camp, which is why we haven’t seen him in so long. Shanahan said Kirk had a “real good week and an awesome weekend,” so Thursday’ll be Kirk’s first official day back. Here are the injuries for Thursday’s practice: Out: WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) LB Garret Wallow (hamstring) DT James Thompson (ankle) EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) S Marques Sigle (ankle WR Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) Limited: DB Siran Neal (neck) RT Colton McKivitz (sick) FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee) WR Christian Kirk (calf) CB Upton Stout (shoulder) Shanahan said Evans is dealing with Achilles soreness. As for Bosa’s availability for Monday night, Shanahan said, “Hoping he can go, but not going to practice today.” He believes it won’t be an injury that lingers for the rest of the season. Linebacker Nick Martin won’t return this week. There was speculation about Martin returning with Greenlaw and Wallow out, but Shanahan said, “He’s not getting up this week.” Deebo Samuel could head to the injured reserve. Shanahan said, “I think if we didn’t have that bye week, it’d be around that area. But gaining that week where we don’t play is still why we’re trying to wait on that right now. And hope we don’t have to do it.” Wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling is “a ways away,” but Shanahan thinks he’s on track. There’s an “outside chance” Demarcus Robinson returns before the bye week. Shanahan said they’re hoping to have him back after the bye, which is his way of saying that’s the expectation.

title: 49ers Stock Report: Evaluating the offensive line through five weeks
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have seen many surprises over the first five weeks of 2026. The defensive line and pass rush have come alive without Nick Bosa; the 49ers’ secondary has developed, particularly Renardo Green; and despite multiple injuries in the wide receiver room, Mike Evans looks every bit the receiver he was in his […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers have seen many surprises over the first five weeks of 2026. The defensive line and pass rush have come alive without Nick Bosa; the 49ers’ secondary has developed, particularly Renardo Green; and despite multiple injuries in the wide receiver room, Mike Evans looks every bit the receiver he was in his prime. I would argue the biggest surprise in 2026 has been the 49ers’ offensive line. During a press conference from training camp, Kyle Shanahan said he never understood the “hate” the offensive line received, proving the team does hear chatter, whether online or from pundits and analysts. Five weeks in, the 49ers organization, Shanahan, and offensive line coach Chris Foerster deserve a ton of credit for sticking with their plan. The continuity is there, even with Connor Colby at left guard, and the line has gelled together. The hope is this play continues into January when the games become more important. As of now, the 49ers have a top-five offensive line, and it is hard to argue against their case. According to Football Insights , the 49ers’ pressure responsibility across the five lineman positions goes 11.6% to Trent Williams, 32.6% to Connor Colby (inflated by Byron Murphy on Sunday, for what it’s worth), 11.6% to Jake Brendel, 14% to Dominick Puni, 18.6% to Colton McKivitz, 16.3% to Brock Purdy, and 7% to blocking tight ends and blitz pickups. For reference, each position is either very good (Williams) or above average, aside from Colby, who sports the second-highest pressure responsibility at left guard. Colby has been fine this season, but Sunday’s performance has drastically changed his number. Here’s a stat for you. The five offensive linemen with the longest snap streak without allowing a sack are as follows: LT Garett Bolles, Denver – 1,077 snaps LG Joe Thuney, Chicago – 1,038 snaps C Lucas Patrick, Washington – 1,031 snaps C Erik McCoy, New Orleans – 1,020 snaps C Jake Brendel, San Francisco – 921 snaps Yes, you are reading that correctly. Brendel hasn’t allowed a sack since Week 16 of 2024. How remarkable is that? The common outcry is about the 49ers’ investments in the offensive line. What it boils down to is that people want first-round investments. The 49ers have invested in the line, but not with first-round picks. Puni and McKivitz were drafted and developed. Colby was drafted and has more development potential in the future. The 49ers pulled off one of the best trades in franchise history with the trade for Williams. Brendel was a free-agent signing. Are the 49ers not investing in the offensive line? Yes, but they are doing it in a way that hasn’t required a first-round pick. Over five weeks, it is hard to argue with their process and the results. Brock Purdy was finally sacked for the first time, but Seattle’s defensive line is excellent. Purdy’s ability to navigate the pocket and his elusiveness outside of the pocket certainly has contributed to the offensive line’s success, but there is no doubt the line has been excellent so far in 2026. Offensive line development is complicated. Players with all the tools fail in the NFL, and players who develop and work turn into plus starters. Bravo, Shanahan, and Foerster. The plan has come together at the best time, and if this continues, the 49ers will have as good a chance as anyone to finish the job. title: 10 players on bad teams that could be of interest to the 49ers at the trade deadline
summary: Five weeks into the NFL season, we’ve seen some teams establish themselves, while others have disappointed. The San Francisco 49ers are on the former side of that spectrum, impressing with a 5-0 start as they’ve beaten three playoff teams from a season ago, including the defending champion Seattle Seahawks last weekend. However, not every team […]
full_text: Five weeks into the NFL season, we’ve seen some teams establish themselves, while others have disappointed. The San Francisco 49ers are on the former side of that spectrum, impressing with a 5-0 start as they’ve beaten three playoff teams from a season ago, including the defending champion Seattle Seahawks last weekend. However, not every team has taken that trajectory. We’ve seen teams like the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans be major disappointments early, while six other NFL teams have won one game or fewer. With the trade deadline coming up in a few weeks, some of those teams could turn into sellers, while the 49ers, with their ample draft capital, could become a clear buyer. San Francisco has a few needs, such as pass-rush depth and help at wide receiver, but who all could be available for them to snag? Let’s look at 10 players on bad teams that could pique the 49ers interest at the deadline. Chargers OLB Khalil Mack Perhaps the most obvious candidate of the bunch is Khalil Mack, who signed a one-year, $18 million extension with the Los Angeles Chargers this offseason. Mack, 35, still has some pass-rush juice. He’s got 14 pressures on the season, although only with a 9.5 percent pass-rush win rate, according to PFF. He’s been healthy, though, and is a solid player against the run. He’ll get a ton of 1-on-1 opportunities in San Francisco if traded there. Chargers EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu If the 49ers are willing to pay a heavier price, they could just look at the other Chargers pass rusher: edge Tuli Tuipulotu. Tuipulotu leads Los Angeles with 17 pressures and a 16.0 percent pass-rush win rate, while also recording eight defensive stops. He had 75 pressures and 13 sacks in a breakout campaign last season and is in the final year of his rookie deal. He could be a younger target to buy at the deadline, albeit likely at a heftier price. Chargers WR Quentin Johnston This one isn’t a pretty name, and would not come with much of a price tag. But the 49ers could also buy on Quentin Johnston to serve as that vertical threat along with Demarcus Robinson and De’Zhaun Stribling when they return. Johnston hasn’t been a good NFL receiver, and an $18 million fifth-year option could be the deterrent, but the 49ers need some speed and help on the perimeter with their injuries. Perhaps he’s a low-cost option. Saints TE Juwan Johnson In an outside-the-box move, the 49ers could target 30-year-old Saints tight end Juwan Johnson as an extra pass-catcher. The 49ers have always wanted that second receiving threat at tight end, which Kyle Juszczyk has essentially been, but Johnson doesn’t have any more guaranteed money on his deal (one year left at $9.5 million) and could be a trade option for the reeling 1-4 Saints. Commanders DT Daron Payne Payne has been subject to trade rumors for a while now, and it could be the year in 2026 with the veteran defensive lineman in the final year of his deal. Payne, 29, has 15 pressures, eight defensive stops, and a forced fumble. He does have a hefty $16.4 million salary, so Washington would probably have to eat some of that money in a trade. Commanders EDGE K’Lavon Chaisson Another option could be K’Lavon Chaisson, who signed a one-year, $11 million deal with the Commanders in the offseason after being a key piece for the Super Bowl-contending New England Patriots last year. Chaisson is Washington’s leader in pressures with 17, and he could be a cheap option off the edge as a pass-rush specialist. Titans edge Jermaine Johnson II Johnson is in the final year of his rookie deal for the 0-5 Titans and is a natural trade candidate on the edge at the deadline. He’s had 11 pressures thus far this year with only a 6.7 percent pass rush win rate, but is a younger candidate than some of the other edges on the market, with familiarity with Robert Saleh. He could be a cheap sell candidate. Titans WR Calvin Ridley On the topic of veteran receivers that could fill a short-term need, Ridley fits the bill as a boundary wideout who could be on the move at the deadline. He’s past his prime at 31 years old, but should also come cheap and can fill a void with the team’s current injuries. With players coming back for the 49ers, it isn’t a need to trade for a big-time name at receiver. Instead, a veteran who can fill a role for a few weeks and provide an upgrade over the current room is what’s needed. Buccaneers DT A’Shawn Robinson Robinson has been a rotational defensive tackle for the Buccaneers, and could give the 49ers some depth as a quality run-defending body in the middle of the defensive line. He’s on a one-year deal and should come cheap if the 49ers or another suitor are interested. Buccaneers EDGE YaYa Diaby Diaby was a standout in 2025, recording 62 pressures and a 17.4 percent pass-rush win rate to go with his seven sacks. He hasn’t had the best start to his 2026 campaign and is in the final year of his rookie contract. If the Buccaneers aren’t willing to pay him, the 49ers could deal a Day 2 pick for the pass-rusher and have the flexibility of retaining him or getting a potential compensatory pick in return.

title: Brock Purdy can achieve an NFL first on Monday Night Football
summary: Brock Purdy has had a phenomenal start to the season. While he hasn’t played faultless football, the 49ers quarterback clearly has taken his game to another level and, after key playmaking in a thrilling road win over the Seattle Seahawks, now leads the MVP race. Purdy leads the NFL in passing touchdowns (13), success rate […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after defeating the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brock Purdy has had a phenomenal start to the season. While he hasn’t played faultless football, the 49ers quarterback clearly has taken his game to another level and, after key playmaking in a thrilling road win over the Seattle Seahawks, now leads the MVP race . Purdy leads the NFL in passing touchdowns (13), success rate (57.9%), and QBR (85.5), while he is tied for first with Lamar Jackson in adjusted EPA per play . Though recent matchups with the Denver Broncos and the Seahawks presented Purdy with more issues than he faced over the opening three weeks, Purdy has been a picture of consistency through five games, and has the chance for a history-making streak when the 49ers host the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football to round off Week 6. Purdy has multiple touchdowns and a passer rating of at least 90 in all five of his games so far this season. Should he continue that run against Washington, he will become the only player in NFL history within their first five career seasons to record multiple touchdown passes and a passer rating of 90 or higher in their team’s first six games of a season. Against a Washington defense that ranks 23rd in EPA per play and 25th in dropback EPA per play, the signs point to another profitable game for Purdy. One concern for San Francisco is the injuries that continue to afflict the wide receiver position, with Deebo Samuel set to miss his reunion with the Commanders with a hamstring injury. However, with Mike Evans in devastatingly effective form and tight end George Kittle hopefully free of the illness he battled through in Seattle, the hope will be that the 49ers’ weaponry is more than sufficient for Purdy to capture that piece of history and, more importantly, help deliver San Francisco’s sixth straight win.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Is it time for the 49ers to finally go all in?
summary: At 5-0, the San Francisco 49ers are enjoying one of their best starts under head coach Kyle Shanahan, especially when considering they’ve beaten three potential Super Bowl contenders through five weeks. The offense has been clicking behind MVP frontrunner Brock Purdy, who has thrown for 1,196 yards, 13 touchdowns, and two interceptions, while completing 69.0 […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos interacts with Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers after an NFL football game at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images At 5-0, the San Francisco 49ers are enjoying one of their best starts under head coach Kyle Shanahan, especially when considering they’ve beaten three potential Super Bowl contenders through five weeks. The offense has been clicking behind MVP frontrunner Brock Purdy, who has thrown for 1,196 yards, 13 touchdowns, and two interceptions, while completing 69.0 percent of his passes. The defense, on the other hand, has looked quite good despite dealing with injuries to the defensive line, as Raheem Morris has his unit ranked third in EPA allowed per play and third in points allowed per game. For years, one of the questions surrounding the 49ers is whether it’s time to push the chips all in and make a splash. Their roster remains one of the oldest in the NFL, and we’ve seen them make some big trades at the deadline, including ones for Christian McCaffrey and Chase Young. We’ve also seen them make other minor moves that have turned out to be quite meaningful, such as trades for Charles Omenihu and even the recent deal for Keion White last year. The 49ers have the requisite draft capital to make a move, as they have one pick in every round in the 2027 NFL Draft. Is it time to go all in? 49ers legend Steve Young believes so, and he shared his thoughts on KNBR on Wednesday. “Can we just take this 5-0 and build off it and just take it and run the table and just not worry about anything? I think that part of us feels like, yeah, we probably should,” Young said about the 49ers. “If we’re going to, if we’re going to go all in, and I know every one of these guys, Trent, they’re all going to be irritated that you hear this, but you can’t help it. You get old fast in the NFL. And so when you have great players, you got to take advantage. And so the window, we talk about the window. And it’s like you got these guys that are all healthy, all performing, 4 guys on offense that are going to the Hall of Fame. Like, you gotta go all in. “It’s like, in some ways, I don’t want to say it’s Ram-like, because you know that they’ve been doing the last couple years, like, they’re going all in. And I’m not saying to copy them because we’ve always been all in. Way before the Rams were doing it, we were doing it. So yeah, I think that we’ve got to optimize like Brock [Purdy] has done with his game. like Mike Evans has brought in, like optimize and make sure that we’re doing everything we can. ‘Cause 2026, I don’t really wanna think about 2027, ’28, ’29. I don’t wanna think about what that looks like. I really think you can smell that 2026 can be that year, but let’s go all in. How can the 49ers push the chips in? What do they need to target at the deadline? “Let’s figure out how to bolster, which we think inevitably by December, if our pass rush is middling, it’ll cost us,” Young continued. “It’ll be a problem. And then if we don’t have the depth, because then we can’t keep everybody healthy the whole time, we better have some depth because the Rams are in a really tight spot, but you can see how good they are, and they’re gonna get healthier. Myles [Garrett] is gonna come back and play, and they’re really good. You saw them on Monday night. They got beat, but you can see how good they are. You can see how good Seattle is. And so in that way, they’re not going away, so we should lean in.” Over the past few trade deadlines, I think the 49ers have done a really good job of assessing their team and status and understanding the time to leverage their draft picks for a move that helps them in the current window. When you look at the two major moves San Francisco made recently at the deadline, they directly correlated with success that led them to a Super Bowl. The 49ers traded for Christian McCaffrey at the deadline in 2022 in a spot of urgency, understanding they were 3-3 and really needing to turn the ship around. They ended up winning their last 10 games that season and beat both the Seattle Seahawks and Dallas Cowboys in the playoffs before their injuries at quarterback in the NFC Championship Game against the Philadelphia Eagles. The following year? With McCaffrey in the fold along with their other elite talent, the 49ers, sitting at 5-3 at the deadline coming off three straight losses, traded for Chase Young, and they went 7-2 the rest of the way, winning the division and reaching the Super Bowl, where they fell just short to the Kansas City Chiefs. It was a similar story back in 2019, when the 49ers traded a Day 2 pick for Emmanuel Sanders, giving them the necessary help they needed at wide receiver to reach the Super Bowl a year after going 4-12. Then, in other years, we’ve seen them make minor moves, like the trades for Charles Omenihu and Keion White, that paid off in that year, but even more the year after with the extra year of team control. It feels like a pass rusher is going to be an inevitable add, given the 49ers’ state at the position and the number of players that usually become available. Receiver could be a possibility, but San Francisco should start getting guys back healthy after the bye week. Depth, like Young mentioned, could be the other area, which also ties into the defensive line. The 49ers are certainly going to have competition in the NFC, and their roster is getting older. With their current draft capital and how well their younger guys are playing, in addition to their veteran talent, it does feel like a ripe moment to push the chips in for a trade or two at the deadline.

We have a lot of season left but man… really pulling for DJ Jones to replicate the success that Gracen Halton and Osa Odighizuwa had against Seattle’s interior. Five reasons why 49ers are 5-0 and atop the NFL despite epic rash of injuries (paywall) “ Steve Young has talked about elite QBs reaching a career sweet spot when their Xs-and-Os knowledge allows them to toy with defenses. He has said that a problem for many is that once they reach that level of mental mastery, their physical skills have diminished. At 26, Purdy may not have achieved genius QB status yet. But something is clearly clicking in his fifth season in Kyle Shanahan’s system…Purdy has made it clear that his ongoing ascent is tied to Shanahan’s system and his increased understanding of its complexities. Shanahan told a Fox broadcast crew this season that Purdy is now starting to understand the “why” of his play calls…..Morris, a safety at Hofstra, was a longtime NFL defensive backs coach, and he might have made his biggest impact in the secondary. The 49ers are still playing primarily zone, but Morris has introduced more match coverage, which allows zone defenders to closely attach to a receiver if a specific route is run.” 49ers practice and media schedule ahead of Week 6 matchup vs. Commanders | “Thursday, October 15 12:35 p.m. – Kyle Shanahan press conference 1:30 p.m. – Practice Friday, October 16 12:30 p.m. – Practice After practice (approx. 2:20 p.m.) – Raheem Morris press conference Following Morris – Klay Kubiak press conference Following Kubiak – Brock Purdy press conference Saturday, October 17 12:35 p.m. – Practice After practice (approx. 1:35 p.m.) – Kyle Shanahan press conference.” 49ers rookie report: The long-term upside is there for this class “Black’s averaging 2.6 yards per carry in the red zone. That jumps to 3.9 yards per carry on non-red-zone carries. The good news is he’s bouncing off tackles, falling forward, and gaining yards after the contact. But he’s also getting stuffed behind the line of scrimmage and failing to force missed tackles. Black struggles to resist the urge to bounce runs that don’t need to or to stop his feet in the backfield. In 1-on-1 situations, he’s indecisive instead of being the aggressor….Halton’s awareness is off the charts. He’s a much better run defender than anticipated. He’s the type of player who causes chaos, and his plays don’t always show up in the box score….It’s been impressive to watch Dugger hold his own against 300-pounders. Four of his seven targets have resulted in first downs, but he’s only surrendering 6.4 yards per reception on those. Week 5 showed that some of those were by design, essentially conceding underneath throws to take away the bigger threat.” 49ers legend Steve Young says Brock Purdy has reached a new level “When I saw him in the Rams game in Australia, I’m like, ‘Whoa, he’s quicker. Whoa, his decision-making is even faster,'” Young said. “He optimized in the offseason. Whoever trained him, whoever—like if he did it himself, I don’t know—but whoever did needs a shout-out as well, because he had optimized his game. “And his game is unique, and unique to him, and he just, instead of kind of resting on all the things that he’s already good at, I felt like he got better. I felt like he’s even more aware. He’s quicker with his reads. And his body, it feels like he’s niftier, and actually has some speed. Like he did speed work, you could tell… ….I always said, it’s 3rd-and-10, my mom’s open, she’s getting the ball,” Young said. “I think what we’re saying is Mike Evans understands spatial relationships in a unique Hall of Fame way, and so all of a sudden, where there doesn’t seem to be anybody open, Mike’s finding that place. “And so that confidence builds with Brock that I’m going to keep my eye [out for] wherever Mike is , and that allows Kyle Shanahan to lean into play-calling. You can call a play knowing that, yeah, if it breaks down, Mike’s in a space that’s going to be really cool, and we’ll figure that out.”

title: How to win, how to lose: Tampa Bay Buccaneers versus Pittsburgh Steelers week 6 game preview
summary: Week 6 is set to be rolling into living rooms all throughout the nation and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no longer winless. Todd Bowles and his pewter pirates managed to pull out a sensationally shocking upset of the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Behind the mighty galloping of Bucky Irving and the poise […]
full_text: Aug 16, 2025; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving (7) catches a touchdown pass in front of Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson (41) during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Week 6 is set to be rolling into living rooms all throughout the nation and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no longer winless. Todd Bowles and his pewter pirates managed to pull out a sensationally shocking upset of the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Behind the mighty galloping of Bucky Irving and the poise of UDFA Jalen Daniels, Tampa’s marauders took over AT&T Stadium. This Sunday (for the third week in a row), it’ll be another classic blueblood NFL franchise on the schedule for the Buccaneers— The Pittsburgh Steelers. “The offense can’t score if they don’t have the ball.” Johan Cruyff How can the Buccaneers win? The Bucs need to make sure they stay on schedule and stick to their gameplan. There are NFL teams that have the benefit of being able to get into different types of games and win in a variety of ways— The Buccaneers are not that team. If a win is in the cards, they need to make sure they are playing the hand that best suits them. Last week, in Dallas, Tampa did a phenomenal job of staying in the realm of football that they themselves are comfortable playing. The Buccaneers kept the ball on the ground, dominated time of possession— Starting with a 10-minute opening drive, and kept Dallas off-kilter. That dictation was not only an advantage for Tampa Bay, it’s the reason they won. That in turn made the Cowboys play the game the Buccaneers needed to play, not the one Dallas wanted to play. It would be easy to say, ‘If Bucky Irving rushes for nearly 200 yards, the Buccaneers have a good chance of winning’ , but it’s more than the yards on the stat sheet. Irving’s performance was eye-popping, but it was the offense’s ability to stay on the field that won Tampa Bay the game. The Buccaneers finished the game with just shy of 40 minutes time of possession, while Dallas’ heralded offense held the ball for just 20. That discrepancy is catastrophic for any team to be on the wrong side of— Personified through the consistent cutaways by Amazon’s broadcast as they kept showing defeated, disengaged, and dispirited Dallas Cowboys on the sideline. Consecutive weeks with 40 minutes of possession may not be on the docket, however, will the Buccaneers’ offense be able to keep themselves steady, avoid turnovers, and push Pittsburgh to play the type of game Tampa wants to play? “The question isn’t who is going to let me; it’s who is going to stop me.” Ayn Rand How can the Buccaneers lose? The Steelers have had some inconsistent offense this year, but they’ve had 24-plus points in each of the last three weeks (30, 24, 34). Of course, they can’t score if they don’t play (See the above portion of this article). The Buccaneers’ second best option for keeping Pittsburgh’s points down, besides pilfering clock, is turnovers. Tampa’s turnover differential on the season is not glamourous (-2). Maybe even more absurd, that hideous -2 sits boldly after the Bucs just had a +3 in their last contest. Aside from points themselves, nothing has ever been, or will ever be, a more clear determinant of wins and losses than turnovers. Teams that take the ball away win a lot more than teams that lose the ball. Having the ball means having more chances to score, more chances to score means more better odds you will score; ergo, turnovers are good. More importantly, for a struggling, very one-dimensional team like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, turnovers level the playing field. The scenario is two-fold. Not only does it fall on your defense to force them, but your offense must avoid turnovers like a coach on the hot seat must avoid losing. Last week, Tampa hit the trifecta— Their defense (and special teams) took the ball away from Dallas three times. Jalen Daniels and the Bucs’ offense did not turn the ball over at all and their coach on the heat seat avoided a loss. This week, it’s not Dak Prescott it’s Aaron Rodgers. Aaron Rodgers is a historically anti-turnover prone quarterback. The former Packers’ legend, Jets’ bust, and current Steelers’ stopgap, has quite literally the greatest touchdown to interception ratio in NFL history— As in, number one. Rodgers is not the type of quarterback that you want to face if the gameplan is get the ball— however , against all odds, Tampa Bay’s ever assailed head coach Todd Bowles has actually had a healthy level of success against Rodgers during his Bucs’ tenure. The two haven’t matched up since Rodgers left Green Bay, but the duels have actually largely favored Bowles. In three games versus Todd Bowles’ Tampa Bay defense, Rodgers has a losing record and has looked extremely ordinary. The four-time NFL MVP has wracked up just five touchdowns and he’s also tossed four interceptions. The backdrop is laid out much differently for the 2026 edition, Rodgers has a new team, a new (his old) coach, is playing at a completely different level (which may actually further favor Bowles), and Bowles does not have nearly the same defensive firepower he once did. Sunday, will likely be the last time the two battle— A final chapter in the story. The storylines for Sunday’s Bowles-Rodgers epilogue, can Todd Bowles get him again? Rodgers has yet to play a clean game against Bowles’ Bucs. Will the Buccaneers’ offense be able to stay mistake free for a second straight week? Turnovers, like they had against Rodgers’ former team two weeks ago, will almost assuredly sink them into a self-dug 1-5 hole.

full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 27: Shelby Harris #93 of the New York Giants tackles Tony Pollard #20 of the Tennessee Titans during their game at MetLife Stadium on September 27, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans have the worst offense in the NFL. A big reason why is the lack of support they receive from the rushing attack. At 0-5, the Titans currently possess the 27th ranked rushing offense in the NFL. Both Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are on expiring contracts. It’s difficult to envision GM Mike Borgonzi re-signing either of them after the lackluster season they are having. If the Titans want to continue supporting Cam Ward, they should consider bringing in a veteran RB to aid the offense. Let’s look ahead to some potential free-agent running backs the Titans can consider signing in 2027. Brian Robinson Jr., Atlanta Falcons Atlanta Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr. has rushed for 210 yards and four touchdowns this season despite backing up Bijan Robinson. He’ll almost certainly be looking for an opportunity to be a feature back next offseason. Robinson probably isn’t a true bellcow, but he’s better than any ball-carrier the Titans have right now. Zach Charbonnet, Seattle Seahawks Zach Charbonnet is about to return for the Seattle Seahawks from a torn ACL injury he suffered during the playoffs last year. Everyone around the league will be monitoring his form once he’s back. The Seahawks don’t believe in signing RBs to second contracts. They made the grave mistake of letting Kenneth Walker III leave, and just drafted Jadarian Price with a first-round pick. Charbonnet will almost certainly hit the open market. Chase Brown, Cincinnati Bengals Chase Brown is probably the best running back currently playing on an expiring contract. Can the Cincinnati Bengals afford to re-sign him after designating so much money on offense to Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins? Probably not. Adding Brown would provide the Titans offense with a true dual-threat back, even if he’s currently struggling in 2026.

title: Washington Commanders vs. Niners on MNF Week 6: Inside the Matchup
summary: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - DECEMBER 31: Terry McLaurin #17 of the Washington Commanders runs with the ball against the San Francisco 49ers during the first half of the game at FedExField on December 31, 2023 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026. From John Portis: The Washington Commanders enter Week 6 coming off one of the worst clock management gaffes in team history. After tying the Giants this past Sunday, the 1-3-1 Commanders will be looking to get their second win of the season as the team takes on the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Back in July , Bill-in-Bangkok predicted a hot start to the season for the Niners but seems to have underestimated their win total, as San Francisco narrowly defeated the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 last week to remain undefeated. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was expected to have one of the best offenses in football, but key injuries to several players, including wide receivers Rickey Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson, Christian Kirk and rookie De’Zhaun Stribling, have limited the team’s potential. News got worse for the Niners last week, as Deebo Samuel was ruled out with a hamstring injury and is expected to miss an extended period of time. Free-agent addition Mike Evans, who is fighting through a rib injury and now Achilles soreness, is playing at a high level and leads the team with 24 receptions for 326 receiving yards and three touchdowns. Quarterback Brock Purdy has made up the difference for the depleted wide receiver corps by playing at an MVP level, and his 85.5 QBR through the first five weeks leads the league. While Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle are starting to slow down, they are still very talented, and the Niners rank 3rd in team offense . Shanahan’s offense was always expected to be good, but San Francisco’s defense has been the real surprise of the 2026 season. After losing Robert Saleh to the Titans, the 49ers turned to Raheem Morris to coordinate their defense. So far, Morris looks to be an upgrade for them and has improved the team’s performance in multiple defensive categories. The 49ers offense was expected to be one of the best in the NFL. But through 5 games the defense ranks 3rd in EPA per play; 4th in scoring; 5th in yards allowed per play; 6th in net yards per pass attempt; 7th in rushing yards allowed per play; and 8th in opponent passer rating. — Matt Maiocco (@MaioccoNBCS) October 13, 2026 The improvement is even more impressive given the team has been without edge rusher Nick Bosa, a player Shanahan indicated has a chance to return this week , although Dre Greenlaw’s suspension was upheld and the linebacker will miss Monday night’s game. San Francisco has made explosive plays on offense while limiting them on defense, and the 49ers are playing well on both sides of the ball, which is why the team remains undefeated headed into Week 6. Explosive Play Rates through Week 5 BUF’s offense and SF’s defense in a league of their own. pic.twitter.com/320dhHAQSU — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) October 13, 2026 The challenge may seem insurmountable for Washington, but one of the positives from last week is that Jayden Daniels appears to have no limitations following his second left-elbow dislocation. The Commanders’ franchise quarterback was spectacular last Sunday and recorded 199 passing yards with a 68% completion rate, along with 103 rushing yards and 2 TDs on 8 rushes. Running back Bill Croskey-Merritt also demonstrated his explosive potential behind an improved offensive line with a 33-yard touchdown run and another 22-yard rush to set up one of Jayden Daniels’ touchdowns. Bill is dealing with a groin injury but could still sit up Monday night. Week 5 Explosive Plays Shows how many runs of 10+ yards and passes of 20+ yards each offense produced. Buffalo leads the league with 13 this week. pic.twitter.com/vhuLfjEJ3o — Gridiron Stats and Info (@GridironInfo_) October 13, 2026 Washington’s run defense continues to be ranked in the top 10 , and the possible return of Trey Amos and Nick Cross could bolster a secondary that has struggled this season . Both players practiced in full yesterday. Washington’s front seven will need to do a better job of generating pressure against an offensive line that allowed zero sacks through the first four weeks of the season, although Seattle’s defense was able to get home last Sunday, generating 3 sacks and 3 turnovers while limiting the 49ers offense to 269 yards, 14 first downs, and an average of 4.8 yards per play. The most important component for head coach Dan Quinn and his players will be the belief they can win in Santa Clara on Monday night. Amik Robertson’s early response this week would indicate that they have the needed belief. Chin up.. Chest Out. New Week, New Opportunity. — Amik Robertson (@_YoungTruth7) October 13, 2026 B etting Lines Oddsmakers have established the home team as the solid favorite for this matchup. Point Spread : 49ers -7.5 Game Total (Over/Under) : 50.5 points Bill-in-Bangkok’s original preview published July 5th: Date: October 19, 2026, 8:15 p.m. ET (Monday Night Football) Location: Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California The 49ers are off to Australia to open their season by playing Thursday Night Football in Victoria at the historic Melbourne Cricket Ground, where I once watched Day 5 of a test match between South Africa and the Aussies (which Australia won handily). San Fran then plays 3 home games in a row (presumably as payback for the Australia travel) before a short road trip to Seattle. They return to Levi’s Stadium for the MNF game against Washington — their 4th home game in 5 weeks! The Niners should have at least a couple of wins on the board as they play the Cardinals and Dolphins in two of those home games (who were ranked 29th & 32nd, respectively, in ESPN’s latest Football Power Index ). They may not be above .500, however, since their 3 other games are NFC & AFC West contests against the Rams, Seahawks and Broncos. We know that Kyle Shanahan always feels a little extra motivation against Washington, where he felt he and his dad got the metaphorical bum’s rush out the door at the end of the 2013 season, the senior Shanahan’s final NFL coaching job after a probable Hall of Fame NFL coaching career. Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch are two of the most petty individuals in the NFL. Washington gave San Fran the best LT and a future HOFer for a hot pocket and an extra large dill pickle because that’s where HE wanted to be traded to. Kyle still being petty after all these years… — Mark Tyler (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) June 25, 2026 The All-Time Series Numbers Dating back to 1952, San Francisco and Washington have played each other 36 times, including 4 playoff games. The Niners have had the best of both regular season and postseason, winning 3 of the 4 playoff games, and holding onto a commanding 23-12-1 lead overall. Washington’s sole playoff win over the 49ers came in the NFC Championship game after the 1983 season, on the way to the Redskins’ first Super Bowl (but 3rd NFL) championship. Things have been a little less one-sided since 2017, with Washington winning 2 out of 5 regular season games. You may remember the not-so-classic mud bowl played in Landover during monsoon rain in 2019 when the 49ers won 9-0. The last time Washington beat the 49ers, they were branded as the “Football Team” in the 2020 COVID-affected season. This will be the first meeting between the two teams in the AP/DQ/JD5 era (though not the first of the Josh Harris ownership), so…

full_text: Commanders running back Bill Croskey-Merritt had his best game of this early season on Sunday, turning in 82 yards and a touchdown on just 11 carries. His high per carry average was boosted by an explosive touchdown, but Croskey-Merritt came out of Sunday’s 27-27 draw with the New York Giants a bit banged up. He did not participate in Thursday’s practice with a groin injury, per the Commanders. Head coach Dan Quinn didn’t address the issue during his press conference earlier in the day, so clarity on Croskey-Merritt might not come until Saturday or even beyond. Also, Austin Ekeler is dealing with a chest injury and was seen by on-site reporters wearing a non-contact jersey. He was formally limited in practice. The Commanders also practiced without receiver Stefon Diggs and safeties Percy Butler and Tyler Owens, who are all dealing with hamstring injuries. Those guys could return to work later in the week. Defensive lineman Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral) was also out on Thursday. Defensive lineman Charles Omenihu (groin) and quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee) remained out of practice but were seen by reporters working off to the side . Quinn said that safety Nick Cross (illness), cornerback Trey Amos (ankle) and running back Jeremy McNichols — the later two are on injured reserve — are expected to be full participants in practice this week.
